## pocketone serve

Starts the web server (default to 127.0.0.1:8090 if no domain is specified)

```
pocketone serve [domain(s)]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--automigrate` | bool | `true` | enable/disable auto migrations |
| `--autotls` | bool | – | HTTPS certificates through CertMagic instead of the built-in autocert (with serve &lt;domain&gt; or `--https`): other CAs, extra domains, wildcards through DNS-01 |
| `--autotlsCA` | string | – | certificate authority for `--autotls`: letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL |
| `--autotlsDNS` | string | – | DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges with `--autotls` (supported: cloudflare) |
| `--autotlsDNSTokenEnv` | string | `CF_API_TOKEN` | environment variable holding the DNS provider's API token for `--autotlsDNS` |
| `--autotlsDomains` | stringSlice | – | extra domains for `--autotls`, obtained at start (comma separated; wildcards like \*.example.com need `--autotlsDNS`) |
| `--autotlsEmail` | string | – | ACME account email for `--autotls` (expiry notices from the CA) |
| `--dev` | bool | `true` | enable dev mode, aka. printing logs and sql statements to the console |
| `--dir` | string | `<the binary's folder>/pb_data` | the PocketBase data directory |
| `--encryptionEnv` | string | – | the env variable whose value of 32 characters will be used as encryption key for the app settings (default none) |
| `--hooksDir` | string | – | the directory with the JS app hooks |
| `--hooksPool` | int | `15` | only with `--jsvm` goja: the JS runtimes kept ready for hooks |
| `--hooksWatch` | bool | `true` | auto restart the app on pb\_hooks file change; it has no effect on Windows |
| `--http` | string | – | TCP address to listen for the HTTP server (if domain args are specified - default to 0.0.0.0:80, otherwise - default to 127.0.0.1:8090) |
| `--https` | string | – | TCP address to listen for the HTTPS server (if domain args are specified - default to 0.0.0.0:443, otherwise - default to empty string, aka. no TLS) The incoming HTTP traffic also will be auto redirected to the HTTPS version |
| `--indexFallback` | bool | `true` | fallback the request to index.html on missing static path, e.g. when pretty urls are used with SPA |
| `--jsvm` | string | `quickjs` | the JS engine: quickjs (PocketOne's) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility) |
| `--migrationsDir` | string | – | the directory with the user defined migrations |
| `--origins` | stringSlice | `[*]` | CORS allowed domain origins list |
| `--pagesDir` | string | – | the directory with the PocketPages app (default pb\_pages next to pb\_data); served when it exists |
| `--pitr` | bool | `true` | point-in-time restore: replicate data.db into pb\_data/litestream/ while serving |
| `--pitrRetention` | duration | `72h0m0s` | how far back a point-in-time restore can go |
| `--publicDir` | string | `./pb_public` | the directory to serve static files |
| `--queryTimeout` | int | `30` | the default SELECT queries timeout in seconds |
| `--s3Redirect` | bool | `true` | answer file downloads with a short-lived signed redirect to the bucket when S3 file storage is on |
| `--s3RedirectTTL` | duration | `5m0s` | how long each signed file download URL stays valid |

From PocketBase.

## pocketone superuser

Manage superusers

From PocketBase.

Every `pocketone superuser` command takes these.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dev` | bool | `true` | enable dev mode, aka. printing logs and sql statements to the console |
| `--dir` | string | `<the binary's folder>/pb_data` | the PocketBase data directory |
| `--encryptionEnv` | string | – | the env variable whose value of 32 characters will be used as encryption key for the app settings (default none) |
| `--hooksDir` | string | – | the directory with the JS app hooks |
| `--hooksPool` | int | `15` | only with `--jsvm` goja: the JS runtimes kept ready for hooks |
| `--jsvm` | string | `quickjs` | the JS engine: quickjs (PocketOne's) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility) |
| `--migrationsDir` | string | – | the directory with the user defined migrations |
| `--queryTimeout` | int | `30` | the default SELECT queries timeout in seconds |

### pocketone superuser create

```
pocketone superuser create
```

From PocketBase.

### pocketone superuser delete

Deletes an existing superuser

```
pocketone superuser delete
```

From PocketBase.

```
pocketone superuser ips
```

From PocketBase.

```

```

From PocketBase.

```

```

From PocketBase.

## pocketone template

From [Templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates).

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dev` | bool | `true` | enable dev mode, aka. printing logs and sql statements to the console |
| `--dir` | string | `<the binary's folder>/pb_data` | the PocketBase data directory |
| `--encryptionEnv` | string | – | the env variable whose value of 32 characters will be used as encryption key for the app settings (default none) |
| `--hooksDir` | string | – | the directory with the JS app hooks |
| `--hooksPool` | int | `15` | only with `--jsvm` goja: the JS runtimes kept ready for hooks |
| `--jsvm` | string | `quickjs` | the JS engine: quickjs (PocketOne's) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility) |

| `--queryTimeout` | int | `30` | the default SELECT queries timeout in seconds |

### pocketone template eject

Copies a template set (every set without a name) into pb\_templates/&lt;set&gt;/ for you to edit

```
pocketone template eject [set]
```

Copies the set's built-in Go templates into pb\_templates/&lt;set&gt;/; the app renders your copy of each file from then on (delete a file to go back to the built-in one). Files you already have and haven't changed are left alone; files you changed are only overwritten after you confirm, or with --force.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--force` | bool | – | overwrite files you changed without asking |

From [Templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates).

### pocketone template list

Lists the template sets extensions offer, and what you've changed in pb\_templates

```
pocketone template list
```

From [Templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates).

### pocketone token create

```
pocketone token create
```

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--collection` | string | – | owner: auth collection (with `--record`) |
| `--name` | string | – | a name to recognize the token by |
| `--record` | string | – | owner: record id or email in `--collection` |
| `--scope` | stringSlice | – | limit the token to a scope (repeatable; none: the owner's full rights) |
| `--superuser` | string | – | owner: a superuser's email |
| `--ttl` | duration | `0s` | lifetime, e.g. 720h (default: never expires) |

From [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens).

## pocketone upgrade

Upgrades this executable to the latest release, keeping the old one as &lt;name&gt;-&lt;version&gt;

```
pocketone upgrade
```

Upgrades this executable to the latest release, keeping the old one as &lt;name&gt;-&lt;version&gt;.

The newest release is offered, prereleases included. Moving from a stable release to a prerelease asks first
(no means the newest stable release instead, if there's a newer one); from one prerelease to the next it doesn't.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--backup` | bool | `true` | Back up pb\_data after upgrading, if this folder has one |
| `-y`, `--yes` | bool | – | Move from a stable release to a prerelease without asking |

From [Upgrade](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/upgrade).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest

# REST reference

Every contract API a PocketOne app with its [standard extensions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard) answers, under `/api/_c/<contract>/`. PocketBase's own API (records, collections, auth, files, settings…) is unchanged; see the [PocketBase docs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketbase).

- **Auth:** an `Authorization` header with a superuser's auth token or an [API token](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens). Each operation needs its token scope; a superuser's own auth token passes every scope.
- **Discovery:** `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` says who you are and lists every contract the app offers ([remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1)).
- **Input:** a JSON body for `POST`, query parameters for `GET`. **Answers** are JSON; streams are server-sent events.
- **Same as the CLI and MCP:** every operation here is also a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, behind the same checks ([how](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote)).

## bulkmail/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1). Answered by [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) in the standard set.

| Endpoint | What it does | Token scope | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/count` | Says how many recipients an audience reaches, how many of them are suppressed, and a few sample addresses. | `bulkmail:read` | `audience` (json) |
| `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/start` | Queues a campaign's recipients and starts sending (Limit &gt; 0: at most that many new recipients). | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string), `limit` (int) |
| `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/pause` | Stops sending a campaign; Resume carries on. | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/resume` | Carries on sending a paused campaign. | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/cancel` | Stops a campaign for good; recipients not yet sent to are dropped. | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/preview` | Renders a campaign's message for one recipient (the first in its audience when Email is empty). | `bulkmail:read` | `campaign` (string), `email` (string) |
| `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/test` | Sends a campaign's message to one address, marked as a test. | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string), `to` (string) |

## cache.clear/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1). Answered by [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache) in the standard set.

| Endpoint | What it does | Token scope | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/_c/cache.clear/v1` | Empties one of the app's cache buckets, or every bucket it has. | `cache` | `bucket` (string) |

## deploy/v1

Its own API under `/api/_c/deploy/v1/`: see [deploy/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/deploy/v1). Answered by [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) in the standard set.

## mail.feedback/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1). Answered by [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) in the standard set.

| Endpoint | What it does | Token scope | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/ses` | Takes an Amazon SNS delivery carrying SES bounce and complaint notifications (and confirms the topic subscription). | public | raw body |
| `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/webhook` | Takes {"type": "bounce\|complaint\|unsubscribe", "email": ..., "campaign": ...} from any provider, with the shared secret in the X-Feedback-Secret header. | public | raw body |

## mail.suppression/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1). Answered by [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) in the standard set.

| Endpoint | What it does | Token scope | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/check` | Says whether an address is suppressed, and why. | `suppression:read` | `email` (string) |
| `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/suppress` | Adds an address (or changes its reason). | `suppression` | `email` (string), `reason` (string), `source` (string), `campaign` (string) |
| `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsuppress` | Removes an address, so it receives bulk mail again. | `suppression` | `email` (string) |
| `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe` | Is the page an unsubscribe link opens (?t=&lt;signed token&gt;). | public | `t` (string) |
| `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe` | Confirms the page's form, or a mail provider's one-click POST (List-Unsubscribe=One-Click). | public | raw body |

## oauth/v1

Its own API under `/api/_c/oauth/v1/`: see [oauth/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/oauth/v1). Answered by [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) in the standard set.

## remote/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1). Answered by [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) in the standard set.

| Endpoint | What it does | Token scope | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` | Says who the credential is, the app's name and URL, and the contracts it offers. | public |  |
| `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` | Reports whether the app is running, its versions, uptime and mode. | `remote:read` |  |
| `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` | Restarts the app; requests in flight finish first. | `remote` |  |
| `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs` | Streams the app's log: the last entries, then new ones as they're written. (stream) | `remote:read` | `n` (int) |

## restore/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1). Answered by [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) in the standard set.

| Endpoint | What it does | Token scope | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` | Says what the app's data can be restored to: a window of time (continuous history) or a list of moments (backups), and whether a restore is running. | `restore:read` |  |
| `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` | Puts the app's data back as it was at the given moment, from the latest point at or before it. | `restore` | `at` (time) |

## settings/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1). Answered by [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings) in the standard set.

| Endpoint | What it does | Token scope | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/settings/v1` | Names the extensions whose settings this app's admins can change. | `settings:read` |  |
| `GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get` | Returns one extension's settings. | `settings:read` | `extension` (string) |
| `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/save` | Replaces one extension's settings and applies them. | `settings` | `extension` (string), `values` (json) |
| `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/test` | Checks one extension's settings without saving them (a test write to a bucket, a test message). | `settings` | `extension` (string), `values` (json) |

## tokens/v1

Its own API under `/api/_c/tokens/v1/`: see [tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tokens/v1). Answered by [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) in the standard set.

## vacuum/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/vacuum/v1). Answered by [Vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum) in the standard set.

| Endpoint | What it does | Token scope | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/vacuum/v1` | Says who compacts the app's databases, whether and how often, and how the last run went. | `vacuum:read` |  |

# MCP reference

A PocketOne app serves MCP at `/mcp` ([MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp)): PocketBase's whole API as `pb_*` tools, the tools your `pb_hooks` add, and one tool per operation of every contract the app provides, listed here for the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard). Each contract tool calls the contract, so it passes the same token scope check and hooks as the REST API and the CLI ([how](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote)). Uploads and downloads have no tool.

## bulkmail/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1). Answered by [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) in the standard set.

| Tool | What it does | Reads only | Token scope | Arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bulkmail_count` | Says how many recipients an audience reaches, how many of them are suppressed, and a few sample addresses. |  | `bulkmail:read` | `audience` (json) |
| `bulkmail_start` | Queues a campaign's recipients and starts sending (Limit &gt; 0: at most that many new recipients). |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string), `limit` (int) |
| `bulkmail_pause` | Stops sending a campaign; Resume carries on. |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `bulkmail_resume` | Carries on sending a paused campaign. |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `bulkmail_cancel` | Stops a campaign for good; recipients not yet sent to are dropped. |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `bulkmail_preview` | Renders a campaign's message for one recipient (the first in its audience when Email is empty). |  | `bulkmail:read` | `campaign` (string), `email` (string) |
| `bulkmail_test` | Sends a campaign's message to one address, marked as a test. |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string), `to` (string) |

## cache.clear/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1). Answered by [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache) in the standard set.

| Tool | What it does | Reads only | Token scope | Arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cache_clear_clear` | Empties one of the app's cache buckets, or every bucket it has. |  | `cache` | `bucket` (string) |

## mail.suppression/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1). Answered by [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) in the standard set.

| Tool | What it does | Reads only | Token scope | Arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mail_suppression_check` | Says whether an address is suppressed, and why. | yes | `suppression:read` | `email` (string) |
| `mail_suppression_suppress` | Adds an address (or changes its reason). |  | `suppression` | `email` (string), `reason` (string), `source` (string), `campaign` (string) |
| `mail_suppression_unsuppress` | Removes an address, so it receives bulk mail again. |  | `suppression` | `email` (string) |

## remote/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1). Answered by [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) in the standard set.

| Tool | What it does | Reads only | Token scope | Arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `remote_whoami` | Says who the credential is, the app's name and URL, and the contracts it offers. | yes | public |  |
| `remote_status` | Reports whether the app is running, its versions, uptime and mode. | yes | `remote:read` |  |
| `remote_restart` | Restarts the app; requests in flight finish first. |  | `remote` |  |
| `remote_logs` | Streams the app's log: the last entries, then new ones as they're written. | yes | `remote:read` | `n` (int) |

## restore/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1). Answered by [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) in the standard set.

| Tool | What it does | Reads only | Token scope | Arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `restore_points` | Says what the app's data can be restored to: a window of time (continuous history) or a list of moments (backups), and whether a restore is running. | yes | `restore:read` |  |
| `restore_restore_to` | Puts the app's data back as it was at the given moment, from the latest point at or before it. |  | `restore` | `at` (time) |

## settings/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1). Answered by [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings) in the standard set.

| Tool | What it does | Reads only | Token scope | Arguments |

| `settings_save` | Replaces one extension's settings and applies them. |  | `settings` | `extension` (string), `values` (json) |

# pocketone.yaml reference

Every section the `pocketone` binary understands, from `pocketone config --json`. Each extension owns its own section. `pocketone config check` checks a file. How the file works (where it's found, `.env` secrets) is on the [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config) page.

#### `app:`

The single app, for every command that opens it: data dir, dev mode, encryption, JS engine, hooks, migrations, and the .env names it may read (env_allow). Not used on a multisite host.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | string |  | The data folder (pb_data). Default: pb_data next to the executable. The --dir flag wins. |
| `dev` | bool |  | Dev mode: logs and SQL statements printed to the console. The --dev flag wins. |
| `encryption_env` | string |  | Name of the environment variable holding a 32-character key that encrypts the app settings. The --encryptionEnv flag wins. |
| `query_timeout` | duration |  | Default timeout for SELECT queries, such as 30s. The --queryTimeout flag wins. |
| `hooks_dir` | string |  | The JS hooks folder. Default: pb_hooks next to pb_data. The --hooksDir flag wins. |
| `jsvm` | string |  | The JS engine for pb_hooks and pb_migrations: quickjs (PocketOne's, the default) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility: pages, $mcp, $tokens and JS contracts are off). The --jsvm flag wins. |
| `hooks_pool` | int |  | Only with jsvm: goja: how many JS runtimes are kept ready for hooks. Default 15. The --hooksPool flag wins. |
| `migrations_dir` | string |  | The migrations folder. Default: pb_migrations next to pb_data. The --migrationsDir flag wins. |
| `env_allow` | list of string |  | Names from the .env the app and its JS hooks may read. Default none. |
| `js_limits.memory` | int |  | The app's JS memory: the JS heap plus the Go objects JS holds, such as 128MiB. Default 64MiB. |
| `js_limits.task_time` | duration |  | JS time one task (a request, a hook, a cron job) may use, Go calls and waits not counted, such as 10s. Default 5s. |
| `js_limits.task_wall` | duration |  | Wall time one task may take, Go calls included, such as 60s. Default 30s. |

#### `autotls:`

Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls* flags win.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | bool |  | Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. |
| `email` | string |  | ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. |
| `ca` | string |  | letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. |
| `storage` | string |  | Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. |
| `domains` | list of string |  | Extra domains to get at start; wildcards (*.example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. |
| `dns.provider` | string |  | DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. |
| `dns.api_token` | string |  | The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. |
| `dns.api_token_env` | string |  | Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv. |

Owned by [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls).

#### `cache:`

The cache (cache/v1): one store for every app in the process (memory, disk tier), and caps per bucket.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | Turns the cache off when false; extensions then run uncached. |
| `eviction` | string |  | Which values leave memory (or disk) first when the store reaches its ceiling: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. |
| `max_memory` | int |  | Memory for every bucket together, such as 512MiB. Default 128MiB. |
| `disk_path` | string |  | Turns on a disk tier there (in a p1cache folder). Relative: under pb_data on a single app, the working directory on a multisite host. |
| `max_disk` | int |  | Size of the disk tier for every bucket together, such as 10GiB. Default 1GiB. |
| `defaults.eviction` | string |  | Which of the bucket's entries go first when it's full: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. |
| `defaults.max_items` | int |  | Most entries the bucket holds. |
| `defaults.max_memory` | int |  | Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds in memory, such as 32MiB (the default). |
| `defaults.max_disk` | int |  | Most bytes of disk files the bucket's keys point at, each counted in full, such as 256MiB (the default). |
| `defaults.ttl` | int |  | How long an entry lives unless the code says otherwise, such as 10m. |
| `buckets` | map of object |  | Caps per bucket name, over what its code asks for. |

Owned by [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache).

#### `docker:`

Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `socket` | string |  | The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. |
| `image` | string |  | Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. |
| `binaries` | string |  | Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. |
| `versions` | list of string |  | The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). |
| `root` | string |  | Folder with one folder per instance (<root>/<id>). Required. |
| `home` | string |  | The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. |
| `default_version` | string |  | Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0.*. Empty: such instances fail. |
| `min_upstream` | string |  | Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. |
| `idle_ttl` | duration |  | Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. |
| `max_concurrent_starts` | int |  | Containers starting at once. Default 4. |
| `start_timeout` | duration |  | How long a container gets to answer its health check. Default 60s. |
| `nano_cpus` | int |  | CPU limit per container in billionths of a CPU (1000000000 = one CPU). 0: no limit. |
| `pids_limit` | int |  | Process limit per container. 0: Docker's default. |
| `nofile` | list of int |  | Open-file limit per container: [soft, hard]. Empty: Docker's default. |
| `cap_drop` | list of string |  | Linux capabilities to drop, such as [ALL]. |
| `no_new_privileges` | bool |  | Set no-new-privileges on every container. |
| `network` | string |  | Docker network for the containers. Default the bridge. |
| `adopt_image` | string |  | Also adopt running unlabeled containers of this image named after an instance id (taking over from another manager). |

Owned by [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker).

#### `edges:`

The fleet: this edge's id and a fixed list of the other edges (id, internal_url, region).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `self` | string |  | This edge's id, such as lax-1. |
| `list` | list of object |  | The other edges: id, internal_url (where this edge reaches it) and optional region. |

Owned by [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge).

#### `firewall:`

Peers allowed to connect, trusted proxies and client-IP headers, trusted clients, the rate-limit header prefix. Turns the firewall on.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_cidrs` | list of string |  | Peers (IPs or CIDRs) allowed to connect; others get 403. Empty: everyone. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of string |  | Peers whose client-IP headers are believed. |
| `client_ip_headers` | list of string |  | Headers read, in order, for the client IP from a trusted proxy. Default CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP. |
| `trusted_clients` | list of string |  | Client IPs or CIDRs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance. |
| `trusted_client_headers` | list of string |  | Headers a trusted client uses to name its end user's IP, so each user gets their own limits. Default X-Client-IP. |
| `rate_limit_header_prefix` | string |  | Prefix of the rate-limit response headers. Default X-RateLimit. |

Owned by [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall).

#### `instances:`

Where a multi-instance host's instances come from (a YAML file), and dev mode (serve unknown hostnames).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | `instances.yaml` | The instances file (id, hosts and settings for each instance), reloaded when it changes. |
| `dev` | bool |  | Also serve unknown hostnames: each becomes an instance named after it, in dev mode, with its folder made on first use. |

Owned by [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite).

#### `lifecycle:`

Instance data on this host: how often disk use is measured and last-request times are reported.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `measure_every` | duration | `24h0m0s` | How old an instance's disk measurement may get before it is measured again. Default 24h. |
| `report_every` | duration | `1h0m0s` | How often changed last-request times are reported to the sink. Default 1h. |
| `concurrency` | int | `2` | How many instances are measured at once. Default 2. |

Owned by [Stats](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/stats).

#### `mothership:`

A community mothership to mirror instances and edges from: url, login, this edge's id, internal URL, region, apex.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string |  | The mothership's URL. Required. |
| `email` | string |  | Superuser email this edge logs in with; use a $VAR from the .env. |
| `password` | string |  | Superuser password; use a $VAR from the .env. |
| `self` | string |  | This edge's edge_id, such as lax-1. Default: the edges section's self. Required. |
| `internal_url` | string |  | Where other edges reach this one. Set: the edge registers itself when the mothership has no record for it. |
| `region` | string |  | Region recorded when the edge registers itself. |
| `apex` | string |  | Makes <name>.<apex> a hostname of every instance. Empty: hosts only. |
| `heartbeat` | duration |  | How often this edge marks itself online. Default 15s; negative: never. |
| `resync` | duration |  | How often everything is reloaded, in case a change was missed. Default 10m. |

Owned by [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership).

#### `multisite:`

Serve many instances (a multisite host) instead of a single app. The runtimes are the providers of runtime/v1.

Owned by [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite).

#### `pitr:`

Point-in-time restore: on by default, retention, snapshot interval. The --pitr and --pitrRetention flags win.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false. The --pitr flag wins. |
| `retention` | duration |  | How far back a restore can go. Default 72h. The --pitrRetention flag wins. |
| `snapshot_interval` | duration |  | How often a full copy is taken. Default 24h. Shorter: faster restores, more storage. |

Owned by [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr).

#### `pocker:`

Runtime provider pocker: instances run in-process (root folder, hooks pool, egress allow list, instance limit defaults).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | string | `./pb_root` | The folder holding one folder per instance: <root>/<id>. |
| `hooks_pool_size` | int | `2` | Ignored: each instance has one JS VM (ext/jsvm). Kept so existing configs load. |
| `max_js_execution` | duration | `30s` | Longest any single JS call (hook, route, cron job, migration) may run. |
| `max_js_allocation` | int | `67108864` | Largest result a JS built-in may allocate in one step, such as 64MiB. |
| `max_call_stack_size` | int | `2000` | Deepest JS recursion allowed. |
| `max_sleep` | duration | `10s` | Longest a JS sleep() call may wait. |
| `max_query_duration` | duration | `30s` | Longest an SQL statement without its own deadline may run. |
| `http_send_max_timeout` | duration | `1m0s` | Longest timeout a JS $http.send call may use. |
| `http_send_max_body` | int | `10485760` | Largest response body a JS $http.send call may read, such as 10MiB. |
| `max_concurrent_js` | int | `16` | JS calls an instance runs at once; more wait up to max_js_execution, then fail. |
| `egress_allow` | list of string |  | Private networks (CIDRs) instances may still connect to. Default none: public addresses only. |

Owned by [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker).

#### `providers:`

Which extension provides a contract when several do.

Owned by [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

#### `rate_limits:`

Default rate limits for every instance (per instance: extensions.firewall.rate_limits). Turns the firewall on.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour from one client IP to one instance. Default 1000. |
| `instance_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour to one instance from everyone. Default 10000. |
| `ip_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one client IP may have open on one instance at once. Default 15. |
| `instance_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one instance may have open at once. Default 250. |
| `file_weight` | number |  | What a /api/files request costs, as a share of a request. Default 0.1. |
| `trusted.ip_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour from one trusted client IP to one instance. |
| `trusted.instance_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour to one instance. |
| `trusted.ip_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one trusted client IP may have open on one instance at once. |
| `trusted.instance_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one instance may have open at once. |
| `off` | bool |  | No rate limiting. The default in dev mode unless rate_limits is set. |

Owned by [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall).

#### `s3redirect:`

Signed S3 redirects for file downloads: enabled, URL lifetime. The --s3Redirect and --s3RedirectTTL flags win.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false (it only acts when S3 file storage is on). Flag: --s3Redirect. |
| `ttl` | duration |  | How long each signed URL stays valid. Default 5m, max 7 days. Flag: --s3RedirectTTL. |

Owned by [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect).

#### `server:`

The serve command: http, https and CORS origins, and for a single app its static files, pages, hooks watching and automigrate.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http` | string |  | Plain HTTP address, such as 127.0.0.1:8090. Single app: the --http default (the flag wins). Many instances: redirects to https when https is set. |
| `https` | string |  | HTTPS address. Single app: the --https default (the flag wins). Many instances: the main address. |
| `origins` | list of string |  | Allowed CORS origins. Single app: the --origins default (the flag wins). |
| `plain` | list of string |  | Many instances only: extra plain HTTP addresses with no redirect. |
| `tls.cert` | string |  | Many instances only: the certificate file, reloaded when it changes. |
| `tls.key` | string |  | Many instances only: the private key file, reloaded when it changes. |
| `shutdown_timeout` | duration |  | Many instances only: how long in-flight requests get to finish at stop. |
| `public_dir` | string |  | Single app only: the static files folder. Default: pb_public next to the executable. The --publicDir flag wins. |
| `index_fallback` | bool |  | Single app only: serve index.html for a missing static path, for single-page apps. On unless false. The --indexFallback flag wins. |
| `pages_dir` | string |  | Single app only: the PocketPages folder, served when it exists. Default: pb_pages next to pb_data. The --pagesDir flag wins. |
| `hooks_watch` | bool |  | Single app only: restart the app when a pb_hooks file changes. On unless false. The --hooksWatch flag wins. |
| `automigrate` | bool |  | Single app only: write a migration file when you change collections in the dashboard. On unless false. The --automigrate flag wins. |

#### `vacuum:`

Defaults for compacting the app's SQLite databases (VACUUM): on or off, and how often. The app's admins change them in Settings.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | Compact the databases on a schedule, until the app's admins change it in Settings. |
| `every` | string | `168h` | How often, e.g. 24h or 168h (weekly). |

Owned by [Vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum).

# Contracts

New to the idea? Read [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/how-pocketone-fits-together) first. This page is the list of every
contract and how to write one.

Every API a PocketOne extension offers is a contract: a versioned Go interface, and the HTTP API, hooks and MCP tools
that come with it, at `/api/_c/<id>/`. Extensions have no routes of their own. An extension says what it
**implements**, **requires** and **works with** in terms of these contracts, never another extension's name, so any
extension that implements a contract can stand in for another. PocketOne answers "who provides this contract on this
app?" at startup and prints the answer.

Every contract lives here, standard or community; extensions live in `ext/<name>`. Each contract is a package named
for its id and major version: `deploy/v1` is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/deploy/v1`,
`mail.fallback/v1` is `.../mail/fallback/v1`. A change to what a contract promises is a new major version (`v2`) next
to the old one.

The table is generated from each contract's README and every extension's `Contracts()`: run
`go run ./.github/extensions contracts` (CI fails when it's stale).

<!-- contracts:catalogue (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts`; edit each contract's README front matter) -->

| Contract | What it promises | Provided by | Required by | Works with | Owners |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`bulkmail/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1) | Run bulk mail campaigns: count an audience; start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign. | bulkmail |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`cache.clear/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1) | Emptying an app's cache buckets, one or all, from the dashboard, the CLI or an agent. | cache (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`cache/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache/v1) | Named buckets of bytes an app keeps for a while, with limits and eviction; memory, disk or a shared cache behind it. | cache (default) |  | pages | @benallfree |
| [`cli.commands/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cli.commands/v1) | The pocketone command tree: every contract operation as a remote command by default; extensions replace or add commands. |  |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`deploy/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/deploy/v1) | A project's code files on an app: check, upload, commit, list, read, write, delete, tree. | deploy (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`gate/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/gate/v1) | What admits requests on a multisite host: peer checks, client IPs and rate limits, in order. | firewall |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`http.wrap/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/http.wrap/v1) | Middleware around everything a multisite host serves, nested in order. | servertiming |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`instance.source/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.source/v1) | The instance record a multisite host serves, and where the records come from. | mothership | pocker |  | @benallfree |
| [`mail.fallback/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.fallback/v1) | Where an app's mail goes when SMTP is off: a chain of providers that send it or pass it on. | mailrelay, mailtrap |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`mail.feedback/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1) | Mail providers' reports (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) received at one place and raised as events any extension can act on. | bulkmail (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`mail.suppression/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1) | Addresses an app must not send bulk mail to, and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries. | bulkmail (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`mcp/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mcp/v1) | The app's MCP endpoint at /mcp, with every provided contract's operations as tools. | mcp (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`oauth/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/oauth/v1) | The app's OAuth 2.1 authorization server, so the CLI and MCP clients can sign in. | tokens |  | mcp | @benallfree |
| [`remote/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1) | Remote control of an app: whoami, status, restart, logs. The base every client starts from. | docker, remotes (default) | deploy |  | @benallfree |
| [`restore/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1) | Put an app's data back as it was at a moment: from continuous history, or the latest backup before it. | backups (default), pitr |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`runtime/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1) | What runs a multisite host's instances (in-process, in containers), in preference order. | docker, pocker |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`settings/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1) | The settings an app's admins change for its extensions, one API for all of them. | settings (default) |  | bulkmail, mailrelay, pitr, vacuum | @benallfree |
| [`templates/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/templates/v1) | An extension's own pages as Go templates a project can eject and edit. | templates |  | tokens | @benallfree |
| [`tls/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tls/v1) | The TLS of a multisite host's listener: automatic certificates instead of certificate files. | autotls |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`tokens/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tokens/v1) | An app's API tokens: check one, register scopes, read a request's token, limit in-process requests; the token API. | tokens |  | deploy, mcp, remotes | @benallfree |
| [`vacuum/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/vacuum/v1) | Compacting an app's databases so freed space goes back to the disk, and when it last happened. | vacuum |  |  | @benallfree |

<!-- /contracts:catalogue -->

[`internal/example/v1`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/internal/example/v1/example.go) is a test-only wire contract that exercises the generated code.

## Three kinds

- **Service:** a Go interface, looked up in the same process (`fallbackv1.Contract.Of(app)`).
- **Wire:** a service with an HTTP API under `/api/_c/<id>/`, generated from its interface: each method is an
  operation with its own HTTP method, path and token scope (`//op: POST restart scope=remote`); inputs and results are
  JSON, uploads (`extkit.RawIn`), downloads (`extkit.RawOut`) or streams (`extkit.Stream`, sent as server-sent
  events). It gets action hooks (`remotev1.OnRestart`, `onRemoteRestart` in `pb_hooks`), an MCP tool per JSON
  operation and a client. Every caller (HTTP, MCP, Go) passes the same scope check and hooks.
- **Routed:** a contract whose provider is an `http.Handler` serving everything under `/api/_c/<id>/` as it is, for an
  API a protocol shapes (OAuth) or an existing API moved under a contract (deploy/v1).

A multisite host can provide a wire or routed contract for its instances, so it works for instances that run stock
PocketBase.

A contract can bring its own dashboard screen (`Contract.UI(name, fsys)`): it shows on every app that provides the
contract, whichever extension does, and calls only the contract's API. restore/v1's "Restore to a moment" works this
way.

An extension that calls a contract for its own work (bulk mail checking whoever keeps the suppression list) passes
`extkit.Internal` as the auth, and can ask who provides it with `Contract.Provider(app)`.

## Add a contract

A contract is a folder `ext/contracts/<id path>/vN/` (`mail.fallback/v1` → `mail/fallback/v1/`) with:

- the Go package: the interface, its `//contract:` directives and `zz_contract.go`;
- a `README.md`, its page on pocketone.dev, with front matter and four sections in this order:

  ```markdown
  ---
  owners: ["@your-github-handle"]
  summary: "One line: what the contract promises."
  ---

  # mail.fallback/v1

  ## Use        how to call it: HTTP, Go, pb_hooks, MCP, CLI
  ## Provide    how to implement it
  ## Extensions (generated: who provides, requires and works with it)
  ## License    MIT
  ```

Whoever first creates a contract owns it; an extension author who adds one owns both the contract and the extension
that provides it. Ids are unique across PocketOne. Pick a name for what the contract does (`restore/v1`), not for the
extension that first provides it.

## Write the interface

A contract is an interface with `//contract:` directives; [`contractgen`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/cmd/contractgen/main.go) writes the rest
(`zz_contract.go`) with `go generate ./...`. A test fails when a generated file is stale.

```go
//go:generate go run github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/cmd/contractgen

// Deployer sends a project's code to an app.
//
//contract:id deploy/v1
//contract:kind wire
//contract:scope deploy
//contract:host
//contract:js hooks
type Deployer interface {
	// Upload writes changed files to the app.
	Upload(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in UploadInput) (UploadResult, error)
}
```

Methods take `ctx`, then (wire) `extkit.Auth`, then at most one input; they return `error` or one value and `error`.
The doc comment of a wire method is its MCP tool's description. Contracts are reviewed like PocketOne's core: a
contract is a promise every implementation keeps.

## Use one

```go
// provide (in Register)
deployv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myDeployer{})

// consume (after registration: in hooks, at serve time)
d := deployv1.Contract.Must(app)

// declare it, so PocketOne can order and switch extensions
func (e *Extension) Contracts() extkit.Contracts {
	return extkit.Contracts{Implements: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1"), Defaults: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1")}
}
```

Choose between providers in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  mail.fallback/v1: mailrelay
```

MIT

# Extensions

Each extension is a Go module in [`ext/`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext) with its own README; the pages here are those READMEs. Want to add one? Read [Writing an extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension).

## Standard extensions

These ship with `pocketone` and add no work to an app that doesn't use them.

| Extension | What it does |
|---|---|
| [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls) | Certificates on demand and wildcards through ACME. |
| [Backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups) | Restore an app to a moment from its own backups: the latest one before it. On by default. |
| [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | Campaigns to your app's own users, with audiences from a collection, a view or SQL. |
| [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache) | Cache buckets for every app in the process from one shared store: bytes or Go values, a budget per bucket, LRU/MRU/FIFO/LIFO eviction, TTLs, a cold disk tier that keeps identical values once. |
| [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config) | The pocketone.yaml config file, with secrets in a .env beside it. |
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | pocketone deploy, dev, pull and logs, and the deploy API. |
| [JSVM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm) | PocketOne's JS engine: one QuickJS VM per app, real globals, async handlers, hard limits. |
| [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | An MCP endpoint at /mcp so agents can manage your app and call its tools. |
| [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/extension) | Server-rendered pages from a pb_pages folder (formerly PocketPages). |
| [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | Point-in-time restore of your database with Litestream. On by default. |
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | Named remotes and saved logins for the pocketone command. |
| [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect) | File downloads as short-lived signed S3 redirects. |
| [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings) | One API for the settings an app's admins change for its extensions. On by default. |
| [Templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates) | Theme an extension's own pages (the OAuth sign-in screens): eject its templates to pb_templates and edit them. |
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | Long-lived API tokens with scopes. |
| [Upgrade](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/upgrade) | pocketone upgrade to the latest release, keeping the old executable. |
| [Vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum) | Compact your app's SQLite databases on a schedule, so space freed by deleted records goes back to the disk. |

## Run many instances

# bulkmail/v1

Campaigns to many recipients, sent at a pace the app's mail account can take. Campaigns are records in the
provider's collection, created and edited with PocketBase's records API; this contract runs them. The list of
addresses never to mail is [mail.suppression/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1); providers' bounce and
complaint reports are [mail.feedback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1).

A wire contract ([bulkmail.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/bulkmail/v1/bulkmail.go)).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP (`POST`) | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Count | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/count` | `{"audience": {...}}` | `bulkmail:read` |
| Start | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/start` | `{"campaign": "<id>", "limit": 0}` | `bulkmail` |
| Pause, Resume, Cancel | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/pause` (`resume`, `cancel`) | `{"campaign": "<id>"}` | `bulkmail` |
| Preview | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/preview` | `{"campaign": "<id>", "email": ""}` | `bulkmail:read` |
| Test | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/test` | `{"campaign": "<id>", "to": ""}` | `bulkmail` |

Campaign actions answer `{"campaign": <the record>}`. The audience's shape is the provider's (see
[Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail)). Only superusers may call these. Agents get them as MCP tools
(`bulkmail_start`, ...); `pb_hooks` can hook each (`onBulkmailStart`).

## Provide

Implement `bulkmailv1.Campaigns` and provide it in your extension's `Register`.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### count

Says how many recipients an audience reaches, how many of them are suppressed, and a few sample addresses.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/count` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote bulkmail count --audience <json>` |
| MCP | `bulkmail_count` |
| Token scope | `bulkmail:read` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `audience` | `--audience` | json |

### start

Queues a campaign's recipients and starts sending (Limit &gt; 0: at most that many new recipients).

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/start` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote bulkmail start --campaign <value> --limit <n>` |
| MCP | `bulkmail_start` |
| Token scope | `bulkmail` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign` | `--campaign` | string |
| `limit` | `--limit` | int |

### pause

Stops sending a campaign; Resume carries on.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/pause` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote bulkmail pause --campaign <value>` |
| MCP | `bulkmail_pause` |
| Token scope | `bulkmail` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign` | `--campaign` | string |

### resume

Carries on sending a paused campaign.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/resume` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote bulkmail resume --campaign <value>` |
| MCP | `bulkmail_resume` |
| Token scope | `bulkmail` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign` | `--campaign` | string |

### cancel

Stops a campaign for good; recipients not yet sent to are dropped.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/cancel` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote bulkmail cancel --campaign <value>` |
| MCP | `bulkmail_cancel` |
| Token scope | `bulkmail` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign` | `--campaign` | string |

### preview

Renders a campaign's message for one recipient (the first in its audience when Email is empty).

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/preview` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote bulkmail preview --campaign <value> --email <value>` |
| MCP | `bulkmail_preview` |
| Token scope | `bulkmail:read` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign` | `--campaign` | string |
| `email` | `--email` | string |

### test

Sends a campaign's message to one address, marked as a test.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/test` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote bulkmail test --campaign <value> --to <value>` |
| MCP | `bulkmail_test` |
| Token scope | `bulkmail` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|

# cache.clear/v1

[cache/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache/v1) is for an app's own code. This contract lets the app's admins empty its buckets from
outside that code, after a change that left stale entries behind: one bucket by name, or every bucket the app has.

A wire contract at `/api/_c/cache.clear/v1` ([clear.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/cache/clear/v1/clear.go)), one provider: whoever provides cache/v1 provides
this too.

## Use

```sh
pocketone remote cache clear --bucket pages.render   # one bucket
pocketone remote cache clear                          # every bucket of the app
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: <token with cache>" -d '{"bucket":"pages.render"}' https://your.app/api/_c/cache.clear/v1
```

The answer says how many keys went (`keys`).

## Provide

Implement `clearv1.Clearer` and provide it in `Register` beside your cache/v1 provider
(`clearv1.Contract.Provide(app, c)`). Empty only the calling app's buckets, never another app's on a shared store.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### clear

Empties one of the app's cache buckets, or every bucket it has.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/cache.clear/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote cache clear --bucket <value>` |
| MCP | `cache_clear_clear` |
| Token scope | `cache` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `bucket` | `--bucket` | string |

## Extensions

|---|---|

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache/v1

# cache/v1

A place for an app and its extensions to keep what was expensive to compute: rendered pages, API answers, resized
images. Code opens a **bucket** by name with the limits it wants and gets and sets keys in it. Who keeps the bytes
(memory and disk in this process, or Redis or Memcached shared between servers) is up to the provider, so a new one
replaces the old without any caller changing.

A bucket has its own caps, inside whatever room the provider has in all:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Eviction` | Which of the bucket's entries go first when it's full: `lru` (default), `mru`, `fifo`, `lifo` |
| `MaxItems` | Most entries the bucket holds |
| `MaxMemory` | Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds |
| `TTL` | How long an entry lives unless `Set` says otherwise |

Where entries live (memory, disk, another server) and how much room there is in all are the provider's and the
operator's business, not the bucket's.

The promise is a cache's: a provider may drop any entry at any time, and a `Get` may miss. It never returns a value
that was deleted, cleared or replaced since, nor one past its TTL. Each app has its own buckets, on a multisite host
too, even when the provider keeps every app's entries in one shared store.

An app service contract, one provider ([cache.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/cache/v1/cache.go)).

## Use

Open a bucket after registration (in a hook or at serve time), keep it, and use it:

```go
b, err := cachev1.Open(app, "myext.answers", cachev1.Options{MaxItems: 1000, TTL: 10 * time.Minute})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
if v, ok, _ := b.Get(ctx, key); ok {
	return v
}
v := compute()
_ = b.Set(ctx, key, v, 0) // 0 = the bucket's TTL
```

Name buckets after your extension (`myext.answers`) so two extensions never share one. Declare cache/v1 in
`WorksWith`: when nothing provides it, `Open` returns a bucket that keeps nothing, so the same code runs uncached.

To empty every bucket the app has (after a change that left stale entries), call `cachev1.Clear(ctx, app)`; the
app's admins can do the same from outside its code through [cache.clear/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1).

### Go values

To cache a Go value (a parsed template, a compiled program) without turning it into bytes on every `Set` and back on
every `Get`, make it a `cachev1.Item` and open the bucket with `OpenItems`:

```go
type compiled struct{ /* ... */ }

func (c *compiled) CacheSize() int64              { /* roughly the bytes it holds in memory */ }
func (c *compiled) MarshalCache() ([]byte, error) { /* bytes decode turns back into an equal value */ }
func (c *compiled) CacheVersion() string          { return "compiled/2" } // change it when the bytes' format changes

items, err := cachev1.OpenItems(app, "myext.compiled", cachev1.Options{MaxMemory: 64 << 20}, "compiled/2",
	func(b []byte) (*compiled, error) { /* ... */ })
if c, ok, _ := items.Get(ctx, key); ok {
	return c
}
c := compile()
_ = items.Set(ctx, key, c, 0)
```

What a provider does with them:

- **Each key holds its own item.** Nothing is shared between keys, buckets or apps: the code that owns the bucket owns
  its items, and every `Get` of a key returns that key's item, not a copy. `CacheSize` counts against the memory caps
  in place of a length.
- **Only a `Marshaler` leaves memory.** `CacheSize` alone makes an item that lives in memory only: evicted, it's
  gone. `MarshalCache` promises bytes that decode back to an equivalent item; the provider calls it only when it
  moves the item (to disk, across a restart, to another server), and may keep identical bytes from many keys once,
  there.
- **Versions keep old bytes out.** The provider keeps `CacheVersion` beside the bytes (bucket, key, version ->
  content), and a decoder of another version never sees them: a miss, so a code change that alters the format
  doesn't decode stale bytes.

On a provider that keeps only bytes, `Items` marshals on `Set` (with the version in front) and decodes on `Get`, so
the code is the same either way.

## Provide

Implement `cachev1.Cache` (`Bucket`, `Clear`) and `cachev1.Bucket` (`Get`, `Set`, `Delete`, `Clear`), and provide it
in `Register`, as the default if another provider should replace yours:

```go
cachev1.Contract.Provide(app, myCache)
```

`Cache.Clear` empties every bucket the app has, including ones it hasn't opened since it started. Provide
[cache.clear/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1) beside it.

To keep Go values without marshaling them, have your buckets also implement `cachev1.ItemBucket` (`GetItem`,
`SetItem`). Items and bytes share a bucket's keys: `Get` of a `Marshaler` returns its bytes (and misses on an item that
can't marshal), and `GetItem` of bytes of the decoder's version returns them decoded, as the key's item from then on.
Never hand one key's item to another key. A bucket that only keeps bytes needs nothing more: `Items` marshals for it.

Keep each app's buckets apart: on a shared store (one per process, or Redis), prefix keys with `extkit.AppID(app)` and
the bucket name. Treat `Options` as caps you keep as well as your storage allows (Redis has its own eviction), and
say in your README which ones you honour.

# cli.commands/v1

The `pocketone` command tree. Every operation of every wire contract linked into the binary is a command under
`remote`, with no code: `pocketone remote restore to --at -2h` calls restore/v1's `RestoreTo` on the project's
remote. An extension replaces one of those commands by providing the same path, or adds commands of its own. One
provider per path; when two extensions provide the same path, `pocketone.yaml` picks one.

A keyed contract (by command path), in the developer's `pocketone` process ([commands.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/cli/commands/v1/commands.go)).

## Use

The generated commands, for any contract:

- **Path:** `remote`, the contract id's words, then the operation: restore/v1's `restore_to` is
  `remote restore to`, mail.suppression/v1's `check` is `remote mail suppression check`, remote/v1's `status` is
  `remote status` (`clicmdv1.PathOf`).
- **Flags:** one per field of the operation's input (`--at`, `--email`, `--campaign`), plus `--json` for the
  whole input (`@file`, `-` for stdin) and `--remote` (a remote's name or a URL; default: the project's default
  remote). Times take RFC 3339, a local time (`2026-11-10 15:00`) or a duration from now (`-2h`).
- **Output:** the answer as JSON; streams print one JSON line per entry until Ctrl-C.
- **Auth:** the remote's saved login (`pocketone login`), or `P1_TOKEN` in CI.
- **Not commands:** public operations that take or return a raw body (an unsubscribe page, a mail provider's
  webhook); they're for browsers and services.

A remote that doesn't offer the contract answers "this remote doesn't offer restore/v1".

## Provide

Provide a command in your extension's `Register`. The same path as a generated command replaces it; a new path adds
one:

```go
clicmdv1.Contract.Provide(app, clicmdv1.Command{
	Path:  "remote rehash",
	Short: "Rehash every stored password",
	Flags: func(fs *pflag.FlagSet) { fs.Bool("dry-run", false, "only count") },
	Run: func(c *clicmdv1.Ctx, args []string) error {
		caller, err := c.Caller("rehash/v1") // the command's remote, with its login
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return caller.Call(c, "POST", "", nil, nil)
	},
})
```

and declare `Implements: extkit.IDs("cli.commands/v1")`. Two providers of one path fail the start until
`pocketone.yaml` picks:

```yaml
providers:
  cli.commands/v1:
    remote rehash: rehasher
```

A binary builds its tree with `clicmdv1.Mount(app, rootCmd)` once the app's contracts are sealed; the standard set
does it in `Register`. Commands already on the tree (`remote add`, `remote whoami`) stay unless a provider replaces
them.

## Extensions

# deploy/v1

A project's code on an app: `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations`, `pb_public` and packages. Clients send only the files
the app lacks, then swap the new set in at once. Restart and logs are [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1)'s, which
it requires.

A routed contract ([deploy.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/deploy/v1/deploy.go)): its provider is an `http.Handler` serving the file API below. A
multisite host can provide it for its instances.

## Use

| HTTP | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/check` | which files the app lacks (JSON) |
| `POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/blobs` | upload them (gzip bytes) |
| `POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/commit` | swap the new code set in (JSON) |
| `GET /api/_c/deploy/v1/files` | list deployed files |
| `DELETE /api/_c/deploy/v1/files` | delete files |
| `GET` / `PUT /api/_c/deploy/v1/files/raw` | read or write one file (raw bytes) |
| `GET /api/_c/deploy/v1/tree` | the app's code tree, for two-way sync |

Token scopes: `deploy` (everything) and `deploy:read` (list, read, tree). The CLI: `pocketone deploy`, `dev`,
`pull`.

## Provide

Provide an `http.Handler` that serves the API under `deployv1.Prefix`:

```go
deployv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, handler)
```

A host provides it for its instances with `deployv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, factory)` and
`extkit.HostRoutes(host, deployv1.Contract, multisite.InstanceID, next)` in its instance routes
(`multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes`, after the gates).

## Commands and APIs

Its own HTTP API under `/api/_c/deploy/v1/`, described above. It has no generated commands or MCP tools. [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote) explains how PocketOne apps are managed from afar.

|---|---|
| [deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | provides (default) |

# gate/v1

What admits requests on a multisite host before an instance is served here or forwarded to another server: a peer
allow list, the real client IP behind a proxy, rate limits. Gates run in order and every one must admit; a gate may
answer the request itself (429, 403).

A host-scope service contract, many providers in order ([gate.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/gate/v1/gate.go)).

## Use

Nothing to call: the host runs every gate on every request. Pick or order them in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  gate/v1: [firewall]
```

## Provide

Implement `gatev1.Gate` (`AllowPeer` before routing, `Admit` per instance, returning a release function), and
`gatev1.ClientIPResolver` if the gate knows the real client. Provide it in a host extension's `RegisterHost`:

```go
gatev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myGate)
```

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | provides |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

# http.wrap/v1

Middleware around everything a multisite host serves: health, every instance, forwarded requests. Wrappers nest in
provider order, the first outermost (a Server-Timing header first, so it measures everything inside it).

A host-scope service contract, many providers in order ([wrap.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/http/wrap/v1/wrap.go)).

## Use

Nothing to call: the host wraps its handler with every provider. Order them in `pocketone.yaml` if needed:

```yaml
providers:
  http.wrap/v1: [servertiming]
```

## Provide

Implement `wrapv1.Wrapper` (`Wrap(next http.Handler) http.Handler`) and provide it in a host extension's
`RegisterHost`:

```go
wrapv1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myWrapper)
```

## Extensions

|---|---|
| [servertiming](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/servertiming) | provides |

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.source/v1

# instance.source/v1

The record of one instance on a multisite host: its id, hostnames, PocketBase version, folder, secrets, limits,
superusers, per-extension settings, whether it's blocked or runs elsewhere. Every host contract reads the same record:
runtimes run it, gates admit requests for it. A source supplies the records and streams changes.

A host-scope service contract ([instance.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/instance/source/v1/instance.go), [limits.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/instance/source/v1/limits.go)).

## Use

A host takes its records from whichever extension provides this contract: by default its `instances` file
(`instances: { file: instances.yaml }`), or a control plane's mirror (ext/mothership). In Go the record is
`sourcev1.Instance` (`multisite.Instance` is the same type).

## Provide

Implement `sourcev1.Source`: `Snapshot(ctx)` returns every instance, `Watch(ctx)` streams changes (upserts and
deletes) until ctx is done. Provide it on the host's scope in a host extension's `RegisterHost`:

```go
sourcev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, mySource)
```

In tests, [sourcetest](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/instance/source/v1/sourcetest/sourcetest.go) provides it: `src, scope := sourcetest.Scope(instances...)` gives a
sealed host scope with a fixed list, and `src.Set(inst)` / `src.Delete(id)` change it the way an edit to the instances
file would.

## Extensions

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership) | provides |
| [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | requires |

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.fallback/v1

# mail.fallback/v1

Where an app's mail goes when its SMTP is off. Providers form an ordered chain: each sends a message or passes it on;
when all pass, PocketBase sends it its own way (`sendmail`). An app with SMTP on never reaches the chain.

A service ([fallback.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/fallback/v1/fallback.go)), many providers, open to `pb_hooks`.

## Use

Nothing to call: mail an app sends with SMTP off goes through the chain. Order the providers in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  mail.fallback/v1: [mailtrap, mailrelay]
```

## Provide

Implement `fallbackv1.Sender` (`Send(ctx, *mailer.Message)`, returning `fallbackv1.ErrPass` to pass), provide it,
and bind the chain once:

```go
fallbackv1.Contract.Provide(app, mySender{})
fallbackv1.Bind(app)
```

From `pb_hooks`:

```js
onContracts((e) => {
  e.provide("mail.fallback/v1", {
    send(m) {
      if (!m.to.some((a) => a.address.endsWith("@example.com"))) throw new ContractError("pass")
      // send it your way
    },
  })
  e.next()
})
```

## Extensions

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [mailrelay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay) | provides |
| [mailtrap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap) | provides |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1

# mail.feedback/v1

What mail providers report back about mail an app sent: bounces, spam complaints, unsubscribes. The provider of this
contract receives the reports and raises one event per address; any number of extensions act on them through one
hook. A suppression list adds the address, a CRM marks the contact, `pb_hooks` logs it.

A wire contract ([feedback.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/feedback/v1/feedback.go)). Its operations are public: SES messages are checked by their SNS
signature, webhook calls by a shared secret.

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | What sends it |
|---|---|---|
| SES | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/ses` | an Amazon SNS HTTPS subscription for SES bounce and complaint notifications |
| Webhook | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/webhook` with `X-Feedback-Secret` | any provider: `{"type": "bounce\|complaint\|unsubscribe", "email": "...", "campaign": "..."}` |

Act on the events in Go:

```go
feedbackv1.OnEvent(app).BindFunc(func(e *feedbackv1.Event) error {
	// e.Kind: bounce, complaint or unsubscribe; e.Email, e.Campaign, e.Source
	return e.Next()
})
```

## Provide

Implement `feedbackv1.Receiver`: check each report, then call `feedbackv1.Raise(app, &feedbackv1.Event{...})` for
each address. Where the webhook secret comes from is the provider's (Bulk Mail keeps it in its settings).

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### s_e_s

Takes an Amazon SNS delivery carrying SES bounce and complaint notifications (and confirms the topic subscription). Point an SNS HTTPS subscription here.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/ses` |
| Token scope | public |
| Body | the raw upload, not JSON |

### webhook

Takes {"type": "bounce|complaint|unsubscribe", "email": ..., "campaign": ...} from any provider, with the shared secret in the X-Feedback-Secret header.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/webhook` |
| Token scope | public |
| Body | the raw upload, not JSON |

## Extensions

|---|---|
| [bulkmail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | provides (default) |

# mail.suppression/v1

The addresses an app must not send bulk mail to (unsubscribed, bounced, complained, added by hand), and the
unsubscribe link in every bulk message. Anything that mails many people checks it.

A wire contract ([suppression.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/suppression/v1/suppression.go)).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Check | `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/check?email=` | superusers (`suppression:read`) |
| Suppress | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/suppress` `{"email", "reason", "source", "campaign"}` | superusers (`suppression`) |
| Unsuppress | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsuppress` `{"email"}` | superusers (`suppression`) |
| UnsubscribePage | `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe?t=<signed token>` | public: the link in a message |
| Unsubscribe | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe` | public: the page's form, or a mail provider's one-click POST |

Reasons: `unsubscribed`, `bounced`, `complained`, `manual`. The page never unsubscribes on a `GET` (link scanners
open every URL in a message); one-click unsubscribes follow RFC 8058 (`List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`). The token is
signed by the provider, so only links it issued work.

## Provide

Implement `suppressionv1.List`; sign the tokens in the links your messages carry, and point `List-Unsubscribe`
at `/api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe?t=...`.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### check

Says whether an address is suppressed, and why.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/check` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote mail suppression check --email <value>` |
| MCP | `mail_suppression_check` |
| Token scope | `suppression:read` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `--email` | string |

### suppress

Adds an address (or changes its reason).

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/suppress` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote mail suppression suppress --email <value> --reason <value> --source <value> --campaign <value>` |
| MCP | `mail_suppression_suppress` |
| Token scope | `suppression` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `--email` | string |
| `reason` | `--reason` | string |
| `source` | `--source` | string |
| `campaign` | `--campaign` | string |

### unsuppress

Removes an address, so it receives bulk mail again.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsuppress` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote mail suppression unsuppress --email <value>` |
| MCP | `mail_suppression_unsuppress` |
| Token scope | `suppression` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `--email` | string |

### unsubscribe_page

Is the page an unsubscribe link opens (?t=&lt;signed token&gt;). It never unsubscribes by itself: link scanners open every URL in a message.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe` |
| Token scope | public |
| Answer | a file or page, not JSON |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `t` | `--t` | string |

### unsubscribe

Confirms the page's form, or a mail provider's one-click POST (List-Unsubscribe=One-Click).

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe` |
| Token scope | public |
| Answer | a file or page, not JSON |
| Body | the raw upload, not JSON |

# mcp/v1

The app's [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint, so agents (a Claude connector, Claude
Code, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with it. It stays at `/mcp`: people paste that URL, MCP versions itself
in the protocol, and OAuth tokens are bound to the resource URL.

What every provider serves the same way, the contract owns:

- **The routes:** `/mcp`, and its protected resource metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`.
- **The tools:** every wire contract the app provides, one tool per operation (`restore_points`, `bulkmail_start`,
  ...), with an input schema from the operation's types and called through the contract, so the same superuser
  check, scopes and hooks apply as over HTTP; and tools extensions add with `AddTool`.

A provider brings the protocol, sign-in and any tools of its own ([MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) adds `pb_*` tools over
the REST API). Replace it and the contract tools stay.

A service ([mcp.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mcp/v1/mcp.go)).

## Use

Add `https://<host>/mcp` to an MCP client and sign in. In Go, an extension adds a tool that isn't a contract
operation, and tells agents what its tools are for:

```go
mcpv1.AddTool(app, mcpv1.Tool{
	Name:        "notes_summarize_week",
	Description: "Summarizes this week's notes.",
	ReadOnly:    true,
	Call: func(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, args json.RawMessage) (any, error) { ... },
})
mcpv1.AddInstructions(app, "Use notes_summarize_week for weekly reviews.")
```

`mcpv1.Tools(app)` lists what every provider serves.

## Provide

Implement `mcpv1.Endpoint` (`ServeMCP` for requests to `/mcp`, `Metadata` for the protected resource metadata),
provide it, and bind the routes once:

```go
mcpv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myServer{})
mcpv1.Bind(app)
```

Serve `mcpv1.Tools(app)` in `tools/list` and `tools/call`, calling each tool as the signed-in caller.

`/mcp` skips PocketBase's `pbRejectUnknownToken`, so the provider rejects a bad token itself: a request with an
`Authorization` header and no signed-in caller (`e.Auth` is nil) gets 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
error="invalid_token"` challenge, never a guest's answer.

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [mcp](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | provides (default) |

<!-- /contracts:index -->
