# oauth/v1

An OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app: authorization code with PKCE, device code, refresh, revocation, and
client registration (dynamic, or by a client metadata document). The CLI's browser login and MCP clients such as
Claude sign in through it, and get API tokens ([tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tokens/v1)).

A routed contract ([oauth.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/oauth/v1/oauth.go)): the OAuth specs fix its API's shape, so its provider serves it as it is.

## Use

| HTTP | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | the server's metadata (RFC 8414 puts it at the root) |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize` | sign in and consent (browser) |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/token` | codes and refresh tokens for access tokens |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device` | start a device-code sign-in |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify` | enter the device code (browser) |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke` | revoke a token |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register` | dynamic client registration (when on) |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback` | sign-in through an OAuth2 provider (Google, Apple, ...) |

In Go, another extension (MCP) turns on dynamic registration and sets token lifetimes:
`oauthv1.Contract.Of(app)` → `EnableDynamicRegistration()`, `SetAccessTTL(path, ttl)`, `Issuer(e)`.

## Provide

Implement `oauthv1.Server` and serve the routes above (`extkit.EventServer` or `extkit.RouteBinder`); issue access
tokens through tokens/v1.

## Commands and APIs

Its own HTTP API under `/api/_c/oauth/v1/`, described above. It has no generated commands or MCP tools. [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote) explains how PocketOne apps are managed from afar.

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | provides |
| [mcp](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | works with |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

# remote/v1

Remote control of an app from afar: who your credential is and what the app offers, its status, a restart, and its
log. Every client starts here: `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` is the one fixed path, and its answer lists every other
contract the app offers. Contracts that add an area (deploy/v1) require this one.

A wire contract ([remote.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remote.go)); a multisite host can provide it for its instances, so it works for
instances running stock PocketBase images.

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| Whoami | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` | public (the answer says more when you're signed in) |
| Status | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` | `remote:read` |
| Restart | `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` | `remote` |
| Logs | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs?n=100` (server-sent events) | `remote:read` |

- **CLI:** `pocketone remote whoami | status | restart | logs`.
- **Go:** `remotev1.Contract.Must(app)` in the app, or `remotev1.NewClient(url, token, http)` from outside. The
  command-line client (linked remotes, saved logins, sign-in) is [remoteclient](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient).
- **Hooks:** `remotev1.OnRestart(app)` in Go, `onRemoteRestart` in `pb_hooks`, for every operation.
- **MCP:** a tool per operation (`remote_status`, ...).

## Provide

Implement `remotev1.Remote` and provide it in your extension's `Register`:

```go
remotev1.Contract.Provide(app, myRemote{})
```

A multisite host provides it for every instance with `remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, factory)` and
serves it with `remotev1.W.HostHandler` in its instance routes (`multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes`, after the gates;
see [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) and
[docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker)).

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### whoami

Says who the credential is, the app's name and URL, and the contracts it offers.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote whoami` |
| MCP | `remote_whoami` |
| Token scope | public |

### status

Reports whether the app is running, its versions, uptime and mode.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote status` |
| MCP | `remote_status` |
| Token scope | `remote:read` |

### restart

Restarts the app; requests in flight finish first.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote restart` |
| MCP | `remote_restart` |
| Token scope | `remote` |

### logs

Streams the app's log: the last entries, then new ones as they're written.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote logs --n <n>` |
| MCP | `remote_logs` |
| Token scope | `remote:read` |
| Answer | a stream of JSON entries (server-sent events); the command prints one line each |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `n` | `--n` | int |

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1

# restore/v1

Put an app's data back as it was at a moment. You ask for a moment ("Tuesday 15:00"); the app restores the closest
point it has at or before it and tells you which one it used. Providers differ only in how close they get:

- [pitr](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) keeps continuous history: any second inside its window.
- [backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups), the default, uses PocketBase's own backups (local or S3): the latest backup
  made at or before the moment. It steps aside when pitr is on for the app.

The app restarts to apply a restore; its data from before the restore is kept until the next one.

A wire contract ([restore.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/restore/v1/restore.go)); a multisite host may provide it for its instances (from host-level
snapshots).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| Points: what can be restored | `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` | `restore:read` |
| RestoreTo a moment | `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` with `{"at": "<RFC 3339 time>"}` | `restore` |

`Points` answers with the provider's name and either a `window` (`kind: "continuous"`) or a list of `snapshots`
(`kind: "snapshots"`, newest first), whether a restore is running, and the last restore. `RestoreTo` answers with
the `point` it restores from; `422 no_point` when there's nothing at or before the moment, `409 busy` while another
restore runs. Only superusers may call either.

- **Dashboard:** Settings → Backups gets a "Restore to a moment" section from this contract ([ui/main.js](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/restore/v1/ui/main.js)),
  whichever extension provides it: a time picker over pitr's window, or one that says which backup a moment uses.
- **Go:** `restorev1.Contract.Must(app).RestoreTo(ctx, auth, restorev1.RestoreInput{At: t})`, or
  `restorev1.NewClient(url, token, http)` from outside.
- **Hooks:** `restorev1.OnRestoreTo(app, fn)` in Go, `onRestoreRestoreTo` in `pb_hooks`: refuse or log a restore.
- **MCP:** `restore_points` and `restore_restore_to`.

## Provide

Implement `restorev1.Restorer` and provide it in your extension's `Register` (`ProvideDefault` if a better
provider should replace yours). Report the point you'll actually restore from, and restart the app to apply it.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### points

Says what the app's data can be restored to: a window of time (continuous history) or a list of moments (backups), and whether a restore is running.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote restore points` |
| MCP | `restore_points` |
| Token scope | `restore:read` |

### restore_to

Puts the app's data back as it was at the given moment, from the latest point at or before it. The app restarts to apply it; its current data is kept aside until the next restore.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote restore to --at <time>` |
| MCP | `restore_restore_to` |
| Token scope | `restore` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `at` | `--at` | time |

|---|---|
| [pitr](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | provides |
| [backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups) | provides (default) |

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1

# runtime/v1

What runs a multisite host's instances: [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) in-process,
[docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) in containers. A host can have several at once, in preference order: each
instance runs on the one it names (`runtime: docker` in its record), else the first that can serve it (by PocketBase
version, for example). Having a `multisite` section makes the binary a host; the runtimes are this contract's
providers.

A host-scope service contract, many providers in order ([runtime.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/runtime/v1/runtime.go)).

## Use

Pick and order the runtimes in `pocketone.yaml`; by default it's every linked runtime that's configured, in link
order (docker needs its `docker` section):

```yaml
multisite: {}
providers:
  runtime/v1: [pocker, docker]   # pocker first; docker for what pocker can't serve
```

## Provide

Implement `runtimev1.Runtime` (`Name`, `Serves`, `ServeInstance`, `Ready`) and any optional hooks the host
calls (`Prechecker`, `Syncer`, `Starter`, `Shutdowner`, `Statser`). Provide it in a host extension's
`RegisterHost`, only when it's configured:

```go
runtimev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myRuntime)
```

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | provides |
| [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | provides |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1

# settings/v1

The settings an app's own superusers change for its extensions (PITR's S3 bucket, Bulk Mail's sending limits), behind
one API: list them, read one, save one, test one without saving. Each extension keeps its settings its own way and
registers a section; the provider serves them all. Settings an operator sets for a whole host stay in
`pocketone.yaml`.

A wire contract ([settings.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/settings/v1/settings.go)).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| List | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1` | `settings:read` |
| Get | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get?extension=pitr` | `settings:read` |
| Save | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/save` with `{"extension": "pitr", "values": {...}}` | `settings` |
| Test | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/test` with `{"extension": "pitr", "values": {...}}` | `settings` |

Each extension's `values` are its own shape (see its README). Secrets come back empty with a flag that they're set;
saving an empty secret keeps the saved one. `Test` answers `{"ok": false, "message": ...}` when the settings don't
work. Only superusers may call any of them.

## Provide

**An extension with settings** registers a section in its `Register`:

```go
settingsv1.Add(app, mySection{}) // Info, Get, Save; Test too if the settings can be checked
```

and declares `WorksWith: extkit.IDs("settings/v1")`.

**A provider of the API** (ext/settings by default) implements `settingsv1.Settings` over
`settingsv1.Sections(app)`.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### list

Names the extensions whose settings this app's admins can change.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote settings list` |
| MCP | `settings_list` |
| Token scope | `settings:read` |

### get

Returns one extension's settings. Secrets come back empty, with a flag saying they're set.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote settings get --extension <value>` |
| MCP | `settings_get` |
| Token scope | `settings:read` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `extension` | `--extension` | string |

### save

Replaces one extension's settings and applies them. A secret left empty keeps its saved value. Settings a host sets are read-only here.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/save` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote settings save --extension <value> --values <json>` |
| MCP | `settings_save` |
| Token scope | `settings` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `extension` | `--extension` | string |
| `values` | `--values` | json |

### test

Checks one extension's settings without saving them (a test write to a bucket, a test message).

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/test` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote settings test --extension <value> --values <json>` |
| MCP | `settings_test` |
| Token scope | `settings` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `extension` | `--extension` | string |
| `values` | `--values` | json |

# templates/v1

An extension that serves pages of its own (tokens' OAuth sign-in, consent and MFA screens) keeps them as a set of Go
`html/template` files, usually embedded in the binary. A project themes them by ejecting the set and editing its copy:
any file it has replaces the built-in one, and anything it leaves out falls back. The format is always Go templates,
so the built-in pages and the ejected ones are the same files.

A set is every `*.tpl` file in an `fs.FS`, at any depth. Each file is one template named by its path without `.tpl`
(`signin`, `parts/head`), so pages include shared pieces with `{{template "parts/head" .}}`.

An app service contract, one provider ([templates.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/templates/v1/templates.go)).

## Use

Add your set in `Register`, then render a page through the provider at request time, falling back to your own set
when nothing provides the contract:

```go
//go:embed templates/oauth
var oauthFiles embed.FS

files, _ := fs.Sub(oauthFiles, "templates/oauth")
templatesv1.Add(app, "oauth", files)

// in a handler
if t, ok := templatesv1.Contract.Of(app); ok {
	return t.Render(e, "oauth", "signin", http.StatusOK, data)
}
set, err := templatesv1.Parse(files, nil)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
return templatesv1.Write(e, set, "signin", http.StatusOK, data)
```

Declare the contract in `WorksWith`. Pass anything that must not be escaped (ready-made HTML) as `template.HTML`.

## Provide

Implement `templatesv1.Templates` (`Render`, `Eject`) and provide it in `Register`. Read the sets with
`templatesv1.Set` and `templatesv1.Names`, and build each page with `templatesv1.Parse(set, projectCopy)` and
`templatesv1.Write`, so every provider renders the same way:

```go
templatesv1.Contract.Provide(app, myTemplates)
```

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

|---|---|
| [templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates) | provides |
| [tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | works with |

# tls/v1

The TLS of a multisite host's main listener. Its provider hands the host a `tls.Config` (certificates on demand,
for hostnames an instance serves) and, for HTTP challenges, a wrapper for the plain-HTTP listener. With no provider
the host uses the certificate files in its `server` section, or plain HTTP.

A host-scope service contract, one provider ([tls.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/tls/v1/tls.go)).

## Use

Nothing to call: the host's listener uses it. Turn the provider on in its own section (`autotls: { auto: true }`).

## Provide

Implement `tlsv1.Provider` and provide it in a host extension's `RegisterHost`; only issue certificates for
hostnames `served` reports true for.

```go
tlsv1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myTLS)
```

## Extensions

|---|---|
| [autotls](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls) | provides |

# tokens/v1

An app's API tokens, as other extensions use them. Tokens are scoped: a token limited to scopes works only on the
requests those scopes reach. Extensions register their own scopes, read the token a request came with, and limit
requests they make on someone's behalf, all through this package.

A service with its own API ([tokens.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/tokens/v1/tokens.go)), served at `/api/_c/tokens/v1`.

## Use

| HTTP | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/tokens/v1/scopes` | the scopes a token may hold, and who may own tokens |
| `GET /api/_c/tokens/v1` | your tokens (superusers: `?owner=`, `?ownerCollection=`) |
| `POST /api/_c/tokens/v1` | create one (`{name, scopes, expires\|ttl}`); the secret is shown once |
| `DELETE /api/_c/tokens/v1/{id}` | revoke one |
| `POST /api/_c/tokens/v1/revoke-all` | revoke all of yours |

In Go:

```go
if tk, ok := tokensv1.Contract.Of(app); ok {
	tk.RegisterScope(tokensv1.Scope{Name: "notes:write", Description: "Change notes",
		Paths: []string{"/api/collections/notes/records"}, Methods: []string{"POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"}})
}
g := tokensv1.FromRequest(e)                       // the request's token, or nil (a JWT, or none)
ctx = tokensv1.WithScopes(ctx, []string{"notes:read"}) // requests made with ctx count as limited to these scopes
```

## Provide

Implement `tokensv1.Issuer` (`Verify`, `RegisterScope`, `Scopes`, `Reaches`), authenticate requests that carry a
token (setting `tokensv1.RequestKey` to the `*Grant`), honour `WithScopes` limits, and serve the token API (the
provider binds its own routes, `extkit.RouteBinder`).

## Commands and APIs

Its own HTTP API under `/api/_c/tokens/v1/`, described above. It has no generated commands or MCP tools. [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote) explains how PocketOne apps are managed from afar.

## Extensions

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | provides |
| [deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | works with |
| [mcp](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | works with |
| [remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | works with |

# vacuum/v1

SQLite keeps a database file as big as it ever was; compacting it (`VACUUM`) gives the space freed by deleted records
back to the disk. This contract says who does that for an app, how often, and how the last run went.

A wire contract at `/api/_c/vacuum/v1` ([vacuum.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/vacuum/v1/vacuum.go)), one provider. On a single app the
[vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum) extension provides it, on the schedule the app's admins set. A multisite host may
provide it for its instances instead: then the host compacts them on its own schedule, the app's vacuum extension steps
aside (no settings, no schedule of its own), and the app's admins see the host's status.

## Use

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: <token with vacuum:read>" https://your.app/api/_c/vacuum/v1
```

`provider` is who compacts (`vacuum` for the app itself, or the host), `enabled` and `every` the schedule, `last` the
last run (bytes saved, databases skipped as not worth it, any error) and `next` the next one.

## Provide

Implement `vacuumv1.Vacuum` and provide it in `Register` (`vacuumv1.Contract.Provide(app, v)`), or on a host for every
instance (`vacuumv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(hostScope, func(id string) vacuumv1.Vacuum {...})`). An app half that
also has settings or a schedule checks `extkit.HostProvides(app, "vacuum/v1")` in `Register` and leaves them out when
the host owns it.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote administration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### status

Says who compacts the app's databases, whether and how often, and how the last run went.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/vacuum/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote vacuum status` |
| MCP | `vacuum_status` |
| Token scope | `vacuum:read` |

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum) | provides |

# Auto TLS

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Automatic HTTPS certificates through ACME, with [CertMagic](https://github.com/caddyserver/certmagic) (Caddy's
certificate engine). PocketBase already gets Let's Encrypt certificates for `serve example.com`. Auto TLS takes over
that job and adds other certificate authorities, extra domains and wildcard certificates.

Status: stable on a multisite host, beta on a single app.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Auto TLS is built into `pocketone` and **off by default**. Turn it on with `--autotls` (or `auto: true` in
`pocketone.yaml`). It only does something when the app serves HTTPS, that is with `serve <domain>` or `--https`; on
plain HTTP it stays idle, and without it PocketBase's own certificates are used as before.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
import (
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/autotls"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
)

app := pocketbase.New()
extkit.MustRegister(app, autotls.NewApp(autotls.Config{Auto: true, Email: "ops@example.com"}))
app.Start()
```

## Configure

### Command-line flags

```sh
pocketone serve example.com --autotls --autotlsEmail ops@example.com
pocketone serve example.com --autotls --autotlsDomains "*.example.com" --autotlsDNS cloudflare   # token in $CF_API_TOKEN
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--autotls` | `false` | Turn it on. |
| `--autotlsEmail` | | ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. |
| `--autotlsCA` | `letsencrypt` | `letsencrypt`, `letsencrypt-staging`, `zerossl`, or an ACME directory URL. |
| `--autotlsDomains` | | Extra domains, obtained at start (comma separated). Wildcards need `--autotlsDNS`. |
| `--autotlsDNS` | | DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges. Only `cloudflare` is supported. |
| `--autotlsDNSTokenEnv` | `CF_API_TOKEN` | Environment variable holding the DNS provider's API token. |

### pocketone.yaml

The `autotls` section sets the defaults for those flags. Flags win over the file.

```yaml
autotls:
  auto: true
  email: ops@example.com
  ca: letsencrypt
  domains: ["*.example.com"]   # wildcards need dns
  dns:
    provider: cloudflare
    api_token: $CF_API_TOKEN   # read from the .env beside pocketone.yaml
```

`storage` is only in the file: where certificates are kept (default `pb_data/.autotls`). The DNS token can be given
as `api_token` (write `$VAR` to read it from the `.env` beside the file) or through `api_token_env`, the name of an
environment variable. `api_token` is only used when `--autotlsDNS` names the same provider as the file.

The Cloudflare token needs permission to edit the zone's DNS.

There are no dashboard settings.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `autotls:`

Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls* flags win.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | bool |  | Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. |
| `email` | string |  | ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. |
| `ca` | string |  | letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. |
| `storage` | string |  | Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. |
| `domains` | list of string |  | Extra domains to get at start; wildcards (*.example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. |
| `dns.provider` | string |  | DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. |
| `dns.api_token` | string |  | The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. |
| `dns.api_token_env` | string |  | Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv. |

## Use

Once on, there's nothing to click. Start the app as usual with `serve <domain>` (or `--https`):

- **Which hostnames get a certificate.** The domains given to `serve` and their `www.` variants, issued on the first
  request for each, plus `--autotlsDomains`, obtained at start. Any other hostname is refused at the TLS handshake, so
  a random `Host` can't trigger issuance.
- **How they're proved.** TLS-ALPN-01 on the HTTPS port, or DNS-01 when a DNS provider is set (needed for wildcards).
  HTTP-01 isn't used on a single app, because port 80 is PocketBase's redirect server.
- **Renewal** is automatic.
- **Where they're stored.** `pb_data/.autotls` by default, separate from PocketBase's own `.autocert_cache`.

Settings are checked at start, before anything touches the network. A wildcard domain without a DNS provider, a
Cloudflare provider without a token, or an unknown provider stops the app with an error such as:

```
tls.domains: wildcard "*.example.com" needs a DNS provider (tls.dns); per-hostname certificates work without one
```

With debug logging, the start shows `autotls: CertMagic serves HTTPS certificates` with the CA and extra domains.

Use `--autotlsCA letsencrypt-staging` while testing, so failed attempts don't count against Let's Encrypt's rate limits.

## Integrations

### Multisite hosts

On a [multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) host (any runtime: pocker or docker), the stock `pocketone` binary runs
`autotls.New()`, a host extension that gets certificates for every instance the host serves. It's configured by the same `autotls`
section:

```yaml
autotls:
  auto: true
  email: ops@example.com
  storage: ./pb_root/.pocker-certs   # default: .pocker-certs in the runtime's instance root
  domains: ["*.example.com", "example.com"]
  dns: { provider: cloudflare, api_token_env: CF_API_TOKEN }   # only needed for wildcards
```

- Without `dns`, every hostname the instance source maps gets its own certificate on its first TLS handshake, with any
  DNS host and no API token. Hostnames no instance serves never trigger issuance.
- Challenges include HTTP-01 on the host's port 80, as well as TLS-ALPN-01 and DNS-01.
- Certificate files (`server.tls.cert`/`key`) stay a core host feature. Setting both files and `auto` is an error.
- Certificates belong to the host, not to instances; the single-app extension (`NewApp`) is a separate type so
  it never runs per instance.

### Building on Auto TLS

- `autotls.New()` is a host extension (`multisite.Extension`) that provides the [tls/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tls/v1)
  contract when `auto` is on. A host adds it to its host extensions (a `pocker.Server` built by hand takes it in
  `Extensions` too):

  ```go
  h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Extensions: []multisite.Extension{autotls.New()}})
  ```

- `AutoTLS.Config` can be set in Go before the server starts; the `autotls` section is read only when `Auto` is false
  there.
- `autotls.SupportedDNSProviders` lists the `dns.provider` values it understands.

## Example

Auto TLS is built into `pocketone`: [`examples/pocketone/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/main.go) registers it with the other default extensions.

## How it works

- Go module `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/autotls`.
- On a single app, an `OnServe` hook swaps the TLS config of PocketBase's HTTPS server for CertMagic's. PocketBase's
  own host policy (the `serve` domains and `www.`) decides which on-demand hostnames are allowed. The certificate
  manager stops when the app terminates.
- TLS 1.2 is the minimum; `h2` and `http/1.1` are offered, and `acme-tls/1` stays on for TLS-ALPN challenges.
- A wildcard in `domains` covers one level (`*.example.com` covers `a.example.com`, not `a.b.example.com`).

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups

# Backups

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Restore an app to a moment from its own backups. Ask for "Tuesday 15:00" and the app restores the latest backup made
at or before it, wherever its backups are kept (pb_data/backups or S3). Every app gets this; with
[PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) on, PITR answers instead and restores any second in its window.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Backups is built into `pocketone` and **on by default**; there's nothing to install. In your own Go build:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{backups.New()}, nil, nil)
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/backups`.

## Configure

There's nothing to configure: it reads the backups PocketBase already makes (Settings → Backups, including the
automatic schedule and S3). An app turns it off with `extensions: { backups: { enabled: false } }`.

## Use

It's the default provider of the [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1) contract:

```bash
# what can be restored (superuser token)
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" https://app.example.com/api/_c/restore/v1
# restore the latest backup at or before a moment
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"at":"2026-11-10T15:00:00Z"}' https://app.example.com/api/_c/restore/v1/restore
```

The answer names the backup it restores. The app restarts to apply it, as a restore from Settings → Backups does.
In the dashboard, Settings → Backups has a "Restore to a moment" section (restore/v1's own screen) that shows which
backup a moment uses.
Agents get the same through MCP (`restore_points`, `restore_restore_to`).

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [points](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1#points) | `pocketone remote restore points` | `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` | `restore_points` |
| [restore_to](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1#restore_to) | `pocketone remote restore to --at <time>` | `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` | `restore_restore_to` |

## Integrations

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | Also provides restore/v1, at any second rather than at backup times; when it's on for an app, Backups steps aside. |
| [S3 Fallback](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback) | Backups kept on the host's storage are listed and restored the same way. |
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) | restore/v1 is the contract; any extension or host can provide it instead. |

## Example

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app whose restore/v1 comes from its backups: create a backup in the dashboard
// (Settings → Backups), then `curl -H "Authorization: <superuser token>" http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/_c/restore/v1`
// lists it, and POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore with {"at": "<RFC 3339 time>"} restores the latest backup before it.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/backups"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{backups.New()}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

`Points` lists the backups filesystem (`app.NewBackupsFilesystem()`), newest first, by each file's time. `RestoreTo`
picks the newest backup at or before the moment and runs PocketBase's own `RestoreBackup`, which swaps pb_data and
restarts the app.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail

# Bulk Mail

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Campaigns to your app's own users, from the dashboard. You pick who gets the mail with a collection, a view or SQL,
write the message, and Bulk Mail sends it at a steady pace through your app's mail settings. It adds one-click
unsubscribe, keeps a list of addresses that must never be mailed again, and handles bounces and spam complaints.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Bulk Mail is built into `pocketone` and **on** for every app. Nothing is sent until a superuser starts a campaign.

In your own Go build, register the extension before the app starts. Bind it into the JS runtime too if you want
`$bulkmail` in `pb_hooks`:

```go
mail := bulkmail.New(bulkmail.Config{Rate: 5, Daily: 5000})

app := pocketbase.New()
extkit.MustRegister(app, mail)
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { extkit.BindJS(app, rt, mail) }})
app.Start()
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail`.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section or command-line flag. The limits are fixed in the binary; `pocketone` uses the
defaults:

| Limit | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Per second | 5 | The most messages this app sends per second. A campaign can only lower it. |
| Per day | 5,000 | The most messages this app sends per UTC day, across all campaigns. |

In a custom build, set them with `bulkmail.Config{Rate, Daily}`. `Daily: bulkmail.NoBulkMail` forbids sending; the
screens then say so.

### Settings → Mail

Campaigns send through the app's own mail settings and from its sender, both set on **Settings → Mail**. Below that
form there's a **Bulk mail** section:

- **Postal address**: shown in every campaign footer. Anti-spam laws require one.
- **Unsubscribe mailbox**: optional. Adds a `mailto:` alternative to the `List-Unsubscribe` header.
- **Bounces and complaints** (click to open):
  - **Amazon SES (SNS) endpoint**: the URL to subscribe to the SNS topic your SES identity sends bounce and complaint
    notifications to.
  - **Allowed SNS topic ARNs**: comma separated. Empty accepts any topic with a valid AWS signature.
  - **Generic webhook** and **Webhook secret**: for other providers. The webhook is off until you set a secret.

The section also shows this app's limits and how many messages it sent today. Click **Save bulk mail settings**.

Unsubscribe links and the feedback URLs are built from **Settings → Application → Application URL**, so set it to
the address people reach your app on.

The settings are stored in the app's database (a `_params` row), so they go along with its backups. Secrets are
never shown again after saving.

## Use

The dashboard gets a **Mail** link in its menu, with two pages: **Campaigns** and **Suppressions**. Only superusers see
them.

### Write a campaign

1. Open **Mail** and click **New campaign**. It starts as a draft for verified users of `users`.
2. Fill in **Name**, **Subject** and **Body**.
3. Under **Audience**, choose who gets it:
   - **Filter**: a **Collection** (or a view), an optional **Filter** in the same syntax as API rules, and the
     **Email field** that holds the address (an email or text field, or a view's computed column).
   - **SQL**: a read-only `SELECT` that returns an `email` column. Every other column is available to the message.

   Click **Count recipients** to see how many match, how many are suppressed, and a few sample addresses.
4. Optional: **Vars (JSON)** for values used in the message, a **Schedule (UTC)**, and **Max per second** to send
   slower than the app's limit.
5. Click **Save changes**. **Preview** shows the message for one recipient; **Send test** mails it to the
   **Test address**.

A view is the easy way to build a dynamic audience: it picks who gets mail and computes the columns the message
uses. The [example](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/bulkmail/example/demo.go) creates one called `newsletter_audience`.

### Placeholders

In the subject and body:

- `{{record.field}}`: a field or column of the recipient's row, for example `{{record.name}}`.
- `{{email}}`, `{{campaign.name}}` and `{{unsubscribe_url}}`.
- Campaign vars: `{"promo": "X"}` gives `{{promo}}`. A var can be computed once when sending starts:
  `{"count": {"sql": "SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM users"}}`.
- `{{if record.field}}…{{else}}…{{end}}` blocks, and `{{if !record.field}}` for the opposite.

Values are HTML-escaped in the body. An unsubscribe footer with your postal address is always added.

### Send

Click **Send** (or **Schedule** when a time is set) and confirm. The campaign page shows its status and progress
(sent, queued, skipped, failed), and a **Recipients** table you can filter by status. While it runs you can
**Pause**, **Resume** or **Cancel** it.

- Every address is queued once per campaign. Sending a finished campaign again mails only new matches.
- A message counts as sent only once the mail server accepts it, so a restart doesn't send twice or skip anyone.
- A permanent error (SMTP 5xx) fails that recipient. Other errors are retried, up to three attempts.
- A campaign pauses itself when more than 5% of its sends fail after the first 100, or when spam complaints pass
  0.3% of its sends (at least 3). The reason shows next to its status.

### Suppressions

**Mail → Suppressions** lists the addresses that never receive campaign mail, whatever the audience says.
Unsubscribes, permanent bounces and complaints are added automatically. Click **Add address** to add one by hand, a
row to edit or delete it, or **Export CSV** to download the list.

### Unsubscribing

Every message has a signed unsubscribe link and the `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post: One-Click`
headers that Gmail and Yahoo require for bulk senders. Opening the link shows a confirm button, so link scanners
can't unsubscribe anyone. The one-click request from a mail provider unsubscribes directly.

### Try it locally

In dev mode with SMTP off, `pocketone` catches every mail, bulk mail included, in an inbox at
http://127.0.0.1:8025:

```bash
pocketone serve --dev
```

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### [bulkmail/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1)

|---|---|---|---|
| [count](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1#count) | `pocketone remote bulkmail count --audience <json>` | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/count` | `bulkmail_count` |
| [start](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1#start) | `pocketone remote bulkmail start --campaign <value> --limit <n>` | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/start` | `bulkmail_start` |
| [pause](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1#pause) | `pocketone remote bulkmail pause --campaign <value>` | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/pause` | `bulkmail_pause` |
| [resume](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1#resume) | `pocketone remote bulkmail resume --campaign <value>` | `POST /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/resume` | `bulkmail_resume` |

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Add the same extension value to `srv.Extensions` and every instance gets Bulk Mail. Each instance can override its limits (below). `$bulkmail` only reaches the instance's own data, so it's safe for untrusted tenants. |
| [Mailtrap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap) | In dev mode with SMTP off, campaign mail lands in the local inbox instead of being sent. |

### Per-instance settings (pocker)

Each instance's `extensions.bulkmail` settings apply over the `Config` given to `bulkmail.New`:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: abc
    extensions: { bulkmail: { rate: 2, daily: 1000 } }
  - id: free-plan-app
    extensions: { bulkmail: { daily: 0 } }      # may not send bulk mail
  - id: other
    extensions: { bulkmail: { enabled: false } } # no Bulk Mail at all
```

### Go API

`bulkmail.For(app)` returns the app's service: `Start`, `StartLimit`, `Pause`, `Resume`, `Cancel`, `Preview`, `Test`,
`CountAudience`, `Suppress`, `Unsuppress`, `IsSuppressed`, `Unsubscribe`, `UnsubscribeURL`, `Limits`, and the hooks:

- `OnSend` fires before every campaign message (not test sends). Change the message, or return an error to fail that
  recipient.
- `OnUnsubscribe` fires when someone unsubscribes through a link or the one-click header.
- `OnFeedback` fires for each bounce or complaint a provider reports.

`Config.Mailer` swaps the mail client, for example for a platform relay. `Config.PublicURL` sets the base of
unsubscribe links instead of the Application URL.

### JS API

`$bulkmail` in `pb_hooks`:

```js
$bulkmail.start(id, [limit])     // limit: queue only the next N new recipients
$bulkmail.pause(id); $bulkmail.resume(id); $bulkmail.cancel(id)
$bulkmail.test(id, [to]); $bulkmail.preview(id, [email])
$bulkmail.count({collection, filter, email_field} | {sql})   // {count, suppressed, sample}
$bulkmail.suppress(email, [reason]); $bulkmail.unsuppress(email); $bulkmail.isSuppressed(email)
$bulkmail.unsubscribe(email, [campaignId]); $bulkmail.unsubscribeURL(email, [campaignId])
$bulkmail.limits()               // {rate, daily, sentToday}
```

React to activity with record hooks on the collections below, for example
`onRecordAfterCreateSuccess((e) => { … }, "_bulkmail_suppressions")`.

### API: contracts

Bulk Mail has no routes of its own. Its API is three contracts it provides, plus a section in
[settings/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1) (`?extension=bulkmail`: sender details, limits and the feedback
endpoint URLs; secrets are never returned):

| Contract | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [bulkmail/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1) | Count an audience; start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign (superusers). |
| [mail.suppression/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1) | The suppression list (check, suppress, unsuppress) and the unsubscribe link in every message (public, signed). Bulk Mail keeps it by default; when another extension provides it, Bulk Mail asks that one before queueing and before each send. |
| [mail.feedback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1) | Bounce and complaint reports from SES (SNS) or a webhook (public; `X-Feedback-Secret`). Any extension can act on them. |

Campaigns and suppressions are created and edited through the regular records API. A campaign's `from_name` and
`from_address` override the app's sender, but only through the records API, JS or Go (the dashboard doesn't show
them), since the app's mail account can usually send only as identities it has verified.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/bulkmail/example/main.go) runs one app with bulk mail: the Mail page, campaigns to the app's own users and `$bulkmail` in JS hooks. Run it with `go run ./example serve --dev` from this folder; the dev mail trap at http://127.0.0.1:8025 catches every mail.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app with bulk mail: a "Mail" page in the dashboard, campaigns to the app's
// own users, and $bulkmail in JS hooks.
//
// Run it in dev mode: while SMTP is off, PocketOne's dev mail trap catches every mail (bulk mail included) and
// shows it at http://127.0.0.1:8025, with nothing else to install:
//
//	go run ./example serve --dev
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit/js"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	registerDemoView(app) // a "newsletter_audience" view to use as a campaign audience (demo.go)

	// the same extension value pocker would host on every instance (srv.Extensions = append(srv.Extensions, mail))
	mail := bulkmail.New(bulkmail.Config{
		Rate:  5,    // messages per second
		Daily: 5000, // messages per day; bulkmail.NoBulkMail forbids sending
	})
	extkit.MustRegister(app, mail)

	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
		OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { extkit.BindJS(app, rt, mail) }, // $bulkmail in JS hooks
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Go module `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail`, an [`extkit`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/extkit/extkit.go) extension.
  [`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/bulkmail/example/main.go) runs one app with Bulk Mail (`go run ./example serve --dev`).
- The audience is resolved when sending starts and queued into a ledger first (one row per campaign and address,
  unique). A background sender then mails one message at a time through the app's mail client, at the lower of the
  app's rate and the campaign's.
- SQL audiences and SQL vars run with SQLite's `query_only` on, inside a transaction that is always rolled back.
- Unsubscribe links are signed with HMAC and a per-app secret, generated on first use.
- SES feedback: SNS signatures are verified, and signing certificates are fetched only from
  `sns.<region>.amazonaws.com`. Permanent bounces and complaints go on the suppression list.

### Data

| Collection | What |
|---|---|
| `_bulkmail_campaigns` | Content, audience, vars, status, counters, schedule. |
| `_bulkmail_sends` | The ledger: campaign, email, status (`queued`, `sent`, `skipped`, `failed`), reason, attempts. |
| `_bulkmail_suppressions` | Addresses that never receive campaign mail, with the reason. |

All are superuser-only system collections with fixed collection and field ids ([`schema.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/bulkmail/schema.go)).
`LegacyJSMigration()` emits a PocketBase JS migration that creates the same collections, for apps that move onto this
schema before they run this extension.
