# Cache

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Extensions and apps often compute the same thing many times: a rendered page, an answer from another API, a compiled
module. Cache gives them named buckets to keep those results in, as bytes or as the Go values themselves, from one
store in your app's process, with an optional folder on disk for more than fits in memory. Each bucket has its own
budget, and you can change it without touching the code that uses it.

On a multisite host the store is shared by every instance: one memory ceiling and one disk tier for all of them. Each
instance still sees only its own buckets. On disk, identical bytes (the same compiled template, the same `.wasm`
file) are one file however many instances or keys hold them.

Cache provides [cache/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache/v1) and [cache.clear/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1).
Code that caches talks only to those contracts, so a cache shared between servers (Redis, Memcached) can replace this
one later without any of it changing.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Cache is built into `pocketone` and on by default; there's nothing to install. Turn it off with
`cache: {enabled: false}` in `pocketone.yaml`. In your own Go build it comes with the standard set, or on its own:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{cache.New(cache.Config{})}, nil, nil)
```

## Configure

Nothing to configure: each bucket gets 32MiB of memory (and 256MiB of disk, when there's a disk tier), the store
128MiB for every bucket together. To change them, add a `cache` section to `pocketone.yaml`. The top keys are the
store's; `defaults` fill in what a bucket's code leaves unset; `buckets` set a named bucket's limits over what its
code asks for:

```yaml
cache:
  max_memory: 512MiB       # the store: every bucket together
  disk_path: cache         # a disk tier; leave out for memory only
  max_disk: 10GiB
  defaults:
    max_memory: 16MiB
    ttl: 10m
  buckets:
    pages.compiled:
      max_memory: 64MiB    # one app's bucket
      max_disk: 1GiB
```

The store, ceilings over every bucket together:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `max_memory` | Memory for every bucket together (default 128MiB) |
| `eviction` | Which values leave memory (or disk) first when the store reaches a ceiling: `lru` (default), `mru`, `fifo`, `lifo` |
| `disk_path` | Turns on the disk tier there, in a `p1cache` folder. Relative paths are under `pb_data` on a single app, and under the working directory on a multisite host |
| `max_disk` | Size of the disk tier (default 1GiB) |

Each bucket (`defaults` and `buckets.<name>`), its own budget:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `max_items` | Most entries the bucket holds, in memory or on disk |
| `max_memory` | Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds in memory (default 32MiB) |
| `max_disk` | Most bytes of disk files the bucket's keys point at, each counted in full even when shared (default 256MiB) |
| `eviction` | Which of its entries go first when the bucket is full |
| `ttl` | How long an entry lives unless its code says otherwise |

Sizes take `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB` (or `KB`, `MB`, `GB`); durations take `s`, `m`, `h`.

A disk tier inside `pb_data` is part of your backups (as throwaway files). To keep it out, give `disk_path` an
absolute folder outside `pb_data`.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `cache:`

The cache (cache/v1): one store for every app in the process (memory, disk tier), and caps per bucket.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | Turns the cache off when false; extensions then run uncached. |
| `eviction` | string |  | Which values leave memory (or disk) first when the store reaches its ceiling: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. |
| `max_memory` | int |  | Memory for every bucket together, such as 512MiB. Default 128MiB. |
| `disk_path` | string |  | Turns on a disk tier there (in a p1cache folder). Relative: under pb_data on a single app, the working directory on a multisite host. |
| `max_disk` | int |  | Size of the disk tier for every bucket together, such as 10GiB. Default 1GiB. |
| `defaults.eviction` | string |  | Which of the bucket's entries go first when it's full: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. |
| `defaults.max_items` | int |  | Most entries the bucket holds. |
| `defaults.max_memory` | int |  | Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds in memory, such as 32MiB (the default). |
| `defaults.max_disk` | int |  | Most bytes of disk files the bucket's keys point at, each counted in full, such as 256MiB (the default). |
| `defaults.ttl` | int |  | How long an entry lives unless the code says otherwise, such as 10m. |
| `buckets` | map of object |  | Caps per bucket name, over what its code asks for. |

## Use

Nothing to click. A bucket that's full moves its values to the disk tier when there is one, and a read brings them
back. The cache, disk tier included, starts empty with the process. On a multisite host, an instance that restarts or sleeps keeps its entries: the store
belongs to the host.

To empty an app's cache, as a superuser: `pocketone remote cache clear` (every bucket) or
`pocketone remote cache clear --bucket pages.compiled` (one), through [cache.clear/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1).

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### [cache.clear/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [clear](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1#clear) | `pocketone remote cache clear --bucket <value>` | `POST /api/_c/cache.clear/v1` | `cache_clear_clear` |

## Integrations

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Every instance shares the host's one store (its memory, its disk tier), and sees only its own buckets: keys live under the instance's id. An instance that sleeps keeps its entries, so it wakes to a warm cache. An instance's `extensions.cache` may set `enabled`, `defaults` and `buckets` for itself; the store's keys are the host's only. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | Each container runs its own `pocketone`, so it has its own store. |

### Building on Cache

Open a bucket through [cache/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache/v1) at serve time, keep it, and get and set keys:

```go
b, err := cachev1.Open(app, "myext.answers", cachev1.Options{MaxItems: 1000, TTL: 10 * time.Minute})
```

Declare cache/v1 in `WorksWith`: when nothing provides it, `Open` returns a bucket that keeps nothing, so your code
runs uncached. Name buckets after your extension so they never collide.

To cache Go values rather than bytes, make them `cachev1.Item`s and open the bucket with `cachev1.OpenItems`
([Go values](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache/v1#go-values)). Each key keeps its own value in memory, never shared with
another key. A value that is also a `cachev1.Marshaler` is marshaled only when it goes to disk, and comes back decoded
as long as its `CacheVersion` matches the reader's; one that isn't stays in memory only.

Cache provides cache/v1 and cache.clear/v1 as defaults: another extension that provides them (a Redis cache, say)
replaces it without any `providers:` line. On a multisite host, the host empties the whole store (every instance's
buckets) with the extension's `Clear`.

## Example

A PocketBase app with one bucket, `example.slow`. `GET /slow` takes a second the first time and
answers from the cache for the next minute.

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app with cache/v1 and one bucket, "example.slow". GET /slow takes a second the first
// time and answers from the cache for the next minute:
//
//	go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/slow   # slow
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/slow   # cached
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"

	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/cache"
	cachev1 "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/cache/v1"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{cache.New(cache.Config{})}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
		b, err := cachev1.Open(app, "example.slow", cachev1.Options{MaxItems: 100, TTL: time.Minute})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		se.Router.GET("/slow", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
			ctx := e.Request.Context()
			if v, ok, _ := b.Get(ctx, "answer"); ok {
				return e.String(http.StatusOK, "cached: "+string(v)+"\n")
			}
			time.Sleep(time.Second) // the expensive part
			v := time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339)
			_ = b.Set(ctx, "answer", []byte(v), 0)
			return e.String(http.StatusOK, "computed: "+v+"\n")
		})
		return se.Next()
	})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

One store per process. Each app's buckets are namespaces in it, `<instance id>/<bucket>` (just `/<bucket>` on a
single app), so no app can read another's keys.

Memory and disk follow different rules. In memory every key holds its own value, bytes or a Go value, and nothing is
shared between keys. On disk values are files named by the SHA-256 of their bytes (an item's `MarshalCache` bytes):
the same bytes under any number of keys, from any number of instances, are one file with a reference count, removed
when the last key pointing at it goes. A key points at its file with the value's version beside it: (bucket, key,
version) -> SHA.

Each bucket has its own budget: entries, memory (its keys and the values it holds there) and disk (the files its keys
point at, each in full). When a bucket is over its memory, its values move to disk (by its own strategy); over its
entries or its disk, its keys go. A busy bucket never evicts another bucket's values. The store's ceilings (memory,
disk) hold over every bucket together, so the total stays bounded however many instances there are; reaching one
evicts across buckets by the store's strategy.

Memory is the hot tier and the disk tier the cold one: a value reaches disk only when memory evicts it (an item is
marshaled then, never before), goes back to memory and leaves disk when it's read, and the folder is emptied when the
process starts. Nothing on disk outlives the process, so nothing on disk can be stale after a restart or a crash.

One lock guards the in-memory index, and it's never held across disk IO, marshaling or decoding. One IO goroutine, running only
while it has work, marshals, writes and removes files in the order the lock decided them. A write waits in a slot of
its key's, at most one per key, and writes whatever the key holds when its turn comes, so a key evicted again and
again before the disk catches up is marshaled and written once, with its latest value. A value waiting to be written
stays readable from memory (at most a quarter of `max_memory` waits; past that, evicted values are dropped). A file is
read once however many readers want it, and a key's bytes are decoded once however many readers want its item; both
are checked against the index again before they're used, so a key changed meanwhile never gets its old value back.

The store is tested against a model under fuzzing (bytes and items: no value deleted, replaced, expired or belonging to another key ever comes back; no value is shared
between keys in memory; every count and list stays consistent; the disk tier holds exactly the files it should) and
under concurrent load with the race detector.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config

# Config

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

PocketOne's config file: `pocketone.yaml`, with secrets in a `.env` beside it. Put your app's settings in one file
instead of a long line of flags. Each extension has its own section in the file.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Config is built into `pocketone` and always on. Without a `pocketone.yaml`, nothing changes: every setting keeps its
default and the flags work as usual.

In your own Go build, load the file before the app is created, so its values can be the flags' defaults:

```go
cfg, err := config.Load(config.FromArgs(os.Args[1:]))
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
appCfg, _ := config.App.Get()
app := pocketbase.NewWithConfig(pocketbase.Config{DefaultDataDir: cfg.ResolvePath(appCfg.Dir)})
app.RootCmd.AddCommand(config.NewCommand(func() config.Options { return config.FromArgs(os.Args[1:]) }))
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/config`. [`examples/pocketone/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/main.go)
shows the full wiring: every `app` key as a flag default, and the `server` keys as the serve command's defaults.

## Configure

### Where the files are

- `pocketone.yaml` is looked for in the working directory, then next to the executable. `--config <path>` picks
  another file.
- The `.env` is looked for beside the config file (or in the working directory when there is no config file).
  `--env-file <path>` picks another one.
- Relative paths in the file are relative to the file's folder, so it works from any working directory.

### What goes in it

Each top-level key is one section, owned by the extension that uses it. This package owns three:

- `app`: your app, as every command that opens it reads it (`serve`, `migrate`, `superuser`, `pitr`, `token`,
  `oauth`, `template`): `dir`, `dev`, `encryption_env`, `query_timeout`, `jsvm`, `hooks_dir`, `hooks_pool`,
  `migrations_dir`, the defaults of those commands' flags of the same name, plus `env_allow`.
- `server`: what `serve` reads. `http`, `https` and `origins` are the defaults for `serve --http`, `--https` and
  `--origins`; for a single app, `public_dir`, `index_fallback`, `pages_dir`, `hooks_watch` and `automigrate` are the
  defaults for `--publicDir`, `--indexFallback`, `--pagesDir`, `--hooksWatch` and `--automigrate`.
- `multisite`: add it only to run many instances from one binary (see [Integrations](#integrations)); `providers:
  { runtime/v1: [...] }` picks which runtimes.

```yaml
server:
  http: 127.0.0.1:8090
  origins: ["*"]
  public_dir: ./pb_public
app:
  dir: ./pb_data
  hooks_dir: ./pb_hooks
  env_allow: [STRIPE_KEY]
  js_limits:          # the JS engine's limits for the app
    memory: 128MiB
    task_time: 10s
pitr:
  retention: 168h
```

Other extensions' sections (such as `pitr` above) are described on their own pages. `pocketone config` lists every
section your binary knows.

### Flags win

A flag on the command line always wins over the file. The file only changes the defaults.

### Secrets in the .env

Write `$VAR` or `${VAR}` in any value, and keep the secret in the `.env`:

```yaml
autotls:
  dns:
    api_token: $CF_API_TOKEN
```

```bash
# .env
CF_API_TOKEN=abc123
```

- A name is looked up in the `.env` first, then in the process environment. `$$` is a literal `$`.
- A name that is set nowhere stops the app at startup, with the missing names listed.
- The `.env` takes `KEY=VALUE` lines. Blank lines, `# comments` and an `export ` prefix are fine. Quote a value to keep
  its spaces; double quotes also understand `\n`, `\t`, `\"` and `\\`.
- The `.env` is used only for these references. It is never put in the process environment, so your JS hooks
  (`$os.getenv`) don't see it, unless you list a name in `app.env_allow`.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `app:`

The single app, for every command that opens it: data dir, dev mode, encryption, JS engine, hooks, migrations, and the .env names it may read (env_allow). Not used on a multisite host.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | string |  | The data folder (pb_data). Default: pb_data next to the executable. The --dir flag wins. |
| `dev` | bool |  | Dev mode: logs and SQL statements printed to the console. The --dev flag wins. |
| `encryption_env` | string |  | Name of the environment variable holding a 32-character key that encrypts the app settings. The --encryptionEnv flag wins. |
| `query_timeout` | duration |  | Default timeout for SELECT queries, such as 30s. The --queryTimeout flag wins. |
| `hooks_dir` | string |  | The JS hooks folder. Default: pb_hooks next to pb_data. The --hooksDir flag wins. |
| `jsvm` | string |  | The JS engine for pb_hooks and pb_migrations: quickjs (PocketOne's, the default) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility: pages, $mcp, $tokens and JS contracts are off). The --jsvm flag wins. |
| `hooks_pool` | int |  | Only with jsvm: goja: how many JS runtimes are kept ready for hooks. Default 15. The --hooksPool flag wins. |
| `migrations_dir` | string |  | The migrations folder. Default: pb_migrations next to pb_data. The --migrationsDir flag wins. |
| `env_allow` | list of string |  | Names from the .env the app and its JS hooks may read. Default none. |
| `js_limits.memory` | int |  | The app's JS memory: the JS heap plus the Go objects JS holds, such as 128MiB. Default 64MiB. |
| `js_limits.task_time` | duration |  | JS time one task (a request, a hook, a cron job) may use, Go calls and waits not counted, such as 10s. Default 5s. |
| `js_limits.task_wall` | duration |  | Wall time one task may take, Go calls included, such as 60s. Default 30s. |

#### `server:`

The serve command: http, https and CORS origins, and for a single app its static files, pages, hooks watching and automigrate.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http` | string |  | Plain HTTP address, such as 127.0.0.1:8090. Single app: the --http default (the flag wins). Many instances: redirects to https when https is set. |
| `https` | string |  | HTTPS address. Single app: the --https default (the flag wins). Many instances: the main address. |
| `origins` | list of string |  | Allowed CORS origins. Single app: the --origins default (the flag wins). |
| `plain` | list of string |  | Many instances only: extra plain HTTP addresses with no redirect. |
| `tls.cert` | string |  | Many instances only: the certificate file, reloaded when it changes. |
| `tls.key` | string |  | Many instances only: the private key file, reloaded when it changes. |
| `shutdown_timeout` | duration |  | Many instances only: how long in-flight requests get to finish at stop. |
| `public_dir` | string |  | Single app only: the static files folder. Default: pb_public next to the executable. The --publicDir flag wins. |
| `index_fallback` | bool |  | Single app only: serve index.html for a missing static path, for single-page apps. On unless false. The --indexFallback flag wins. |
| `pages_dir` | string |  | Single app only: the PocketPages folder, served when it exists. Default: pb_pages next to pb_data. The --pagesDir flag wins. |
| `hooks_watch` | bool |  | Single app only: restart the app when a pb_hooks file changes. On unless false. The --hooksWatch flag wins. |
| `automigrate` | bool |  | Single app only: write a migration file when you change collections in the dashboard. On unless false. The --automigrate flag wins. |

## Use

### See every section

```bash
pocketone config
```

It prints each section with its description and defaults, as YAML you can copy into your file. For the same list as
JSON (each section's name, description, owning extension, and each key with its type and default):

```bash
pocketone config --json
```

### Check your file

```bash
pocketone config check
```

It reads the file and the `.env` and reports problems, or a line like:

```
/srv/app/pocketone.yaml: ok (3 sections), secrets from /srv/app/.env
```

With no file it says `no config file: defaults only`.

### What stops startup

The app won't start, and says why, when the file has:

- a top-level key no extension in the binary owns (usually a typo); the error lists the sections it knows;
- the same section twice;
- a value that doesn't fit its key (for example text where a number goes);
- a `$VAR` that is set in neither the `.env` nor the environment.

An empty section (`pitr:` with nothing after it) is allowed and means all defaults.

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone config`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-config) | Lists the pocketone.yaml sections this binary understands, with their defaults |
| [`pocketone config check`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-config-check) | Checks the config file: every section known and valid, every $VAR set |

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| Every extension with a section | Each extension declares its own section; its values become that extension's defaults or flag defaults. [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr), [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect) and [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls) are examples. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) and [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | Add a `multisite` section and `pocketone serve` runs many instances instead of one app, on the runtimes `providers: { runtime/v1: [...] }` picks (default: every configured one). The `app` section and `env_allow` don't apply then; each instance has its own folder under its runtime's root. |

### The server section with many instances

On a multisite host, `server` has a few more keys: `https` is the main address, `http` then redirects plain HTTP to it
(`http` alone serves plain HTTP), `plain` lists extra plain-HTTP addresses with no redirect, `tls` names a certificate
and key file (reloaded when they change), and `shutdown_timeout` limits how long in-flight requests get at stop.

```yaml
multisite: {}
server:
  https: ":443"
  http: ":80"
  plain: [":8080"]
  tls: { cert: /etc/certs/cert.pem, key: /etc/certs/key.pem }
```

### Give your extension a section

Declare it in your own package with a typed key and defaults:

```go
type Config struct {
	Limit int `yaml:"limit" doc:"Requests per minute. The --limit flag wins."`
}

var Section = extkit.NewSection("firewall", Config{Limit: 60}, "Request limits for the app.")

cfg, found := firewall.Section.Get()   // the defaults with the file's values applied
cfg, err := firewall.Section.Require() // fails when the file doesn't have the section
```

- An extension reads a section only through its owner's key, so it can read only sections from packages it imports.
  There is no lookup by name and no access to the raw file.
- The `doc:"…"` tag on each field describes the key in `pocketone config --json` and in the key table on
  pocketone.dev.
- `config.Load` checks every section when the app starts, so a bad value fails early.

## Example

Config is built into `pocketone`: [`examples/pocketone/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/main.go) loads `pocketone.yaml` with it before the app starts and adds the `config` command.

## Go API

- `config.FromArgs(args)` reads `--config` and `--env-file` before the full flag parse.
- `config.Load(opts)` finds, reads and checks the files, and makes them the source for every section.
  `config.Read(opts)` does the same without checking or installing them.
- `(*Config).ResolvePath(p)` makes a relative path from the file absolute, relative to the file's folder.
- `(*Config).AllowEnv(names)` copies those `.env` values into the process environment (what `app.env_allow` does).
- `config.Describe()` returns every section with its keys, types, defaults and docs (the data behind `--json`).
- `config.NewCommand(opts)` is the `config` command.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy

# Deploy

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Send your project's code to a running app from your own machine: `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations`, `pb_pages`,
`pb_public`, packages and the production `node_modules` tree. Only changed files are uploaded and the app swaps them
in; `restart` applies new migrations and packages. `pocketone dev` keeps your folder and the app in step both ways and
streams the app's logs; `pull` and `logs` work the other way.

```bash
pocketone link https://myapp.example.com   # add the remote and sign in (Remotes)
pocketone deploy                           # upload what changed
pocketone logs
```

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Deploy is built into `pocketone` and **on** in both directions: every app it serves accepts deploys from its
superusers, and the `deploy`, `dev`, `pull`, `logs` and `restart` commands are there to deploy to other apps. There's
nothing to install.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts. [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) gives the commands their
remotes and logins, and [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) lets you deploy with API tokens:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{
	tokens.New(tokens.Config{}),   // optional: API tokens with the deploy scope
	remotes.New(remotes.Config{}), // remote/v1 (whoami, restart, logs), login
	deploy.NewExtension(deploy.Config{}), // deploy/v1 + deploy/dev/pull/logs/restart commands
}, nil, nil)
app.Start()
```

The [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard) does this for you.

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy`. `deploy.Config{DisableServer: true}` keeps only the
commands, for a binary that deploys elsewhere but must not accept deploys.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or settings screen. Defaults on the receiving app:

- **Who may deploy:** superusers. You sign in with `pocketone login` (see [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes)) or use an
  API token. A token needs the `deploy` scope (or no scopes); `deploy:read` allows reading files and logs only.
- **Where files land:** next to `pb_data`, PocketBase's usual layout (`pb_hooks/`, `pb_migrations/`,
  `pb_public/`, `node_modules/` beside it).
- **Upload store:** uploaded files and past deploys are kept in `.pb_deploy/` next to `pb_data`. It's outside
  `pb_data`, so backups skip it, and it's never deployed.

On your machine, the commands use the project's remotes and saved logins from [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes). In CI,
set `P1_TOKEN` (or `P1_TOKEN_<REMOTE>`) instead of signing in.

## Use

All commands take an optional remote name or URL; without one they use the project's default remote. Run them from
your project folder (or any folder below it).

### `deploy`

```bash
pocketone deploy                      # to the default remote
pocketone deploy prod -m "fix signup" # to the remote "prod", with a note
pocketone deploy --restart            # and restart if migrations or packages changed (CI)
pocketone deploy --dry-run            # list what would be sent, send nothing
pocketone deploy --out /tmp/set       # write the files to a folder instead
```

You'll see how many files are deployed and how many are uploaded, then a line like
`Deployed <id>: 3 changed, 0 deleted, 41 unchanged.` With nothing changed it says `Up to date: no changes.`

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--restart` | Restart the app after the files are in, when migrations or packages changed. |
| `--dry-run` | List what would be deployed; deploy nothing. |
| `--out <dir>` | Write the deploy set to a local folder instead of deploying. |
| `-i`, `--include` | Add include patterns to the default set. |
| `-e`, `--exclude` | Exclude patterns (`pb_data` is always excluded). |
| `--node-modules` | Ship the production `node_modules` tree (the default when there's a `package.json`). |
| `--no-node-modules` | Don't ship `node_modules`; leave the remote's alone. |
| `--commit <sha>` | Commit to record. Default: `$GITHUB_SHA`, `$CI_COMMIT_SHA`, or git `HEAD`. |
| `-m`, `--message` | A note to record with the deploy. |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | List every file. |

**What's sent:** files matching `pb_*` and `pb_*/**/*` except `pb_data`, plus `package.json`, `bun.lock(b)` and
`patches/**`. Dotfiles are included (`pb_public/.well-known`); `.git*` files and symlinks are skipped.

**Packages:** with a `package.json`, the production `node_modules` tree is collected the way Node resolves it (hoisted
npm and bun, pnpm's store, workspace links; never devDependencies) and shipped as plain files, so plain JS hooks can
`require` npm packages. The remote then owns its root `node_modules`: packages you no longer ship are removed there.

**Restarts:** files are swapped in while the app runs, each rename atomic, and deploy never restarts the app on its
own. `pb_pages` and `pb_public` are read from disk on each request, and hooks reload by themselves (PocketBase's
`--hooksWatch`, Pocker's watcher). Migrations and packages apply only when the app starts, so a deploy that changes
them says `Migrations or packages changed` and leaves the restart to you: pass `--restart` (the app restarts once,
after the whole batch is in, and you hear if it fails to start), run `pocketone restart`, or type `r` in `dev`. So
does the first deploy that creates `pb_hooks`, since a watcher only sees folders that existed when the app started.

### `restart`

```bash
pocketone restart prod
```

Restarts the app so it applies new migrations and packages, and tells you if it fails to start. An app that isn't
running (a sleeping Pocker instance) is left alone; it applies them when it starts.

### `dev`

```bash
pocketone dev
pocketone dev prod --prefer local   # first sync: upload yours where both sides differ
```

Keeps the project folder and the remote in step, both ways, and streams the remote's logs. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

| What | Direction |
|---|---|
| `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations`, `pb_pages`, `pb_public` and other `pb_*` folders | both ways |
| `package.json`, `bun.lock(b)`, `patches/` | both ways |
| `node_modules` | uploaded only, when `package.json` or the lockfile changes |
| `pb_data` | never (it's the app's live data) |

- **Your edits** go up half a second after you save.
- **Changes on the remote**, such as the migrations the dashboard writes when you edit a collection, come down within
  a few seconds (`--poll`, default 5s). `dev` asks the remote for one hash and only looks further when it changed, so
  a large `pb_public` costs nothing while it's quiet.
- **Restarts:** `dev` never restarts the app by itself. Hooks reload by themselves, pages and public files are live on
  the next request. After you upload a migration or new packages, `dev` says so: type `r` and Enter to restart the app
  and apply them. Migrations that come down are already applied on the remote.
- **Deletes** go both ways too.
- **Changed on both sides:** your copy wins and is uploaded; the remote's is saved in `.pocketone/conflicts/` and
  `dev` says so.
- **First run:** files that exist on only one side are copied to the other. If a file differs on both sides, `dev`
  lists them and asks whether to keep yours or take the remote's; `--prefer local|remote` answers in advance.

`dev` keeps what it last synced in `.pocketone/sync.json` (add `.pocketone/` to `.gitignore`). List files to leave
out, such as ones your hooks generate, in `.pocketoneignore`, one gitignore-style pattern per line.

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--prefer local\|remote` | First sync: who wins where both sides differ (default: ask). |
| `--poll <duration>` | How often to check the remote (default 5s). |
| `--push-only` | Only upload, the way `dev` used to work. Also used by itself for remotes without two-way sync. |
| `--no-logs` | Don't stream the remote's logs. |

It takes the same file flags as `deploy`.

### `pull`

```bash
pocketone pull prod                              # pb_hooks, pb_migrations, pb_pages, pb_public, pb_templates, package.json
pocketone pull prod pb_hooks pb_public/index.html
pocketone pull prod --dry-run
```

Downloads files from a remote into the project. `pb_data` is only reachable on an instance that's powered off, so a
single app (always running while it answers) refuses it.

### `logs`

```bash
pocketone logs prod
pocketone logs prod -n 20
```

Replays the last 100 lines (`-n`, `--lines`, 0 to 1000), then follows. Requests show as `GET /url → 200 (1.2 ms)` and
errors are marked `ERR`. PocketBase writes its logs in batches, so lines show up a few seconds late. The stream
reconnects by itself if it drops.

### Deploy history

Every deploy is recorded in the `_deploys` collection of the receiving app: status, file counts, bytes, commit,
message, source, token name, superuser and any error. Superusers can browse it in the dashboard.

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone deploy [remote]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-deploy) | Deploys pb\_hooks, pb\_migrations, pb\_pages, pb\_public and packages to a remote |
| [`pocketone dev [remote]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-dev) | Keeps the project's code and a remote in step both ways (and streams the remote's logs) |
| [`pocketone logs [remote]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-logs) | Streams a remote's app logs |
| [`pocketone pull [remote] [paths...]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-pull) | Downloads files from a remote into the project (default: pb\_hooks, pb\_migrations, pb\_pages, pb\_public, pb\_templates, package.json) |
| [`pocketone restart [remote]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-restart) | Restarts a remote's app so it applies new migrations and packages |

### [deploy/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/deploy/v1)

Its HTTP API under `/api/_c/deploy/v1/`, as the contract describes.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | Gives the commands their remotes, saved logins and CI tokens. The commands find deploy/v1 in the remote's whoami, and `restart` and `logs` use its remote/v1 (deploy requires it). |
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | `pocketone login` signs in through the browser when the remote runs it. |
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | Deploy registers the `deploy` and `deploy:read` scopes, so you can make API tokens for CI that can only deploy or only read. Add `remote` for `--restart` and `remote:read` for `dev`'s logs. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | The same API runs for many instances with your own backend: build it with `deploy.New` (below). PocketHost does this. |

### Building on Deploy

- **Go client.** `deploy.NewClient(ctx, rc)` takes a remote/v1 client (`remoteclient.Open`, from
  [ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient)) and finds its deploy API.
  `Deploy`, `Pull`, `Collect`, `Watch` and `NewSyncer` (two-way sync: `Sync`, `RemoteChanged`) are the commands'
  building blocks.
- **Your own host.** `deploy.New(deploy.Options{Prefix, Backend, Instances, PBRoot, DataRoot, PlatformPaths})`
  builds the API; mount `api.Wrap(next)`. `Backend` decides which instance a request is for (`Lookup(r)`), who it
  acts as (`Authenticate(r, inst)` → `Auth{UserID, Scopes, Via, TokenLabel}`, an `*AuthError`, or `ErrNoAccess` for a
  404) and records history. `Instances` is pocker's Manager (stop, swap, start). Serve it as deploy/v1 for the host's
  instances (`deployv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances`, `extkit.HostRoutes` in `multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes`); restart and logs are the host's remote/v1.
- **Restarts.** Your `Instances` should reload an instance by itself when its `pb_hooks` change (pocker's Manager
  does); deploy only restarts through it when a client asks (`Client.Restart`, or `DeployOptions.Restart`).
- **Discovery.** Deploy provides the [deploy/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/deploy/v1/deploy.go) contract, which whoami lists, so
  clients find it at `/api/_c/deploy/v1`. A multisite host can provide it for its instances instead.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/deploy/example/main.go) is an app that both accepts deploys and makes them: the deploy API, API tokens, remotes and the deploy commands. Its comment walks through a first deploy against itself.

```go
// Command example is a PocketOne app that accepts deploys and can deploy: deploy/v1 (/api/_c/deploy/v1), remote/v1
// (restart, logs), API tokens, and the deploy/dev/pull/logs/restart commands.
//
//	go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090                  # the remote
//	cd myproject && mkdir pb_hooks && echo 'routerAdd("GET", "/hi", (e) => e.string(200, "hi"))' > pb_hooks/main.pb.js
//	go run ./example link http://127.0.0.1:8090 --email admin@example.com   # password: password
//	go run ./example deploy
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/hi
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	// registered through their contracts (the standard set does this for you); deploys land next to pb_data
	exts := []extkit.Extension{tokens.New(tokens.Config{}), remotes.New(remotes.Config{}), deploy.NewExtension(deploy.Config{})}
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, exts, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // deployed pb_hooks and pb_migrations

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Deploy API

deploy/v1, at `/api/_c/deploy/v1` (superusers, see Configure): the files only, on an app or a host. Whoami, restart
and logs are remote/v1's (`/api/_c/remote/v1`), which deploy requires.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /check` | Takes a manifest, returns the hashes the server is missing. |
| `POST /blobs` | Gzipped `PHB1` bundles: `[sha256][uint32 length][bytes]`…, every hash verified, 64 MB per request. |
| `POST /commit` | Stage, swap in, record. `"restartNeeded": true` in the answer when migrations or packages wait for a restart; `"restart": true` in the request restarts after the swap. With `"partial": true` only the listed files (and `"delete"`) change. |
| `GET`/`DELETE /files` | List or delete files. |
| `GET`/`PUT /files/raw` | Download or upload one file. |
| `GET /tree` | One folder of the code set (`?path=`, default the root) with a hash over everything below it; `hashOnly=1` for just the hash. |

The protocol is the pockethost npm CLI's, so the same client deploys to PocketOne apps and PocketHost.

## How it works

- Go module `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy`. [`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/deploy/example/main.go) is an app that accepts
  deploys and can deploy (logins from [devusers](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go): admin@example.com / password).
- A deploy is a hash diff: the client sends a manifest, uploads only the missing files in bundles, then commits.
- On a single app the files are swapped in while it runs; a restart (when a client asks) is `app.Restart()`, which
  re-executes the process (`Config.Restart` overrides it; not on Windows).
- `Config.Dir` and `Config.StoreDir` move the deploy folder and the upload store; `Config.Prefix` moves the API.
- Logs on a single app come from its own `_logs` table; entries at error level and above are marked as stderr.
- The `node_modules` collector is [`nodemodules`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/deploy/nodemodules/nodemodules.go), a port of the npm CLI's.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm

# JSVM

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

PocketOne's JS engine for `pb_hooks` and `pb_migrations`. It runs the same JS API as PocketBase (`$app`, `onX`,
`routerAdd`, `cronAdd`, `$http`, `$security`, ...) on QuickJS, with one VM per app:

- **Real globals.** Every hook file runs in the app's one global scope, so top-level helpers, constants and state are
  visible to every handler. No more `require()` inside each handler.
- **ES modules.** `*.pb.mjs` (and TypeScript `*.pb.ts`/`*.pb.mts`) hook files and modules use `import`/`export`,
  including top-level `await`; `*.pb.js` and `*.pb.cjs` stay scripts with `require()`. Both share the same module
  instances.
- **TypeScript.** `.ts`, `.mts` and `.cts` hooks, migrations and modules run directly (types stripped by esbuild,
  linked into the binary), with error positions in your `.ts` source.
- **Async.** Handlers can be `async`. Every Go function has an `.async(...)` twin that runs off the VM and returns a
  promise, so one app serves other requests while it waits: `await $app.findRecordById.async("posts", id)`.
- **Hard limits per app.** A memory cap (JS heap plus Go objects JS holds), a CPU and a wall-clock budget per task, and
  caps on queued tasks and async calls. A runaway script stops with an error; other apps in the process keep running.
- **Real error positions.** Stack traces name `pb_hooks/<file>:<line>`.

The `pocketone` binary and every Pocker instance run on it. PocketBase's own `plugins/jsvm` (goja) is for pure
PocketBase compatibility only: `jsvm: goja` under `app:` in `pocketone.yaml` (or `--jsvm goja`) runs a single app on it,
with pages, `$mcp`, `$tokens`, `$bulkmail` and JS contracts off.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The engine is pure Go (QuickJS translated to Go by [modernc.org/libquickjs](https://pkg.go.dev/modernc.org/libquickjs),
the way PocketBase uses modernc.org/sqlite), so it needs no cgo: `CGO_ENABLED=0` builds and cross-compiles work as with
stock PocketBase. In your own Go build, register it where you'd register `plugins/jsvm`:

```go
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks", MigrationsDir: "pb_migrations"})
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm`.

## Configure

`Config` takes PocketBase's jsvm fields (`HooksDir`, `HooksWatch`, `HooksFilesPattern`, `MigrationsDir`,
`MigrationsFilesPattern`, `TypesDir`; `HooksPoolSize` is accepted and ignored) plus:

- `OnInit func(rt js.Runtime)`: add globals after everything else is set up.
- `VM`: the limits. `MemoryLimit` (default 64 MiB), `TaskBudget` (JS time per task, default 5 s), `TaskWall` (wall time
  per task, Go calls included, default 30 s), `QueueSize`, `MaxAsync`, `MaxPumpDepth`.
  Array methods that walk every index (`join`, `indexOf`, `slice`, `forEach`, `concat`, `flat`, ...) and arrays passed
  to Go throw a `RangeError` past `MemoryLimit / 16` elements: QuickJS doesn't check `TaskBudget` inside those loops,
  and a sparse array (`new Array(1e9)`) or array-like costs no memory, so the cap is what stops them. No dense array
  that long fits in `MemoryLimit`.
- `Extensions`: values that extend it (below).

## Use

Write hooks and migrations as in PocketBase's [JS docs](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-overview/); they run unchanged.
What's new:

```js
// pb_hooks/main.pb.js
const cache = new Map()

routerAdd("GET", "/post/{slug}", async (e) => {
	const slug = e.request.pathValue("slug")
	if (!cache.has(slug)) {
		cache.set(slug, await e.app.findFirstRecordByData.async("posts", "slug", slug))
	}
	return e.json(200, cache.get(slug))
})
```

- Hook files run before the app opens its database, as in PocketBase, so a `$app` query at a file's top level fails.
  Read data in `onBootstrap` after `e.next()`, or in a handler:

  ```js
  let users = null
  onBootstrap((e) => {
  	e.next()
  	users = e.app.findCollectionByNameOrId("users")
  })
  ```
- Globals live as long as the app's VM. A restart, a hooks reload or running out of memory starts a fresh one, so keep
  durable data in the database.
- After an `await`, other requests may have run: use `e.app`, not the global `$app`, and keep transactions short across
  `await`s (they hold SQLite's write lock).
- Calls that wait on I/O (`$app` methods, DB queries, `$http.send`, `sleep`) let the app's other requests run even
  without `.async`.
- `process.env` and a small `Buffer` (`from`, `toString` with utf8, base64, hex) are there.

### Modules: import and require

Name a file for what it is: `.mjs` is an ES module, `.cjs` is CommonJS. A plain `.js` file is CommonJS, so existing
PocketBase hooks run unchanged (inside `node_modules`, Node's rule applies: `"type": "module"` in the package's
`package.json` makes its `.js` files ES modules). TypeScript is written as ES modules, so `.ts` and `.mts` are ES
modules and `.cts` is the CommonJS exception.

| File | Runs as | Shares through |
|---|---|---|
| `pb_hooks/*.pb.mjs`, `*.pb.ts`, `*.pb.mts` | ES module: `import`, `export`, top-level `await`, `import.meta` | `export` / `import`; its top-level names are private |
| `pb_hooks/*.pb.js`, `*.pb.cjs`, `*.pb.cts` | script in the app's one global scope, with `require()` | globals |
| `pb_migrations/*.mjs`, `*.ts`, `*.mts` | ES module | each migration has its own scope either way |
| `pb_migrations/*.js`, `*.cjs`, `*.cts` | script in its own function scope | |

All of them run in the app's one VM: scripts and modules share the global object (a module can read a script's
globals) and one instance of every module.

```js
// pb_hooks/lib/store.mjs
export const state = { hits: 0 }
export const bump = () => ++state.hits

// pb_hooks/main.pb.mjs
import { bump } from "./lib/store.mjs"
import legacy from "./lib/legacy.cjs"      // CommonJS: module.exports is the default export
import { hello } from "some-package"       // node_modules, CommonJS or ES
const { greeting } = await import("./lib/greeting.mjs")      // top-level await: done before the app serves

routerAdd("GET", "/hit", (e) => e.json(200, { hits: bump() }))
```

- `import` and `require()` resolve the same way: relative paths (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.json` and `index.*`
  tried in turn), then `node_modules` packages by `package.json` `exports` (the `import` or `require` condition) or
  `main`.
- A module loads once per app, however many files import or require it, so its state is shared by every request.
  Importing a CommonJS module gives its `module.exports` as the default export, its keys as named exports, and the same
  instance `require()` returns.
- `require()` of an ES module returns its namespace (the same instance `import` gives), as in Node 22, as long as the
  module has no top-level `await`; for one that does, use `await import("./lib/x.mjs")`.

### TypeScript

`.ts`, `.mts` and `.cts` files run as they are: esbuild strips the types when the file loads, and each file's source
map is kept, so an error names `pb_hooks/main.pb.mts:12:5` in your source, not in the stripped code.

- There's no type checking at runtime. Check with `tsc --noEmit` or your editor; `pb_data/types.d.ts` types the
  whole JS API.
- Imports may name the compiled file, as TypeScript's `NodeNext` style does: `import { add } from "./math.js"` loads
  `math.ts` when there's no `math.js`.
- `import type` and other type-only imports disappear, so a `*.pb.cts` script can use them and stay a script.
- A `.cts` module may still be written with `import`/`export`; it's turned into CommonJS.

### Types

When the app starts, `pb_data/types.d.ts` gets the declarations of the whole JS API, for your editor and `tsc`:

- PocketBase's API generated from PocketOne's core (its extra hooks included), by PocketBase's own generator.
- What this engine adds ([`pocketone.d.ts`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/jsvm/pocketone.d.ts)): `.async` on every Go function, fully typed
  (`await $app.findRecordById.async(...)` is a `Promise<core.Record>`), `require`, `process`, `Buffer`, `console`,
  `import.meta`.
- Each extension's own API, for the extensions on in that app (`$mcp`, `$tokens`, `$bulkmail`, `onContracts` and
  the contracts' action hooks).

To type-check, point a `tsconfig.json` at it:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2022", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "Bundler", "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "strict": true, "noEmit": true, "allowImportingTsExtensions": true, "skipLibCheck": true },
  "include": ["pb_data/types.d.ts", "pb_hooks/**/*", "pb_migrations/**/*"]
}
```

`skipLibCheck` skips two type errors inside PocketBase's own generated declarations. In a PocketOne checkout,
`go generate` in `ext/jsvm` regenerates the declarations after a core change (the `TestTypes` tests fail until you
do).

## Integrations

Extensions plug in through `Config.Extensions` with the engine-neutral types in
[`ext/extkit/js`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/extkit/js/js.go). A value implements any of:

- `OnInit(rt)`: set up the VM. `BindJS(app, rt)`: expose a Go API. `TypeScript()`: declare it for editors and
  `tsc` (appended to `pb_data/types.d.ts`).
- `OnCall(rt)`: wrap every handler call; an error refuses it.
- `HTTPClient(rt)`: the client `$http.send` uses.
- `HookFiles`, `MigrationFiles`, `Modules`: hooks, migrations and `require()` modules from somewhere other than disk.
- `OnLoad(rt, root, file, content)`: wrap loading each hook file.

`js.Run(app, fn)` runs Go code on the app's VM; a `js.Func` kept from JS can be called from any goroutine.

[Bundle](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bundle) uses these to serve hooks and migrations embedded in the binary.

## Example

```go
// Command example serves example/pb_hooks with the jsvm extension: one QuickJS VM for the app, so the hook file's
// top-level helpers and state are visible to every handler.
//
//	cd example && go run . serve
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/hello/world
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app)
	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks", MigrationsDir: "pb_migrations"})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Each app's VM is owned by one goroutine, its loop; everything that touches the VM runs there. Go code
  elsewhere posts tasks and waits. A Go call made from JS that fires a hook runs it inline, so Go → JS → Go → JS works.
- Go values cross live through two QuickJS classes: `GoObject` (property get/set/has/keys go to Go by reflection, with
  PocketBase's JS names) and `GoFunc` (calls go to Go). Each holds a handle into the VM's table; QuickJS's refcounting
  frees it as soon as JS drops it.
- Memory: QuickJS caps its own heap. Go objects JS holds are charged to the same budget: a per-type estimate, and a
  reachability walk for fresh results of Go calls.
- QuickJS is [modernc.org/libquickjs](https://pkg.go.dev/modernc.org/libquickjs), Bellard's QuickJS translated to Go,
  so there is no cgo. It runs about as fast as goja; deep recursion stops at `VM.StackSize` (QuickJS stack slots,
  about one per call; default 5000) with "InternalError: stack overflow".
- Benchmarks and the red team (27 attacks against 50 VMs in one process) are in the package's tests
  (`ASYNCVM_BENCH=1`, `ASYNCVM_REDTEAM=1`).

## License

MIT

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp

# MCP

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint at `/mcp`, so an agent (Claude Code, a Claude
connector, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with your app. No sidecar process.

- **Every tool is one REST call, run as the caller.** A tool call becomes a request to your app's own API, made
  in-process as whoever signed in. API rules, request hooks, middleware and rate limits apply because it *is* the REST
  request. MCP makes no permission decisions of its own.
- **The whole stock API is built in** as `pb_*` tools (records, files, auth, collections, settings, logs, crons, SQL,
  backups). An app that only uses the stock API needs nothing else.
- **Your own endpoints get tools the same way:** write the REST endpoint, then the tool wrapper (`$mcp.addEndpoint`
  in `pb_hooks`, or `AddEndpoint` from Go).
- **Every contract the app provides is there too.** Its operations are tools (`restore_points`,
  `bulkmail_start`, `remote_status`, ...), with input schemas from the contract's types, called through the contract
  so its superuser check, scopes and hooks apply. MCP provides the [mcp/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mcp/v1) contract:
  another MCP server can replace this one, and serves the same contract tools.
- **Sign-in with OAuth** through [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth): add `https://<host>/mcp` to Claude and sign
  in in a browser, as a superuser or an app user. The connection stays signed in until you revoke it.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

MCP is built into `pocketone` and always on, with [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) and
[the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) for sign-in and `$mcp` in `pb_hooks`. There's nothing to install or turn on.

MCP is a member of the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard), so every PocketOne app has it: the stock binary, every
[Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) instance, and your own Go build made with `standard.New()`. The set also registers
Tokens (with its OAuth server) for sign-in and binds `$mcp` in `pb_hooks`:

```go
set := standard.New()
app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks"})
app.Start()
```

Tools that `pb_hooks` declare before MCP registers wait for it. The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mcp`.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag, environment variable or settings screen for MCP. In `pocketone` it serves
`/mcp` with every built-in tool, and:
- anyone who can sign in through [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) can connect: superusers and app users of
  any auth collection, each with their own rights;
- an agent's connection doesn't expire; it lasts until you revoke it;
- the server's name for clients comes from **Settings → Application → Application name**.

A Go build can change the path, the tools, the caps and the sign-in (see [Go config](#go-config)).

### Scopes

MCP registers no scopes of its own. When an agent connects, the consent page offers **Full access** (the account's
rights, like a PocketBase auth token) or **Only these**, with a box for each of your
[token scopes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens#your-own-scopes) (scopes that only reach contract APIs under `/api/_c/`, like `deploy`, aren't
offered unless the client asks for them). The protected resource metadata lists the same scopes in
`scopes_supported`, so a client can ask for some up front; the user can still change the ticks.

A connection limited to scopes is held to them exactly like an API token with those scopes on the REST API:

- Each tool call is checked against the scopes' paths and methods (or `Match` guards). A request they don't cover is
  refused with `403`, and the tool returns that as an error.
- Collection rules see only those scopes in `@request.headers.x_token_scope_<name>`.
- `tools/list` hides tools none of the scopes reaches, and the instructions name the scopes.

The token itself still works only on `/mcp`. To limit an agent further, sign it in as an account with fewer rights.

### Behind a proxy

The OAuth resource URL must match the URL clients use. MCP builds it from the request's host, taking the scheme from
**Settings → Application URL** when its host is the same, else from TLS or `X-Forwarded-Proto`. If your proxy rewrites
the host, set `Config.PublicURL` in a Go build.

### Browsers

Requests with an `Origin` header from another site get `403`. Clients that send no `Origin`, such as Claude's servers
and Claude Code, pass. A Go build can allow more origins with `Config.AllowedOrigins`.

## Use

### Connect Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http my-app https://<host>/mcp
claude mcp login my-app        # or /mcp in a session
```

A browser opens on your app's sign-in page. Sign in (as an app user, or with **Sign in as a superuser**), check what
the consent page says and click **Allow**. Claude and Claude Code can connect without registering, through their
published client metadata documents.

For a Claude connector, add `https://<host>/mcp` as a custom connector and sign in the same way. Other MCP clients
register themselves with your app first.

### Paste a token instead

A PocketBase auth token, or an API token not bound to any resource, works on `/mcp` as it does on the REST API, and
tool calls forward it unchanged. A scoped API token works only if one of its scopes covers `/mcp`; to limit an agent
to scopes, connect it through the consent page instead (see [Scopes](#scopes)).

### Who a tool call runs as

Whoever signed in. A superuser gets what the API gives superusers; an app user gets what your collection rules give
them. Superuser-only tools are left out of other callers' tool list (that's presentation; the endpoint still
decides).

### See and revoke connected agents

Each sign-in creates an API token bound to `/mcp`, named "<client> (OAuth)". They're listed under
**Settings → API tokens** with an `oauth: <client id>` label; click **Revoke** to disconnect an agent.

### Built-in tools

One per stock endpoint:

| Group | Tools | Who |
|---|---|---|
| `health` | `pb_check_health` | everyone |
| `records` | `pb_list_records` (`perPage` 20 by default), `pb_get_record`, `pb_create_record`, `pb_update_record`, `pb_delete_record`, `pb_run_batch` | per collection rules |
| `auth` | `pb_list_auth_methods`, `pb_request_otp`, `pb_request_verification`, `pb_confirm_verification`, `pb_request_password_reset`, `pb_confirm_password_reset`, `pb_request_email_change`, `pb_confirm_email_change` | per collection |
| `files` | `pb_download_file` (protected files through a file token made as the caller; images as images, text as text, others as embedded data; up to 10 MB) | per view rules |
| `collections` | `pb_list_collections`, `pb_get_collection`, `pb_create_collection`, `pb_update_collection`, `pb_delete_collection`, `pb_truncate_collection`, `pb_import_collections`, `pb_get_collection_scaffolds`, `pb_list_oauth2_providers`, `pb_dry_run_view` | superusers |
| `settings` | `pb_get_settings`, `pb_update_settings`, `pb_test_s3`, `pb_test_email`, `pb_generate_apple_client_secret` | superusers |
| `logs` | `pb_list_logs`, `pb_get_log`, `pb_get_log_stats`, `pb_truncate_logs` | superusers |
| `crons` | `pb_list_crons`, `pb_run_cron` | superusers |
| `sql` | `pb_run_sql` | superusers |
| `backups` | `pb_list_backups`, `pb_create_backup`, `pb_upload_backup`, `pb_download_backup`, `pb_delete_backup`, `pb_restore_backup` | superusers |

- Record create and update take field values in `data`, with files as `{"name", "base64", "type"}` objects
  (`"field+"` appends, `"field-"` removes).
- `pb_delete_collection`, `pb_truncate_collection`, `pb_delete_backup` and `pb_restore_backup` need `confirm` set to
  the name.
- Endpoints that hand out a new token (auth-with-*, auth-refresh, impersonate) and realtime (a stream) aren't tools.
- Each tool call counts against the API's rate limits, like any request. Batch sub-requests skip route middleware
  (PocketBase behaviour).

### Add your own tools from pb_hooks

Write the endpoint as you would anyway, then declare its tool at the top level of a hooks file:

```js
// pb_hooks/blog.pb.js
routerAdd('POST', '/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish', (e) => { /* … */ }, $apis.requireSuperuserAuth())

$mcp.addEndpoint({
  name: 'blog_publish_post',
  description: 'Publish a draft post and email subscribers.',
  method: 'POST',
  path: '/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish', // {id} comes from args.id
  inputSchema: { type: 'object', required: ['id'], properties: { id: { type: 'string' } } },
  // optional; request is the default mapping, return a changed copy
  request: ({ args, auth, request }) => ({ ...request, body: { at: args.when } }),
  // optional; throw for an error the model can read
  response: ({ status, json }) => (status === 200 ? { published: json.id } : json),
})
$mcp.instructions('blog_publish_post also emails subscribers.')
```

- The tool runs the request as the caller, so the route's own auth check is what protects it. One tool serves every
  caller.
- `title`, `outputSchema` and `annotations` are optional. Without annotations, `GET` tools are marked read-only and
  `DELETE` tools destructive.
- `request` gets `{args, auth, request}` and returns `{method, path, query, body, headers, files}` (missing keys keep
  the default; `$mcp.pathValue(v)` escapes a path segment).
- `response` gets `{args, auth, status, headers, body, json, truncated}`.
- Both run one at a time on the VM that loaded the hooks and may use the file's top-level variables; the REST call
  itself runs outside it. Keep them small: the work belongs in the endpoint.
- `$mcp.tools()` lists the registered tool names.

Agents are told to prefer the app's own tools: when an app has any, the instructions sent on connect say to use them
when one fits and fall back to `pb_*`, and the tool list shows them first. Put work that spans collections in a
custom endpoint (one transaction, the app's checks), not in a chain of `pb_*` calls. A wrapper can sit over a stock
endpoint too, to give it the app's meaning (for example `notes_add_note` over `POST /api/collections/notes/records`).

### In the logs

Without the OAuth server on the app, MCP logs a warning on serve:
`mcp: the OAuth server (ext/tokens) is off; /mcp accepts pasted PocketBase auth tokens only, and clients can't sign in by themselves`.
In `pocketone` it always is.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | Signs MCP clients in. MCP points clients at it from the protected resource metadata, turns on its client self-registration, and makes tokens bound to `/mcp` never expire. Who may sign in comes from its `Collections` (default: superusers and every auth collection). |
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | The access tokens are API tokens bound to `https://<host>/mcp` (RFC 8707): they work nowhere else, and are listed and revoked under Settings → API tokens. |
| Your token scopes | On a full-access connection a tool call holds every scope you registered (except ones its collection can't hold): `$tokens.requireScope` guards pass, and `@request.headers.x_token_scope_<name>` is `"1"` in collection rules. On a connection limited to scopes it holds only those, and requests they don't cover are refused (see [Scopes](#scopes)). |
| [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/extension) | A `pb_pages` `+api.js` route is a REST endpoint like any other; declare its tool with `$mcp.addEndpoint`. |
| [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect) | `pb_download_file` follows its one redirect to storage. |
| JS hooks | `$mcp` in `pb_hooks` (above). |

Under [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), every instance gets MCP from the standard set, with its own tokens, OAuth sign-in
and `/mcp`; an instance turns it off with `extensions.mcp.enabled: false`.

### Tools from Go

An extension registered on the same app reaches the server with `mcp.For(app)`:

```go
server := mcp.For(app) // or the *mcp.Server that mcp.MustRegister returned

// the endpoint, as you'd write it anyway
app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
    se.Router.POST("/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish", publish).Bind(apis.RequireSuperuserAuth())
    return se.Next()
})

// the tool wrapper
server.MustAddEndpoint(mcp.Endpoint{
    Name:        "blog_publish_post",            // lowercase <extension>_<verb>_<noun>; pb_ is the built-ins'
    Title:       "Publish post",
    Description: "Publish a draft post and email subscribers.",
    Method:      http.MethodPost,
    Path:        "/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish", // {id} is filled from args.id
    InputSchema: map[string]any{"type": "object", "required": []any{"id"},
        "properties": map[string]any{"id": map[string]any{"type": "string"}}},
    Annotations: mcp.Write,                      // default from the method: GET read-only, DELETE destructive
    Request:     nil,                            // optional: func(c *mcp.Call) (*mcp.Request, error)
    Response:    nil,                            // optional: func(c *mcp.Call, res *mcp.Response) (any, error)
})
server.AddInstructions("blog_publish_post also emails subscribers.")
```

The default mapping:

- `{name}` path segments come from the argument of the same name, escaped. Empty, `.` and `..` are refused (the
  router would clean them into another route).
- Other arguments go to the query string for `GET`, `HEAD` and `DELETE`, and to the JSON body for other methods.
- An argument holding a file, `{"name": "a.png", "base64": "…", "type": "image/png"}` or a list of them, makes the
  body multipart (other arguments ride along as `@jsonPayload`), the way PocketBase takes uploads. Up to 10 MB per
  file.
- Arguments are checked against the schema's `required`, top-level `type`s, `enum`s and `additionalProperties: false`
  before the request is made; the endpoint validates the rest.
- The result: 2xx JSON comes back as the result (also as `structuredContent` when it's an object); other 2xx bodies
  as text; 4xx/5xx as a tool error with PocketBase's `{status, message, data}`, so the model can fix its call. JSON
  results are capped at 1 MB and say when they were cut.

`Request` sees the caller (`c.Auth()`) but can't change who the request runs as: an `Authorization` header it sets is
dropped. Build paths with `c.Path(template)` or `mcp.PathValue`, never by joining raw strings. `c.Do` makes another
request as the same caller (e.g. a file token before a download). `Response` may return any JSON-able value, a
string, or an `mcp.Content` list (images, text, embedded files). `SuperuserOnly: true` hides a tool from other
callers' tool list.

### Tools from an extension

An extension's API is contracts, and a contract's operations are already tools: nothing to add. For a tool that
isn't a contract operation, an extension calls `mcpv1.AddTool(app, mcpv1.Tool{...})` (and `mcpv1.AddInstructions`)
in its `Register`, which works with whichever extension provides mcp/v1.

A PocketOne extension that adds tools names them `<extension>_<verb>_<noun>`: its name (with `-` as `_`), then at least two
lowercase words, such as `notes_list_notes` or `oauth_server_revoke_client`. Each has a description, and an input
schema, when it has one, is a JSON Schema object. The [conformance test](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension) checks all of this
when the extension's test puts an MCP server on the test apps:

```go
conformance.Run(t, newExtension, conformance.Options{Setup: func(app core.App) error {
    _, err := mcp.Register(app, mcp.Config{})
    return err
}})
```

### How sign-in works

With Tokens (with its OAuth server) on the app, `/mcp` uses OAuth the way Claude connectors and Claude Code expect:

1. A request without a token gets `401` with
   `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://<host>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`.
2. The protected resource metadata names the app as its authorization server (the OAuth server's issuer). The OAuth server
   publishes the authorization server metadata, with PKCE S256, client metadata documents and dynamic registration.
3. The client registers itself (Claude's published identity through a client metadata document, or dynamic
   registration), and the user signs in in a browser.
4. The access token is an API token bound to `https://<host>/mcp`. It carries the account's rights but works only on
   `/mcp`. Each MCP request makes a PocketBase auth token for the same account, and tool calls reach the REST API
   with it (as Pages' `ctx.pb()` does). For a token limited to scopes, those requests carry the scopes
   (`tokensv1.WithScopes`, through the tokens/v1 contract), and Tokens checks them as it would a scoped token's request.

Without the OAuth server, `/mcp` falls back to `PocketBaseTokenAuth`: pasted PocketBase auth tokens (`Collections` limits
which auth collections, default any), and the warning above. `Config.Auth` overrides the choice; `mcp.OAuth{Issuer}`
overrides the authorization server listed in the metadata.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/mcp/example/main.go) runs one app with an MCP endpoint at `/mcp`: the built-in `pb_*` tools, a tool over a Go route and one over a JS route.

```bash
cd example
go run . serve
```

The example registers [devusers](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go), so the logins are `admin@example.com` / `password`
(superuser) and `user@example.com` / `password` (user). It also registers Tokens (with its OAuth server) for OAuth sign-in,
and adds a tool over a Go route (`example_get_whoami`) and one over a JS route (`example_list_recent_users`, in
[`pb_hooks/mcp.pb.js`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/mcp/example/pb_hooks/mcp.pb.js)). Then:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http pb-example http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp
claude mcp login pb-example
```

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app with an MCP endpoint at /mcp: the built-in pb_* tools (the whole stock REST
// API), a tool over a Go route, and a tool over a JS route from pb_hooks/mcp.pb.js.
//
//	cd ext/mcp/example && go run . serve
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
//
// Sign-in is OAuth (the OAuth server in ext/tokens): add the endpoint to Claude Code and sign in in the browser when it
// asks. Tool calls run as whoever signed in.
//
//	claude mcp add --transport http pb-example http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp
//	claude mcp login pb-example   (or /mcp in a session)
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/apis"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit/js"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mcp"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	// OAuth sign-in: API tokens + the authorization server. ext/mcp picks it up on serve and turns on dynamic client
	// registration.
	tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{}) // its OAuth server comes with it

	server := mcp.MustRegister(app, mcp.Config{
		Name:        "pb-example",
		Description: "Example PocketOne app with ext/mcp.",
	})

	// A tool from Go: write the REST endpoint, then the tool wrapper. The tool runs the request as the caller, so
	// the route's own auth check is what protects it.
	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
		se.Router.GET("/api/example/whoami", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
			return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"collection": e.Auth.Collection().Name, "email": e.Auth.Email()})
		}).Bind(apis.RequireAuth())
		return se.Next()
	})
	server.MustAddEndpoint(mcp.Endpoint{
		Name:        "example_get_whoami",
		Title:       "Who am I",
		Description: "The signed-in record's collection and email.",
		Method:      http.MethodGet,
		Path:        "/api/example/whoami",
	})

	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
		OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { mcp.BindJS(app, rt) },
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Go config

| Field | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `Name`, `Version`, `Description`, `Icons` | app name slug, `dev` | `serverInfo` |
| `Instructions` | generated | first paragraph of the instructions sent on connect |
| `PublicURL` | the request's host | origin used for the OAuth resource URL; set it when a proxy rewrites the host |
| `Auth` | `OAuth{}` with Tokens' OAuth server on, else `PocketBaseTokenAuth{}` | the `Authenticator` |
| `BuiltinGroups` | all | which `pb_*` groups (`mcp.BuiltinGroups`) |
| `ReadOnlyBuiltins` | `false` | keep only the read-only `pb_*` tools |
| `NoBuiltins` | `false` | drop every `pb_*` tool |
| `MaxResponse` | 1 MB | cap on a JSON result |
| `MaxFile` | 10 MB | cap on one file uploaded or downloaded through a tool |
| `AllowedOrigins` | none | extra browser origins allowed besides the app's own |

The endpoint speaks MCP Streamable HTTP, stateless: each POST carries one JSON-RPC message and gets JSON back.
Protocol versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18` and `2025-03-26`. Tools only for now.
