Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/extension

# Pages

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Server-rendered pages from a `pb_pages` folder, next to your `pb_data`. Each file becomes a route: EJS, Markdown,
JSX and TSX templates, layouts, middleware and API routes, plus static files. Page code runs in your app's JS VM, so it
can use your data directly. This is PocketPages v1, formerly the npm PocketPages package.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Pages is built into `pocketone` and **on whenever a `pb_pages` folder exists** next to `pb_data`. There's no switch:
no folder, no pages. If the folder appears while the app runs, it starts serving it.

In your own Go build, register it after the JS VM ([ext/jsvm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm)), since page code runs there:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{})   // page code runs in the app's JS VM
pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{}) // serves pb_pages next to pb_data
pages.RegisterCommand(app.RootCmd)      // the `pages create` and `pages starters` commands
app.Start()
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pages`. See [example/main.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/example/main.go) and
[Create your own extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension).

## Configure

### Where the folder is

By default the folder is `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`. To use another one:

```bash
pocketone serve --pagesDir /path/to/pb_pages
```

A relative path resolves against the working directory, like `--hooksDir`. Its `pocketone.yaml` key is `server.pages_dir`.

### +config.js

Settings for your pages live in the folder itself, in `pb_pages/+config.js`:

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
  debug: false,
}
```

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins` | `[]` | Module names (a `_private/` file, a `node_modules` package or a path, loaded with `require`), built-in plugins by name (`auth`, `realtime`, used when no module by that name is found), or JS plugins such as the [add-ons](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/README.md). EJS and Markdown are always on. |
| `debug` | `false` | Detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output even outside dev mode. |

`+config.js` runs on each page request. Unknown keys, names that are neither a module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page
answer with an error, and the reason goes to the log.

### Dev mode

When the app runs in dev mode (`--dev`, or `app.dev` in `pocketone.yaml`), or `+config.js` sets `debug: true`, you
get detailed error pages with the file and line, and `ctx.log.debug` output. Otherwise visitors see a plain
"Something went wrong" page and the full error goes to the log.

## Use

### Start from a starter kit

```bash
pocketone pages starters                         # list the kits
pocketone pages create myapp --starter daisyui-docs
cd myapp
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. `pages create` makes a new folder (it must not exist yet) with `pb_pages` and
anything the kit needs beside it, such as `pb_migrations`. Without `--starter` you get `minimal`.

| Kit | What it is |
|---|---|
| [minimal](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/minimal/README.md) | One page, no layout, no build step (the default). |
| [mvp](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/mvp/README.md) | One page styled with MVP.css. |
| [htmx](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/htmx/README.md) | A realtime chat and counter with htmx and the `realtime` plugin. |
| [daisyui](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/daisyui/README.md) | A navbar and drawer layout with Tailwind CSS and DaisyUI. |
| [daisyui-docs](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/daisyui-docs/README.md) | A docs site from Markdown pages. |
| [datastar](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/datastar/README.md) | A realtime chat with rooms, with Datastar. |
| [auth](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/auth/README.md) | Sign-up, sign-in (password, OTP, OAuth2, anonymous), email flows and a protected account page. |

### Write pages

Add or edit files in `pb_pages` and reload the browser; no restart is needed. A few examples of what the folder holds:

```
pb_pages/
  +config.js         settings (above)
  +layout.ejs        wraps every page
  +error.ejs         your error page
  index.ejs          /
  about.md           /about
  blog/[slug].ejs    /blog/anything
  feeds/rss/+api.js  /feeds/rss, a route without a template
  _private/          partials, never served
  assets/app.css     a static file
```

The full contract is in [SPEC.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/spec): routes and precedence, middleware, `+page.js` and `+api.js`, EJS,
partials, slots and layouts, Markdown, JSX and TSX, the `ctx` object, errors, the built-in `auth` and `realtime`
plugins, JS plugins, add-ons and the changes from 0.x.

Highlights:

- Static files get ETags and fingerprinted URLs through `asset()`.
- `ctx.pb()` is the bundled PocketBase JS SDK, called in-process as the visitor.
- `ctx.res.sse()` streams server-sent events.
- The `auth` plugin gives cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: password, OTP, anonymous, register, OAuth2 and the email
  flows (verification, password reset, email change). Accounts that need MFA (the collection's MFA is on and its rule matches) are refused by every pages sign-in method; pages has no second sign-in step yet.

### What you'll see in the log

Problems in the folder (a bad file name, two files claiming the same route) are logged as `pages: ...` errors. If the
site served cleanly before, pages keeps the previous routes until the folder builds cleanly again. Errors thrown by
page code are logged in full.

### Try the demo

[`example/`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/example) is a demo app with EJS, Markdown, JSX, auth, `ctx.pb()`, SSE and a JSON route. It has a live
speed check at `/speed`.

```bash
cd example && go run . serve --dir=./pb_data
```

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone pages create <name>`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-pages-create) | Create a folder with a starter kit (pb\_pages and anything it needs) |
| [`pocketone pages starters`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-pages-starters) | List the starter kits |

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Pages is in the standard set, so every instance serves its own `pb_pages` (below). |
| [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache) | Compiled templates and modules go in the `pages.compiled` bucket (cache/v1, at most 32 MiB per app), keyed by content, so old versions are evicted instead of piling up. On a multisite host, instances serving the same files share one compiled copy. On a multisite host they also outlive an instance's restarts, since the cache belongs to the host. With the cache off, each JS VM compiles a file the first time it meets it. |
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | `pb_pages` deploys with your other `pb_*` folders. `pull` doesn't fetch it by default; name it: `pocketone pull prod pb_pages`. |

### Under pocker

Pages is a member of the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard), so every instance serves its own
`<instance dir>/pb_pages`, in the stock `pocketone` binary and in any host built on `standard.New()`. A host without
the standard set adds it like any extension:

```go
srv := &pocker.Server{Config: cfg, Extensions: []pocker.Extension{pages.New(pages.Config{})}}
```

- Each start of an instance's app gets its own route table, compiled templates (in its own `pages.compiled` bucket; identical files share one copy in the host's cache) and caches. An instance that sleeps
  drops them; nothing is shared between instances.
- Page code runs in the instance's own sandboxed JS VM ([jsvm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm)), under its limits (execution time,
  memory, stack). `include`, `require`, `ctx.resolve`, `ctx.res.file` and `asset` never reach outside the instance's
  `pb_pages`; `$os` file access stays inside the instance folder. Tests:
  [multiinstance_test.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/multiinstance/multiinstance_test.go).
- An instance turns pages off in its settings with `extensions: { pages: { enabled: false } }`.

Measured on the earlier goja engine (same machine as [Speed](#speed), docs kit; not yet re-measured on jsvm): each
awake instance added about **2.3 MB** (50 instances: 41 MB idle to 155 MB), and one instance under pocker served about
**4,000 requests/s** (p50 5.6 ms, p99 80 ms at 50 concurrent).

To try it: copy sites into `multiinstance/example/pb_root/<name>.localhost/pb_pages`, run
`go run ./multiinstance/example`, and open `http://<name>.localhost:8791`.

### Building on pages

- **Read the routes.** `pages.For(app)` returns the service: `Dir()` is the folder, `Table()` the current route
  table, `Errors()` the problems from the last build.
- **JS plugins.** A factory in `+config.js` can add to `ctx`, run on each request and transform rendered HTML
  ([SPEC.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/spec), section 9.2). [Add-ons](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/README.md) are built this way.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/example/main.go) serves the demo in [`example/pb_pages`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/example/pb_pages): EJS, Markdown, JSX/TSX, auth, SSE and a JSON route. Run `go run . serve --dir=./pb_data` in `example/` and open http://127.0.0.1:8090.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app that serves the demo in ./pb_pages (EJS, Markdown, JSX/TSX, auth,
// ctx.pb(), SSE, a JSON route, +404). ./pb_migrations creates a "notes" collection
// with three seed notes. From this folder:
//
//	go run . serve --dir=./pb_data
//
// Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. Edit anything in pb_pages and reload; no restart needed.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com /
// password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pages"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // page code runs in the app's JS VM
	pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Speed

`ext/pages` against npm PocketPages 0.22.5 (the last 0.x release), serving the same starter kit pages: the 0.x kits
in `pb_hooks/pages` on stock PocketBase 0.41.1, the v1 ports in `pb_pages` on the PocketOne binary.

| Page | Version | Requests/s (50 concurrent) | p50 | p99 | One at a time (median) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `minimal` `/` (EJS) | npm 0.22.5 | 620 | 30 ms | 670 ms | 5.7 ms |
| | **ext/pages** | **10,850** | **1.8 ms** | **37 ms** | **0.2 ms** |
| `daisyui-docs` `/docs/overview` (layouts, Markdown, partial) | npm 0.22.5 | 580 | 28 ms | 1.1 s | 6.5 ms |
| | **ext/pages** | **6,510** | **4.1 ms** | **49 ms** | **0.4 ms** |
| PocketBase's own `/api/health` (the ceiling) | PocketOne | 55,000 | 0.9 ms | 2.4 ms | 0.1 ms |

About **17.5× more requests per second** on the simple page and **11×** on the docs page, with p99 latency 20× lower.
Single requests take 0.2 to 0.4 ms instead of 6 ms. Memory after each run was similar (170 to 350 MB for both).

Why: 0.x parsed routes, ran EJS through a JS implementation and loaded its plugins inside the JS VM on every request.
v1 builds the route table once, compiles each template once (EJS to JS in Go, Markdown with goldmark) and enters the
JS VM once per request.

How it was measured (2026-11-11): Apple M1 Max, 10 cores, macOS 27, Go 1.27.4, `hey` against `127.0.0.1`. Each server
was warmed with 500 requests, then `hey -z 10s -c 50` and `hey -n 2000 -c 1`; two rounds, which agreed within 5%.
Every response was a 200 with the full page. The 0.x docs kit inlines about 6 KB of CSS into each page where v1
links `app.css`. Rerun it with [`bench/run.sh`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/bench/run.sh):

```bash
cp -R starters/daisyui-docs /tmp/v1-docs
pocketone superuser upsert admin@example.com password --dir=/tmp/v1-docs/pb_data
bench/run.sh v1-docs 8804 /docs/overview "$(which pocketone)" /tmp/v1-docs
```

## More in this folder

- [SPEC.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/spec): the full PocketPages v1 contract.
- [fixtures/](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/fixtures/README.md): the request test cases (`go test ./...` runs them all).
- [starters/](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/starters): the starter kits. [addons/](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/README.md): JS add-ons such as Datastar.
- [site/](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/site/_private/toc.md): the PocketPages docs, as PocketPages pages (formerly pocketpages.dev), shown on
  pocketone.dev under this page. [blog/](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/blog): the PocketPages blog posts.

# PITR

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Point-in-time restore: your database as it was at any moment in the last few days, restored from the dashboard.
History is recorded with [Litestream](https://litestream.io), next to your data or in an S3-compatible bucket.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

PITR is built into `pocketone` and **on by default**. Every app it serves starts recording history the first time it
serves; there's nothing to install.

To run without it:

```bash
pocketone serve --pitr=false
```

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
pitr.MustRegister(app, pitr.Config{})
app.Start()
```

## Configure

### On, off and how far back

Set it in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
pitr:
  enabled: true          # false turns it off
  retention: 72h         # how far back a restore can go
  snapshot_interval: 24h # how often a full copy is taken
```

Or with flags, which win over the file:

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--pitr` | `true` | Record history while serving. `--pitr=false` turns it off. |
| `--pitrRetention` | `72h` | How far back a restore can go. |

A shorter `snapshot_interval` makes restores faster and uses more storage.

### Where the history is stored

By default the history is kept next to your database, in `pb_data/litestream/`. That protects you from mistakes in
your data, but not from losing the disk. To keep it somewhere else, use your own S3-compatible bucket:

1. Open **Settings → Backups** in the dashboard and find **Point-in-time restore**.
2. Tick **Store the history in my own S3 bucket** and fill in the endpoint, bucket, region, access key and secret.
   Tick **Force path-style addressing** for MinIO and similar servers. The prefix defaults to `litestream`.
3. Click **Test connection** to check that the bucket accepts a write, then **Save**.

From then on the history is recorded in the bucket, starting with a fresh copy, so restores go back to the moment you
saved. The secret is never shown again after saving. If the app runs with an encryption key (`--encryptionEnv`), the secret
is stored encrypted.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `pitr:`

Point-in-time restore: on by default, retention, snapshot interval. The --pitr and --pitrRetention flags win.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false. The --pitr flag wins. |
| `retention` | duration |  | How far back a restore can go. Default 72h. The --pitrRetention flag wins. |
| `snapshot_interval` | duration |  | How often a full copy is taken. Default 24h. Shorter: faster restores, more storage. |

## Use

### What's covered

Your database: records, collections, settings and superusers. **Not** uploaded files, `pb_hooks`, `pb_public` or the
logs database. Use PocketBase's backups for those.

History starts with the first change after PITR is turned on, and goes back as far as the retention allows (72 hours
by default).

### Restore from the dashboard

1. Open **Settings → Backups**. **Restore to a moment** (the [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1)
   contract's section) shows how far back you can go; **Point-in-time restore** shows how big the history is and where
   it's stored.
2. Under **Restore to**, pick a date and time, then click **Restore**.
3. The app keeps serving while the old database is rebuilt, then restarts with it.

Only superusers see this section.

### Undo a restore

The database you replaced is kept in `pb_data/litestream/before-restore.db`, and history keeps recording, so a restore
can be undone. After a restore, the section shows when you restored and to what time, with an **Undo this restore**
button.

### From the command line

```bash
pocketone pitr status
pocketone pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z --to /tmp/then.db   # a copy, any time
pocketone pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z                     # in place
```

`--at` takes an RFC 3339 time. With `--to`, you get a copy of the database as it was, to inspect or pull records
from; the app keeps running. Without `--to`, run it while the server is stopped: the restore is swapped in when it
next starts.

### What it costs

About 176 KiB of memory per serving app, and the storage for your history. Replication runs only while the app is
serving, never during CLI commands.

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone pitr restore`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-pitr-restore) | Restore the database as it was at --at, into --to, or in place on the next start |
| [`pocketone pitr status`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-pitr-status) | Show the restorable window and history size |

### [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [points](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1#points) | `pocketone remote restore points` | `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` | `restore_points` |
| [restore_to](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1#restore_to) | `pocketone remote restore to --at <time>` | `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` | `restore_restore_to` |

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Every instance on the host gets PITR. The `pitr` section sets the defaults for all of them; each instance can override `enabled` and `retention` (below). A restore restarts only that instance, and sleeping instances cost nothing. |
| [S3 Fallback](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback) | Mount `litestream` on a backend and every app without its own bucket keeps its history there, under its own prefix. An app's own bucket (Settings → Backups) still wins. |
| [Multitenant](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants) (planned) | Sets each instance's `enabled` and `retention` from its plan, for example a plan without PITR. |
| PocketBase backups | `pb_data/litestream/` is left out of backup zips, and restoring a zip doesn't wipe it. |

### Per-instance settings (pocker)

Each instance can override `enabled` and `retention` in its `extensions.pitr` settings, from `instances.yaml` or a
provider:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: abc
    extensions: { pitr: { retention: 168h } }
  - id: free-plan-app
    extensions: { pitr: { enabled: false } }
```

Each instance's history goes to `instances/<id>/litestream/` in the shared bucket, or its own `pb_data/litestream/`.
A bucket in an instance's settings is refused, so credentials never sit in instance data.

### Building on PITR

- **Store history somewhere else.** PITR asks PocketBase for a filesystem of kind `litestream` (`pitr.Kind`) through
  `OnFilesystemCreate`. Answer it and the history goes to your filesystem; S3 Fallback works this way.
- **Set it per instance.** Write `extensions.pitr.enabled` and `extensions.pitr.retention` into an instance's settings;
  PITR reads them when the instance starts. Multitenant will work this way.
- **Go API.** `(*pitr.Extension).Status(ctx, app)` returns the restorable window, size, destination and last restore;
  `Restore(ctx, app, at)` restores an app to a time.
- **restore/v1.** PITR provides the [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1) contract (superusers):
  `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` for the window, size, destination and last restore, `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore`
  with `{"at": "<RFC 3339 time>"}` to restore. Without PITR the same calls restore the latest backup before the
  moment ([Backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups)), so clients and agents don't care which is on.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pitr/example/main.go) runs one app with point-in-time restore on, keeping three days. Run it with `go run ./example serve` from this folder.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app with point-in-time restore: Litestream copies data.db continuously into
// pb_data/litestream/, and Settings → Backups gets a "Point-in-time restore" section.
//
//	go run ./example serve
//	go run ./example pitr status
//	go run ./example pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z --to /tmp/then.db
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pitr"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	pitr.MustRegister(app, pitr.Config{
		Retention: 72 * time.Hour, // on by default; Enabled: false turns it off
		// Bucket: &pitr.Bucket{Endpoint: "...", Bucket: "...", Region: "auto", AccessKey: "...", Secret: "...", Label: "EU"},
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Go module `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pitr`, Litestream v0.5.18 (pinned).
  [`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pitr/example/main.go) runs one app with local history.
- Litestream continuously copies `data.db` to its destination: the app's own bucket (its PITR settings), else a
  filesystem of kind `litestream` (an `OnFilesystemCreate` handler, such as S3 Fallback), else `pb_data/litestream/`.
  Buckets go through PocketBase's own S3 client, not the AWS SDK. Each LTX file's timestamp is kept in object
  metadata, so restoring to a time doesn't depend on upload times.
- Replication runs only while the app serves (`OnServe`), never for CLI commands. On terminate it's flushed and
  detached, so under pocker a sleeping instance costs nothing.
- A restore is built into a side file while the app keeps serving, then swapped in by `app.Restart()`. The replaced
  database is kept as `pb_data/litestream/before-restore.db`.
- Apps with different retention get separate Litestream stores, since Litestream applies retention per store.
- Cost per serving app: about 176 KiB of memory, 4 goroutines, 5 file descriptors. Binary: about +4 MiB.

## License

MIT

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes

# Remotes

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Named remotes for the `pocketone` command: the apps a project deploys to, each signed in to once. Give an app a name
like `prod`, log in, and commands such as `pocketone deploy prod` know where to go and who you are.

```bash
pocketone remote add prod https://myapp.example.com
pocketone login prod
pocketone deploy prod          # Deploy
```

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Remotes is built into `pocketone` and **on**: the `remote`, `login`, `logout` and `link` commands are always there, and
every app provides [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts): whoami at `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` (so other machines can sign
in to it), status, restart and logs. There's nothing to install: it's in the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

In your own Go build, use the standard set, or register it through its contracts yourself:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{remotes.New(remotes.Config{})}, nil, nil) // remote/v1; on *pocketbase.PocketBase also the commands
app.Start()
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes`. Add [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) for API tokens and
[the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) for browser login.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or settings screen. Remotes keeps two files and reads a few environment
variables.

### The project's remotes

`.pocketbase/remotes.json` in the project holds names and URLs only, so commit it:

```json
{"default": "prod", "remotes": {"prod": {"url": "https://myapp.example.com"}}}
```

Commands find it by walking up from the current folder. It isn't a `pb_*` name, since `pb_*` folders are deployed.

### Saved logins

Logins are saved per user, keyed by URL, in `~/.config/pocketone/credentials.json` (mode 0600). Set
`P1_CONFIG_DIR` to use another folder; with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set, it's `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pocketone/`.

### Environment variables

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `P1_TOKEN_<REMOTE>` | A token for one remote, for CI. The name is upper case, other characters as `_` (`P1_TOKEN_PROD`). |
| `P1_TOKEN` | A token for any remote. |
| `P1_CONFIG_DIR` | Where saved logins are kept. |

A token in the environment wins over a saved login. Every PocketOne variable starts with `P1_`, in every build (the
`pockethost` binary reads `P1_TOKEN` too). The `pocketone` folder comes from the command's name, so a build shipped
under another name keeps its logins apart (`~/.config/pockethost`).

## Use

### Manage remotes

```bash
pocketone remote add prod https://myapp.example.com --default
pocketone remote list            # names, URLs and who you're logged in as; * marks the default
pocketone remote default prod
pocketone remote rm staging      # the saved login stays; see logout
pocketone remote whoami prod     # who you are there, your token's scopes, and what the app offers
```

A URL without a scheme gets `https://`. The first remote you add becomes the default. A command that names no remote
uses the default, else the only remote, else the one called `default`. Any command also takes a URL in place of a
name: `pocketone deploy https://other.example.com`.

### Log in

```bash
pocketone login prod
```

`login` tries, in order (the command itself never asks for a password):

1. **The browser**, when the remote runs [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth). Your browser opens, you sign in
   and approve, and the command finishes. Over SSH or without a display it shows a code to enter on another device
   instead; `--device` asks for that, and `--no-browser` prints the URL without opening it.
2. **A pasted token** (`pbt_...`, a PocketHost token, or a PocketBase auth token). At the prompt, paste it, or pass
   `--token <token>` or `--token-stdin`.

A browser login keeps a refresh token and renews itself when it's within a day of expiring.

You'll see `Logged in to https://myapp.example.com as admin@example.com (oauth).`

### Link in one step

```bash
pocketone link https://myapp.example.com
pocketone link https://myapp.pockethost.io ph_pat_...
```

`link` adds the remote (named `default`, or `--name`), makes it the default if there's none yet, and logs in. It takes
the same login flags.

### Log out

```bash
pocketone logout prod
```

Forgets the saved login. A browser login is also revoked on the remote (its refresh token); a pasted token stays
valid until you revoke it in the dashboard. If the remote can't be reached, it tells you to revoke it in the dashboard.

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone link <url> [token]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-link) | Adds a remote (default name "default") and signs in to it |
| [`pocketone login [remote]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-login) | Signs in to a remote and saves the login |
| [`pocketone logout [remote]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-logout) | Forgets the saved login (and revokes it, for a browser login) |
| [`pocketone remote add <name> <url>`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-remote-add) | Adds or replaces a remote |
| [`pocketone remote default <name>`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-remote-default) | Sets the default remote |
| [`pocketone remote list`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-remote-list) | Lists remotes and whether you're logged in |
| [`pocketone remote rm <name>`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-remote-rm) | Removes a remote (its saved login stays; see logout) |
| [`pocketone remote whoami [remote]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-remote-whoami) | Shows who you are on a remote and what it offers |

### [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [whoami](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1#whoami) | `pocketone remote whoami` | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` | `remote_whoami` |
| [status](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1#status) | `pocketone remote status` | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` | `remote_status` |
| [restart](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1#restart) | `pocketone remote restart` | `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` | `remote_restart` |
| [logs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1#logs) | `pocketone remote logs --n <n>` | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs` | `remote_logs` |

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | `deploy`, `dev` and `pull` resolve their remote and login through Remotes and find deploy/v1 in whoami's contracts; `restart` and `logs` use remote/v1. |
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | Provides oauth/v1, so whoami lists it; `login` then signs in through the browser (loopback redirect on 127.0.0.1 with PKCE) or a device code. |
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | Provides the API tokens `login` takes when pasted. Whoami reports a token's id and scopes. |

### remote/v1

Remote control of an app, at `/api/_c/remote/v1`:

| Operation | Endpoint | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| whoami | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` | none needed (any token may ask who it is) |
| status | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` | `remote:read` |
| restart | `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` | `remote` |
| logs | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs?n=100` (server-sent events) | `remote:read` |

Whoami says who the request's credential is and what the app offers, so clients can discover it:

```json
{"auth": {"collection": "_superusers", "id": "…", "email": "admin@example.com"}, "via": "token",
 "tokenId": "…", "scopes": ["deploy", "remote"], "contracts": ["deploy/v1", "oauth/v1", "remote/v1", "tokens/v1"],
 "extensions": ["tokens", "remotes", "deploy"],
 "app": {"name": "Acme", "url": "https://myapp.example.com"}}
```

`via` is `token` for an API token, `jwt` for a PocketBase auth token, and empty with no credential (`auth` is then
`null`, and `extensions` is left out). `contracts` are the contract APIs the app offers, each at `/api/_c/<id>/`:
everything a client can use (oauth/v1's metadata is at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`). Restart answers at once and restarts just after (under Pocker, only
that instance).

### Building on Remotes

- **remote/v1 client.** `remotev1.NewClient(url, token, httpClient)` (ext/contracts/remote/v1) calls whoami, status,
  restart and logs.
- **Go client.** The CLI client lives with the contract, in
  [`remoteclient`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient) (ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient), so other extensions'
  commands use it without importing this one. `remoteclient.Open(dir, name)` resolves a remote and its credential
  (environment first, then the saved login, renewing a browser login when due) and returns a `*remoteclient.Client`:
  base URL, bearer token, an HTTP client with short connect timeouts, and `JSON`, `NewRequest`, `Do` and `Whoami`.
  It also holds the linked project (`LoadProject`), saved logins (`LoadCredentials`) and the sign-ins
  (`LoginWithToken`, `OAuthLogin`). Deploy's commands build on it.
- **Commands.** `remotes.Commands()` returns the `remote`, `login`, `logout` and `link` commands, for a binary that
  isn't a `*pocketbase.PocketBase`. The rest of `remote` is generated: every operation of every contract the binary
  links is a `remote ...` command ([cli.commands/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cli.commands/v1)), such as `remote status`,
  `remote restart`, `remote restore to --at -2h`.
- **Login.** `remotes.BrowserLogin` is the sign-in `login` tries first (`remoteclient.OAuthLogin`; tests replace it).

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/remotes/example/main.go) is an app with remotes and API tokens. Run two copies and add one as a remote of the other; its comment has the commands.

```go
// Command example is a PocketOne app with remotes and API tokens: run two copies, add one as a remote of the other's
// project and sign in.
//
//	go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090                # the "remote"
//	go run ./example remote add local http://127.0.0.1:8090    # in a project folder
//	go run ./example login local                               # browser sign-in: admin@example.com / password
//	go run ./example remote whoami
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	// registered through their contracts (the standard set does this for you): remotes provides remote/v1 (whoami at
	// /api/_c/remote/v1, status, restart, logs) and the remote/login/logout/link commands; tokens adds API tokens
	// and the OAuth server login signs in through
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{tokens.New(tokens.Config{}), remotes.New(remotes.Config{})}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

MIT

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect

# S3 Redirect

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

File downloads as short-lived signed redirects to your bucket, after PocketBase's own access check.

When an app keeps its files in S3 (Settings → Files storage), PocketBase normally downloads each file from the bucket
and streams it to the browser. With S3 Redirect, `/api/files/...` answers **302** with a presigned GET URL instead,
and the browser fetches the file straight from the bucket. The app's bandwidth, memory and connections stay free.
With Cloudflare R2 the downloads cost no egress either.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

S3 Redirect is built into `pocketone` and **on by default**. It only acts when S3 file storage is on: turn on S3 in
Settings → Files storage and downloads redirect. With files on local disk, nothing changes.

To stream files through the app as before:

```bash
pocketone serve --s3Redirect=false
```

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
import "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/s3redirect"

app := pocketbase.New()
s3redirect.MustRegister(app, s3redirect.Config{TTL: 5 * time.Minute})
app.Start()
```

Then turn on S3 in Settings → Files storage.

## Configure

Set it in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
s3redirect:
  enabled: true   # false streams files through the app
  ttl: 5m         # how long each signed URL is valid
```

Or with flags, which win over the file:

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--s3Redirect` | `true` | Redirect downloads when S3 file storage is on. `--s3Redirect=false` streams them. |
| `--s3RedirectTTL` | `5m` | How long each signed URL stays valid (at most 7 days). |

Keep the TTL short: anyone holding a URL can fetch the file until it expires, protected files included.

The bucket itself is PocketBase's own S3 setting, in **Settings → Files storage**. There are no other settings
screens.

**Bucket CORS.** A redirect followed by `fetch()` or `<img crossorigin>` from your site needs a CORS rule on the
bucket allowing `GET` from your origin. Plain `<img>`, `<video>` and links need nothing.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `s3redirect:`

Signed S3 redirects for file downloads: enabled, URL lifetime. The --s3Redirect and --s3RedirectTTL flags win.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false (it only acts when S3 file storage is on). Flag: --s3Redirect. |
| `ttl` | duration |  | How long each signed URL stays valid. Default 5m, max 7 days. Flag: --s3RedirectTTL. |

## Use

Once S3 is on, there's nothing to click. File URLs stay the same; they answer with a redirect:

- **Access checks don't change.** PocketBase still finds the record, checks protected-file tokens and the view rule,
  and creates thumbnails on first request. The redirect happens only after all of that.
- **The file token stays private.** It never goes into the bucket URL, and the redirect sends
  `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
- **Same headers as PocketBase:** inline or attachment (`?download=1`), the filename, and forced content types (SVG,
  CSS, JS) are signed into the URL as S3 `response-*` overrides. Range requests work, because S3 serves them.
- **Caching:** the browser may reuse the redirect for 80% of the TTL (`Cache-Control: private`, never shared
  caches); the file itself gets PocketBase's usual 30-day `Cache-Control`.
- **Falls back to streaming** when S3 is off, the extension is turned off, or signing fails. A failed signature logs a
  warning, `s3redirect: signing failed, streaming instead`.
- Only `GET` and `HEAD` requests are redirected.

**Inline vs attachment:** PocketBase decides this from the stored content type; S3 Redirect goes by the file
extension (it doesn't ask the bucket, so a redirect costs no extra round trip). They agree for every file PocketBase
names.

### Try it

```
cd example && go run . serve
```

The example runs one app with its own in-process bucket, nothing to set up. It:

- starts an S3-compatible bucket on `127.0.0.1:9199` ([gofakes3](https://github.com/johannesboyne/gofakes3),
  objects kept in `pb_data/demo-s3.bolt`), and points the app's Files storage at it;
- seeds a `demo_files` record with an image (thumbs `100x100`) and a protected text file, uploaded through PocketBase;
- prints the URLs to open. Each answers `302` to the bucket.

The bucket only serves presigned GETs whose signature, re-computed with the **AWS SDK's own SigV4 signer**, matches
and hasn't expired, and logs each one (`demo bucket: presigned GET ..., signature valid`). Unsigned or edited URLs get
`403`. So a working download proves the signatures are AWS-compatible, not just accepted by a lenient fake.

`S3REDIRECT_DEMO=0` skips the demo bucket (use your own Files storage settings); `S3REDIRECT_DEMO_ADDR` moves it.
The example is its own Go module, so its demo dependencies (gofakes3, the AWS SDK signer) never reach the extension's
`go.mod`.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | The same extension runs on every instance. The `s3redirect` section sets the defaults; each instance can override `enabled` and `ttl` (below). |
| [S3 Fallback](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback) | Apps without their own S3 settings keep files in its bucket (under pocker, fenced to `instances/<id>/storage/`). Its driver signs, so those downloads redirect too. |

### Per-instance settings (pocker)

```go
srv.Extensions = append(srv.Extensions, s3redirect.New(s3redirect.Config{}))
```

```yaml
s3redirect:            # server defaults
  enabled: true        # on unless false
  ttl: 5m

instances:
  - id: abc
    extensions:
      s3redirect: { enabled: false }   # per instance: enabled, ttl
```

It's an [extkit](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/extkit/extkit.go) extension, so the same value works on a single app and on every pocker
instance; it doesn't link pocker.

### Building on S3 Redirect

- **Supply your own bucket.** S3 Redirect signs for whatever filesystem PocketBase serves the download from: the
  app's own S3 settings, or one an extension supplies through `OnFilesystemCreate`. Implement `s3redirect.Signer`
  (`SignedURL(key, ttl, now, overrides)`) on your filesystem driver and its downloads redirect. Nothing else needs
  wiring; a filesystem that can't sign (local disk) streams as usual.
- **Your own download handlers run first.** The extension binds `OnFileDownloadRequest` last (priority 1000, id
  `s3redirect.HookID`, `__ext_s3redirect__`), so your Go or JS handlers can still change the served file or answer
  themselves without calling `e.Next()`. Unbind the id to turn it off for one app.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/s3redirect/example/main.go) starts its own in-process S3 bucket, points the app's file storage at it and seeds a record, so every download redirect works with nothing to set up. Run `go run . serve` in `example/` and open the URLs it prints.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app whose file downloads redirect to an S3 bucket, with nothing to set up:
// it starts its own S3-compatible bucket in-process (gofakes3, stored in pb_data/demo-s3.bolt), points the app's
// Files storage at it, and seeds a "demo_files" record with an image and a protected document.
//
//	go run . serve
//
// Open the URLs it prints. Each answers 302 with a signed URL; the bucket logs every fetch and only serves it if the
// signature is valid and unexpired, checked independently with the AWS SDK's SigV4 signer.
//
// Set S3REDIRECT_DEMO=0 to skip the demo bucket and use whatever Files storage you configure in the dashboard.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"os"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/s3redirect"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	s3redirect.MustRegister(app, s3redirect.Config{TTL: 5 * time.Minute})

	if os.Getenv("S3REDIRECT_DEMO") != "0" {
		addr := os.Getenv("S3REDIRECT_DEMO_ADDR")
		if addr == "" {
			addr = "127.0.0.1:9199"
		}
		registerDemo(app, addr)
	}

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Go module `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/s3redirect`, no dependencies beyond PocketOne.
- The redirect is an `OnFileDownloadRequest` handler; the hook already exists upstream, so there's no core change.
- Signing is SigV4 query-string auth in [`sigv4`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/s3redirect/sigv4/sigv4.go), checked against AWS's documented example. It needs
  no change to PocketBase's S3 client. The TTL is clamped to between 1 second and 7 days.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings

# Settings

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

One API for the settings an app's admins change for its extensions: PITR's S3 bucket, Bulk Mail's sending settings,
and any extension that registers a section. The dashboard screens, the CLI and agents all use it.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Settings is built into `pocketone` and **on by default**; there's nothing to install. In your own Go build:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{settings.New(), pitr.New(pitr.Config{})}, nil, nil)
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/settings`.

## Configure

There's nothing to configure.

## Use

It provides the [settings/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1) contract (superusers only):

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" https://app.example.com/api/_c/settings/v1                      # which extensions
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" "https://app.example.com/api/_c/settings/v1/get?extension=pitr" # one extension's
```

Agents get the same through MCP (`settings_list`, `settings_get`, `settings_save`, `settings_test`).

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### [settings/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [list](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1#list) | `pocketone remote settings list` | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1` | `settings_list` |
| [get](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1#get) | `pocketone remote settings get --extension <value>` | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get` | `settings_get` |
| [save](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1#save) | `pocketone remote settings save --extension <value> --values <json>` | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/save` | `settings_save` |
| [test](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1#test) | `pocketone remote settings test --extension <value> --values <json>` | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/test` | `settings_test` |

## Integrations

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | Its S3 destination is a section. |
| [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | Its sending settings are a section. |
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) | settings/v1 is the contract; a host could provide it instead. |

## Example

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app with settings/v1: the standard extensions' admin settings (here pitr's) behind
// one API. `curl -H "Authorization: <superuser token>" http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/_c/settings/v1` lists them.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pitr"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/settings"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{settings.New(), pitr.New(pitr.Config{})}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates

# Templates

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Some extensions serve pages of their own, such as the OAuth sign-in, consent and MFA screens the CLI and MCP agents
sign in through. Templates lets you restyle them: eject an extension's templates into your app's `pb_templates`
folder and edit them. Any file you keep there replaces the built-in one; delete it to go back.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Templates is built into `pocketone` and on by default; there's nothing to install. In your own Go build:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{templates.New(templates.Config{})}, nil, nil)
```

## Configure

Nothing to configure. Your copies live in `pb_templates/` next to `pb_data` (in a Go build, `templates.Config.Dir`
moves it). `pocketone deploy` and `pocketone dev` sync it like `pb_hooks`.

## Use

See the template sets your app's extensions offer, and what you've changed:

```sh
pocketone template list
```

Eject one to edit it (leave out the name to eject every set):

```sh
pocketone template eject oauth
```

That copies every file of the set into `pb_templates/oauth/`. Edit any of them; the next request uses your copy, no
restart. Keep only the files you change if you like: the rest come from the built-in set.

Ejecting again is safe: files you haven't changed are left alone and missing ones are written back. Files you did
change are listed and only overwritten if you answer yes; without a terminal to ask in it refuses, and `--force`
overwrites them without asking.

The files are Go templates (`html/template`): `{{.AppName}}` prints a value (HTML-escaped), `{{if .Error}}…{{end}}`
and `{{range .Providers}}…{{end}}` branch and loop, and `{{template "head" .}}` includes another file of the set
(`head.tpl`). A broken file shows its error instead of the page, so you see what to fix.

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone template eject [set]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-template-eject) | Copies a template set (every set without a name) into pb\_templates/&lt;set&gt;/ for you to edit |
| [`pocketone template list`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-template-list) | Lists the template sets extensions offer, and what you've changed in pb\_templates |

## Integrations

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | Its OAuth pages are the `oauth` set: sign-in, MFA, one-time code, consent, device code, done and error, with a shared `head` and `foot`. Without Templates it serves them built in. |

### Building on Templates

An extension adds its own set through the [templates/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/templates/v1) contract: embed a
folder of `.tpl` files, add it under a name in `Register` (`templatesv1.Add(app, "mine", files)`), and render a page
with `templatesv1.Contract.Of(app)`'s `Render`. Declare templates/v1 in `WorksWith` and render the embedded set
yourself (`templatesv1.Parse`, `templatesv1.Write`) when nothing provides it.

## Example

A PocketBase app with one inline set, `hello`, served at `/hello`. Run `go run . template eject hello`, edit
`pb_templates/hello/page.tpl`, and reload.

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app with templates/v1 and one template set, "hello", served at /hello. Run
// `go run . template eject hello`, edit pb_templates/hello/page.tpl, and reload /hello.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"testing/fstest"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"

	templatesv1 "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/templates/v1"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/templates"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{templates.New(templates.Config{})}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	// an extension would go:embed its set; this one is inline
	templatesv1.Add(app, "hello", fstest.MapFS{"page.tpl": {Data: []byte(`<h1>Hello, {{.}}!</h1>`)}})
	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
		se.Router.GET("/hello", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
			return templatesv1.Contract.Must(app).Render(e, "hello", "page", http.StatusOK, "world")
		})
		return se.Next()
	})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens

# Tokens

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Long-lived API tokens for your app: secrets that start with `pbt_`, for CI, deploys, scripts and agents. Each token
belongs to an account and acts as that account. It can be limited to scopes, given an expiry, and revoked on its own.
Send one as `Authorization: Bearer pbt_…`. Ordinary PocketBase auth tokens keep working unchanged.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Tokens is built into `pocketone` and always on. There's nothing to install or turn on.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{})
app.Start()
```

To use `$tokens` in `pb_hooks`, bind it in jsvm's `OnInit` (the stock binary does):

```go
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { tokens.BindJS(app, rt) }})
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens`.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or environment variable for Tokens. In `pocketone`:
- any account (a superuser, or a record of any auth collection) can own tokens;
- a token never expires unless you give it an expiry.

A Go build can narrow both (see [Go config](#go-config)).

### Scopes

A token without scopes has its owner's full rights. A token with scopes works only on the requests its scopes cover,
plus remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`); anywhere else it gets `403`. Extensions and your own `pb_hooks` register the scopes. In
`pocketone` the built-in ones are:

| Scope | From | Allows | Who can hold it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deploy` | [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Deploy code (hooks, migrations, public files, packages), read files and logs | superusers |
| `deploy:read` | [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Read deployed files and stream logs | superusers |

`pocketone token scopes` lists every scope your app has, with its paths.

### Your own scopes

Declare a scope at the top level of a `pb_hooks` file. It then shows up in **Settings → API tokens** and on the
[the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) consent page:

```js
// pb_hooks/scopes.pb.js
$tokens.registerScope({
  name: 'notes:read',                        // lower-case letters, digits, ":" and "_"
  description: 'Read notes',                 // shown in the token screen and on the consent page
  paths: ['/api/collections/notes/records'], // URL prefixes where a token holding it works
  methods: ['GET'],                          // optional: only these methods (GET covers HEAD)
})
$tokens.registerScope({ name: 'notes:write', description: 'Change notes', paths: ['/api/collections/notes/records'] })
```

- `collections: ['users']` limits which accounts may hold the scope.
- Registering a name again merges its paths, methods and collections, so reloading hooks is safe.
- Two names whose headers would be the same (`notes:write` and `notes_write`) can't both be registered.

Check a scope on your own route:

```js
routerAdd('POST', '/api/notes/archive', (e) => { /* ... */ }, $apis.requireAuth(), $tokens.requireScope('notes:write'))
```

`$tokens.requireScope` refuses a signed-out request, and a token that doesn't hold the scope. Inside a handler,
`$tokens.hasScope(e, 'notes:write')` tells you the same.

Check a scope in a collection API rule. Every signed-in request carries `X-Token-Scope-<Name>: 1` for each scope it
holds, and rules read it as `@request.headers.x_token_scope_<name>` (`:` becomes `_`):

```
@request.auth.id = owner && @request.headers.x_token_scope_notes_write = "1"
```

- A PocketBase auth token or an unscoped API token holds every registered scope (except ones its collection can't
  hold).
- A scoped token holds only its own scopes. A signed-out request holds none.
- Headers a client sends with that prefix are always dropped, so they can't be forged.

`$tokens.ruleField('notes:write')` returns the rule field for a name, and `$tokens.scopes()` lists every registered
scope with its header and rule field.

## Use

### From the dashboard

1. Open **Settings → API tokens** (under **Access**). Only superusers see this screen.
2. Fill in a **Name**. Optionally set **Expires in (days)**, and tick any **Scopes** (none means full rights).
3. By default the token is yours. To make one for another account, fill in **Owner collection** (default
   `_superusers`) and **Owner (id or email)**.
4. Click **Create token**. Copy the token now: it's shown only once and never stored.

The list shows each token's name, its first characters, owner, scopes, expiry and when it was last used (time and IP).
Tokens issued by [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) carry an `oauth: <client id>` label. Click **Revoke** and
confirm to delete one; anything using it stops working at once.

App users who aren't superusers manage their own tokens through the [REST API](#rest-api).

### From the command line

The `token` command works on the local data dir, like `superuser`, so you can set up tokens before the first serve:

```bash
pocketone token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci --scope deploy --ttl 720h   # prints the secret
pocketone token create --collection users --record user@example.com --name script
pocketone token list                                    # every token, or one owner's with an owner flag
pocketone token revoke <id> [<id>...]
pocketone token revoke --all --superuser admin@example.com
pocketone token scopes
```

Pick the owner with `--superuser <email>`, or `--collection <name> --record <id or email>`. `--scope` can be repeated;
without `--ttl` the token never expires.

### Using a token

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer pbt_…" https://myapp.example.com/api/collections/notes/records
```

- An invalid, revoked or expired token leaves the request signed out, like an invalid PocketBase token.
- A scoped token used outside its scopes gets `403` ("This API token's scopes (…) don't allow this request.").
- A token can't be exchanged for a PocketBase auth token (`auth-refresh` and `impersonate` refuse it), so revoking a
  token really ends its access.
- Expired tokens are deleted once a day. Deleting an account deletes its tokens.

### In the logs

- A rejected token is logged at debug level: `tokens: rejected API token`.
- The daily cleanup logs `tokens: deleted expired tokens` with a count when it deletes any, and
  `tokens: delete expired` as a warning if it fails.

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone oauth clients add`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-oauth-clients-add) | Registers a client (prints its id, and its secret once for a confidential client) |
| [`pocketone oauth clients list`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-oauth-clients-list) | Lists registered clients |
| [`pocketone oauth clients rm <client_id>`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-oauth-clients-rm) | Removes a client |
| [`pocketone token create`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-token-create) | Creates an API token and prints its secret (shown once) |
| [`pocketone token list`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-token-list) | Lists API tokens (all, or one owner's) |
| [`pocketone token revoke [id...]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-token-revoke) | Revokes API tokens by id, or all of one owner's (--all) |
| [`pocketone token scopes`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-token-scopes) | Lists the scopes extensions registered |

### [oauth/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/oauth/v1)

Its HTTP API under `/api/_c/oauth/v1/`, as the contract describes.

### [tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tokens/v1)

Its HTTP API under `/api/_c/tokens/v1/`, as the contract describes.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | Its access tokens are API tokens, issued with the client's id, the granted scopes and, when asked for, an audience. They show up under Settings → API tokens and can be revoked there. The OAuth server needs Tokens on the app. |
| [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | An agent's OAuth sign-in to `/mcp` is an API token bound to `/mcp` that never expires; revoke it to disconnect the agent. Tool calls run as the token's owner. A full-access token's calls hold every registered scope; a token limited to scopes on the consent page has its calls checked like requests with those scopes (`WithScopes`). |
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Registers `deploy` and `deploy:read`; a `deploy` token is what CI uses. |
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | `pocketone login` takes a pasted API token when the remote has no OAuth server. In CI, put a token in `P1_TOKEN` (or `P1_TOKEN_<REMOTE>`). remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`) reports a token's id and scopes, whatever its scopes. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Add `tokens.New(tokens.Config{})` to the host's extensions and every instance gets its own tokens, routes and screen. Per instance, `extensions: {tokens: {enabled: false}}` turns it off and `collections: [...]` picks who may own tokens. The stock `pocketone` binary doesn't add it to pocker instances. |

### Building on Tokens

**Register a scope from Go.** Extensions register their scopes on the app, usually on bootstrap, and guard their routes:

```go
tk := tokens.For(app)
tk.MustRegisterScope(tokens.Scope{
    Name:        "notes:write",
    Description: "Change notes",
    Paths:       []string{"/api/collections/notes/records"},
    Methods:     []string{"POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"}, // optional
    Collections: []string{"users"},                   // optional: who may hold it
})
se.Router.POST("/api/notes/archive", h).Bind(apis.RequireAuth(), tokens.RequireScope("notes:write"))
```

- **Guards.** A Go scope can add `Match func(*core.RequestEvent) bool`: a token with the scope also works on any
  request it returns true for. It runs before the owner is loaded, so it may look only at the request.
- **Shared scopes.** Registering a name again merges its paths, methods, guards and collections, so several extensions
  can share one scope.
- **Read the token on a request.** `tokens.FromRequest(e)` returns the token a request used (nil for a PocketBase
  auth token), with its `Owner`, `Scopes` and `Audience`. `tokens.HasScope(e, "x")` is true for PocketBase auth
  tokens and unscoped API tokens.
- **Without importing this package.** Other extensions use the [tokens/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/tokens/v1/tokens.go)
  contract instead: `tokensv1.Contract.Of(app)` registers scopes (`RegisterScope`), lists them and checks `Reaches`;
  `tokensv1.FromRequest(e)` is the request's token (its `Grant`: owner, scopes, audience, client id);
  `tokensv1.WithScopes` limits in-process requests. Deploy and MCP work this way. The `X-Token-Scope-*` headers work
  for rules and JS.
- **Audience.** A token created with `CreateOptions.Audience` (the OAuth server sets it from the RFC 8707 `resource`
  parameter) only works under that URL's path, plus remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`); elsewhere it gets `403`. When the audience has
  a path (like `https://host/mcp`), the token works there whatever its scopes: the scopes limit what that endpoint
  does on the token's behalf (MCP passes them on with `WithScopes`), not the endpoint itself.
- **Limit in-process requests.** `tokens.WithScopes(ctx, scopes)` returns a context whose requests are checked like a
  token limited to `scopes`, whatever credential they carry: `403` where the scopes don't reach, and only those
  scopes in the `X-Token-Scope-*` headers and `HasScope`. Requests made inside them with the same context inherit
  the limit, and a nested `WithScopes` only narrows it. No client value can set it. `tokens.ScopesFromContext(ctx)`
  reads it. `Reaches(scopes, method, pattern)` says whether scopes could cover a route pattern (`{name}` segments
  match anything), and `Scope.Infrastructure()` whether a scope only reaches contract APIs (`/api/_c/`).

**Go API.** `tokens.For(app)` returns the service: `Create(owner, CreateOptions{Name, Scopes, Expires, ClientId,
Audience})` returns the secret and record; also `Verify(secret)`, `List(owner)`, `Get(id)`, `Revoke(id)`,
`RevokeAll(owner)`, `DeleteExpired()`, `RegisterScope`, `MustRegisterScope`, `Scopes()`, `Collections()` and
`AllowedCollection(c)`. `tokens.BindJS(vm, app)` adds `$tokens`; the extkit extension (`tokens.New`) also binds it.

**JS.** `$tokens.registerScope({name, description, paths, methods, collections})`, `$tokens.requireScope(name)`,
`$tokens.hasScope(e, name)`, `$tokens.ruleField(name)` and `$tokens.scopes()`.

### REST API (tokens/v1)

The [tokens/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/tokens/v1/tokens.go) contract, at `/api/_c/tokens/v1`. Any signed-in account; superusers
see and manage everyone's.

| Route | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/tokens/v1` | Your tokens. Superusers see all, or one owner's with `?ownerCollection=&owner=`. |
| `POST /api/_c/tokens/v1` | `{name, scopes, ttl \| expires}` (`ttl` in seconds, `expires` RFC 3339); superusers may add `ownerCollection` and `owner`. Returns the secret once. A scoped token can only create tokens within its own scopes. |
| `DELETE /api/_c/tokens/v1/{id}` | Revoke one. |
| `POST /api/_c/tokens/v1/revoke-all` | Revoke all of yours (superusers: `{ownerCollection, owner}`). |
| `GET /api/_c/tokens/v1/scopes` | The registered scopes, who may own tokens, and whether you can. |

Owners can also list, view and delete their own tokens through the records API of `_tokens`.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/tokens/example/main.go) runs one app with API tokens: Settings → API tokens, the token API (`/api/_c/tokens/v1`) and the `token` command.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app with API tokens: Settings → API tokens in the dashboard, the token API (/api/_c/tokens/v1)
// and the `token` command.
//
//	go run ./example serve
//	go run ./example token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci
//	curl -H "Authorization: Bearer pbt_..." http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/apis"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	tk := tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{
		Collections: []string{"_superusers", "users"}, // who may own tokens
	})
	// an extension's scope: a token limited to "hello" only authenticates under /api/hello; a JWT or unscoped token
	// holds it too, and every request that holds it carries X-Token-Scope-Hello: 1 for rules and hooks
	tk.MustRegisterScope(tokens.Scope{Name: "hello", Description: "Say hello", Paths: []string{"/api/hello"}, Methods: []string{"GET"}})

	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
		se.Router.GET("/api/hello", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
			return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"hello": e.Auth.Email()})
		}).Bind(apis.RequireAuth(), tokens.RequireScope("hello"))
		return se.Next()
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Go config

```go
tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{
    Collections: []string{"_superusers", "users"}, // who may own tokens (default: every auth collection)
    MaxTTL:      0,                                // cap on a token's lifetime (0: none)
})
```

With `MaxTTL` set, a token asked for with no expiry or a later one gets the cap instead. If you narrow `Collections`,
The OAuth server can only sign in accounts of those collections.

## How it works

- Tokens live in the `_tokens` collection: owner (collection id and record id), name, `hash` (SHA-256 of the secret;
  the secret itself is never stored), display prefix, scopes, expiry, last use (time and IP), OAuth client id and
  audience.
- The bearer check is a middleware that runs just before PocketBase's own auth middleware; a second one, right after
  it, sets the scope headers. Last use is written at most once a minute per token.
- [`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/tokens/example/main.go) runs one app where superusers and users may own tokens, with a `hello` scope
  for `GET /api/hello`. Try it with `go run ./example serve` and
  `go run ./example token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci` (logins from
  [devusers](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go): admin@example.com / password, user@example.com / password).
