# Vacuum

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

SQLite doesn't give space back to the disk when records are deleted; the file stays as big as it ever was. Vacuum
compacts your app's databases on a schedule (SQLite's `VACUUM`), so the space comes back. It only compacts a database
when enough of it is free space (10%, or 64 MB), so a busy, tidy app is left alone.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Vacuum is built into `pocketone`. In your own Go build:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{vacuum.New()}, nil, nil)
```

## Configure

The app's admins turn it on and set how often in the dashboard, in the **Vacuum** section at the bottom of
**Settings → Backups** (a settings/v1 section, so the CLI and agents can change it too). `pocketone.yaml` sets the
defaults until they do:

```yaml
vacuum:
  enabled: true
  every: 168h   # weekly; at least 1h
```

Without either, it's off.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `vacuum:`

Defaults for compacting the app's SQLite databases (VACUUM): on or off, and how often. The app's admins change them in Settings.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | Compact the databases on a schedule, until the app's admins change it in Settings. |
| `every` | string | `168h` | How often, e.g. 24h or 168h (weekly). |

## Use

Once on, every `every` while the app serves, Vacuum checks `data.db` and `auxiliary.db` and compacts the ones with
enough free space (PocketBase's own online `VACUUM`; writes wait while it runs). `VACUUM` needs free disk space about the
size of the database it compacts.

The same section shows its status: whether it's on, how often, the next run, and the last run's bytes given back and
databases skipped. It's [vacuum/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/vacuum/v1), also on the command line:

```sh
pocketone remote vacuum status
```

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### [vacuum/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/vacuum/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [status](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/vacuum/v1#status) | `pocketone remote vacuum status` | `GET /api/_c/vacuum/v1` | `vacuum_status` |

## Integrations

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings) | Its on/off and schedule are a settings/v1 section, in the dashboard, the CLI and for agents. |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | A host may compact its instances itself: when it provides [vacuum/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/vacuum/v1) for them, Vacuum steps aside in each instance: the Vacuum section shows the host's status, read-only, with no setting. |
| [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | A compacted database is a new file to Litestream, so the next replication starts a fresh generation. |

### Building on Vacuum

`vacuum.App(app)` compacts a running app now and returns what it did. `LoadSettings`/`SaveSettings` read and change the
app's settings.

## Example

A PocketBase app that compacts its databases once when it starts serving.

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app that compacts its databases once when it starts serving (vacuum.App), the work
// the extension does on its admins' schedule. Run `go run . serve` and watch the log for "vacuum: once".
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"

	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/vacuum"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{vacuum.New()}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(e *core.ServeEvent) error {
		go func() {
			run := vacuum.App(app)
			app.Logger().Info("vacuum: once", "saved_bytes", run.Saved, "skipped", run.Skipped, "error", run.Error)
		}()
		return e.Next()
	})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker

# Docker

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Run every instance on a host in its own container, with the official PocketBase or PocketOne binary of the version
the instance asks for. One host can serve PocketBase 0.23 and 0.36 and PocketOne side by side.

Docker is one of the two runtime providers of the multi-instance [multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite). The other is
[Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), which runs every instance inside one process. A host runs exactly one of them.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Docker is built into `pocketone`. It needs a Docker daemon on the same machine; nothing else to install.

It's off until `pocketone.yaml` names it as the provider (below). Then `pocketone serve` runs the host instead of a
single app.

In your own Go build, add it to the host's extensions; it provides the [runtime/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1)
contract when `pocketone.yaml` has a `docker` section:

```go
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath,
	Extensions: []multisite.Extension{&docker.Provider{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath}}})
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/docker`. Add `docker.NewCommand(...)` to your root command for the
`docker seed` and `docker update` commands.

## Configure

Add a `multisite` section (host mode) and a `docker` section to `pocketone.yaml`. Listeners (`server`), instances
(`instances`) and the firewall are the host's sections. With pocker linked too, both run: each instance on the one
its record names (`runtime: docker`), else the first that serves its version; `providers: { runtime/v1: [docker] }`
keeps docker alone.

```yaml
multisite: {}
docker:
  image: alpine:3.20                 # base image the binaries run in
  binaries: /var/lib/pocketbase      # release binary cache
  root: /var/lib/instances           # one folder per instance: <root>/<id>
  versions: ["pb:0.23", "pb:0.36", "p1:0.0"]
  default_version: "pb:0.36.*"
  idle_ttl: 10m
  max_concurrent_starts: 4
instances:
  file: ./instances.yaml
```

`image`, `binaries` and `root` are required.

**Versions.** An instance picks its binary with the prefix of its `version`: `pb:` is upstream PocketBase, `p1:` is
PocketOne, no prefix means `pb:`. `versions` lists the minors the host serves; the newest cached patch that matches
wins. A version that isn't listed gets a clear 503. Upstream PocketBase 0.22 and older are refused unless you lower
`min_upstream` and keep those releases in the cache yourself.

**Per instance** (`instances.yaml` or a mothership): `version`, `secrets` (passed as environment), `encryption_key`,
`dev`, and `dir` to put its folder somewhere other than `<root>/<id>`. An instance with `runtime` set to anything but
`docker` isn't served here.

**Limits and hardening** are optional: `nano_cpus`, `pids_limit`, `nofile`, `cap_drop` and `no_new_privileges`.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `docker:`

Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `socket` | string |  | The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. |
| `image` | string |  | Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. |
| `binaries` | string |  | Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. |
| `versions` | list of string |  | The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). |
| `root` | string |  | Folder with one folder per instance (<root>/<id>). Required. |
| `home` | string |  | The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. |
| `default_version` | string |  | Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0.*. Empty: such instances fail. |
| `min_upstream` | string |  | Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. |
| `idle_ttl` | duration |  | Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. |
| `max_concurrent_starts` | int |  | Containers starting at once. Default 4. |
| `start_timeout` | duration |  | How long a container gets to answer its health check. Default 60s. |
| `nano_cpus` | int |  | CPU limit per container in billionths of a CPU (1000000000 = one CPU). 0: no limit. |
| `pids_limit` | int |  | Process limit per container. 0: Docker's default. |
| `nofile` | list of int |  | Open-file limit per container: [soft, hard]. Empty: Docker's default. |
| `cap_drop` | list of string |  | Linux capabilities to drop, such as [ALL]. |
| `no_new_privileges` | bool |  | Set no-new-privileges on every container. |
| `network` | string |  | Docker network for the containers. Default the bridge. |
| `adopt_image` | string |  | Also adopt running unlabeled containers of this image named after an instance id (taking over from another manager). |

## Use

### Fetch the binaries

```bash
pocketone docker update   # find the latest patch of each docker.versions minor, record and download it
pocketone docker seed     # download whatever is recorded but not in the cache yet
```

`update` checks upstream PocketBase releases (ganigeorgiev.com, then the archived GitHub) and PocketOne releases on
GitHub, verifies each download against the release's checksums.txt, and records the list in the cache's
`releases.json`. Run it when you want new patches. Nothing is downloaded at request time: when the host starts, any
listed release missing from the cache is downloaded in the background.

The cache layout is `<binaries>/<version>/<platform>/pocketbase` for PocketBase (PocketHost's existing layout) and
`<binaries>/p1/<version>/<platform>/pocketone` for PocketOne.

### Run the host

```bash
pocketone serve
```

- A container starts on an instance's first request and is ready when `/api/health` answers. At most
  `max_concurrent_starts` start at once.
- It stops after `idle_ttl` without requests.
- It restarts on its next request when what it runs changed (secrets, version, mounts). A change to routing only
  doesn't restart it.
- It stops when the instance is deleted or moves to another edge.
- Containers keep running when the host restarts; the next process adopts them by their labels.

### Hooks and migrations

A change in an instance's `pb_hooks` restarts its container. PocketBase's own hooks watcher stays on too, so a hook
file that fails to load is logged and skipped instead of stopping the instance. A request that arrives while the
instance restarts waits for it instead of failing; one that lost its connection mid-restart is sent once more if
it's safe to repeat (GET, HEAD or OPTIONS without a body). Migrations run when a container boots.

### Maintenance

Instance folders are ordinary folders under `root`. To work on one while nothing has it open, a host's Go code calls
`WithInstanceStopped` (below); requests for that instance wait up to 30 s, then get a 503 with `Retry-After`.

### Remote control

Containers run stock images with no PocketOne extensions, so the host answers
[remote/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remote.go) for them at `/api/_c/remote/v1/` on each instance's hostname: the
`pocketone remote` commands work the same as against a Pocker instance or a single app. It answers after the host's
gates (firewall, rate limits) and blocked check, so a blocked instance's remote/v1 gets the blocked answer and the
container stays stopped.

- `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` (whoami) is public and lists `remote/v1`.
- `status`, `restart` and `logs` need a superuser token of that instance (`pocketone remote login` with a superuser
  email and password). The host asks the instance itself to check it.
- A host with its own accounts sets `docker.Provider.RemoteAuth` to decide who may call them instead (PocketHost: the
  instance owner's tokens). `remote/v1` is provided on the host's scope, so whoami also lists the other contracts the
  host provides for its instances (a host's `deploy/v1`).
- `restart` replaces the container; `logs` replays and follows the container's output, the last 1000 lines per
  instance kept by this host since it started following the container.

### Switching provider

Docker and Pocker both use `<root>/<id>`, so switching is a config change. Stop the containers first when leaving
docker, since they keep running across a host restart on purpose. Data only moves forward: an instance started on a
newer PocketBase than wrote its data is upgraded.

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone docker seed`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-docker-seed) | Downloads the releases docker.versions lists that the cache doesn't have yet |
| [`pocketone docker update`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-docker-update) | Finds the latest patch of each docker.versions minor, records and downloads it |

### [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [whoami](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1#whoami) | `pocketone remote whoami` | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` | `remote_whoami` |
| [status](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1#status) | `pocketone remote status` | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` | `remote_status` |
| [restart](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1#restart) | `pocketone remote restart` | `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` | `remote_restart` |
| [logs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1#logs) | `pocketone remote logs --n <n>` | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs` | `remote_logs` |

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Docker is a runtime provider of the host: the host routes by hostname, runs the listeners and gates, and hands each request to docker. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | The other provider. A host runs one or the other, over the same instance folders. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | For a fleet: requests for instances on another edge are forwarded there. |
| [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership) | Instances (and their versions) come from a mothership instead of a file. |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | Rate limits and allow lists in front of every instance. |
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | The host provides remote/v1 for every container, so the CLI's whoami, status, restart and logs work. |

### Building on Docker

- **`docker.Provider`** fields extend the provider from Go: `Container` adds mounts, environment and labels to each
  container; `Version` rewrites an instance's version before the binary is picked; `OnLog` receives container output
  (default: the debug log); `Versions` replaces the `versions` list (for example a fleet's list from a mothership);
  `MinUpstream` replaces `min_upstream`.
- **`Spec`** (what `Container` fills in): `Binds`, `Env`, `Labels`, plus `Cmd` to adjust the command (for example
  drop a flag an old release lacks) and `HealthPath` / `HealthAnyStatus` for the readiness check.
- **`VersionsSource`**: any type with `Releases(ctx)` decides which releases the host serves, each pinned to its
  download and sha256. `YAMLVersions` (the `versions` key) is the built-in one.
- **Runtime API**: `docker.New(docker.Config{...})` builds the runtime without the config file.
  `WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn)` stops an instance, holds its requests and runs `fn` on its folder (for deploys
  and restores); `StartInstance` starts one now; `InstanceDir` returns its folder. `Remote(host, dir)` and `SuperuserAuth()` are the
  remote/v1 provider and the host-side auth that `Provider` wires in, for a host built by hand
  (`remotev1.W.HostHandler(host, multisite.InstanceID, rt.SuperuserAuth(), next)` in `Host.InstanceRoutes`).
- **Release helpers**: `ParseVersion`, `Pick` / `PickMin`, `LatestPatches`, `Update` and `Seed` are what the commands
  use.

## Example

A minimal docker host: instances from a YAML file, each in its own container, routed by hostname on one listener. With
a Docker daemon running, start it from this folder with
`go run ./example --instances instances.yaml --data ./instances --binaries ./bin --versions pb:0.23,p1:0.0`.

```go
// A minimal docker host: instances from a YAML file, each in its own container with the PocketBase or PocketOne
// version it asks for, routed by hostname on one listener.
//
//	go run ./example --instances instances.yaml --data ./instances --binaries ./bin --versions pb:0.23,p1:0.0
//
// instances.yaml:
//
//	instances:
//	  - { id: blog, hosts: [blog.localhost], version: "pb:0.23.*" }
//	  - { id: shop, hosts: [shop.localhost], version: "p1:0.0.*" }
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"strings"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/docker"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/multisite"
)

func main() {
	instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file")
	data := flag.String("data", "./instances", "folder with one folder per instance")
	binaries := flag.String("binaries", "./bin", "PocketBase and PocketOne binary cache")
	versions := flag.String("versions", "pb:0.23,p1:0.0", "minors to serve (latest patch each; fetched at start)")
	image := flag.String("image", "alpine:3.20", "base image")
	listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address")
	flag.Parse()

	b := &docker.Binaries{Root: *binaries}
	tracked := strings.Split(*versions, ",")
	if err := docker.RunUpdate(context.Background(), os.Stdout, docker.DefaultDiscovery(), b, tracked); err != nil {
		slog.Error("versions", "error", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	rt, err := docker.New(docker.Config{Image: *image, DataRoot: *data, Binaries: b, Versions: docker.YAMLVersions{Tracked: tracked, Root: b.Root}})
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("docker", "error", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	h := &multisite.Host{Source: &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: *instances}, Runtimes: []multisite.Runtime{rt}, Listeners: multisite.Listeners{Listen: *listen}}
	if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil {
		slog.Error("host", "error", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Each instance folder is mounted at `/home/pockethost` and the binary read-only at `/home/pockethost/pocketbase`.
  The container runs `./pocketbase serve --http 0.0.0.0:8090`, plus `--dev` for dev instances and
  `--encryptionEnv=PB_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when the instance has an encryption key. Its secrets are its environment.
- The port is published on 127.0.0.1 and the host proxies to it. This is the layout PocketHost's Node edge uses, so
  its instance folders and binary cache move as they are.
- Every container carries labels: `p1.runtime`, `p1.instance`, `p1.version` (the resolved release, such as
  `pb:0.36.9`) and `p1.spec` (a hash of its configuration, used to tell when it must restart). `adopt_image` also
  adopts unlabeled containers of an image, for taking over from another manager.
- Docker is reached over its socket API directly; there's no Docker SDK dependency.

### Status

Tested against a real Docker daemon, with upstream PocketBase 0.23 and PocketOne 0.0.1 side by side, alone and as a
host's runtime. Not yet in production.

`go test ./...` runs the Docker tests when a daemon is reachable (they're skipped with `-short`). The first run
downloads an upstream release and a PocketOne release into the user cache.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge

# Edge

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

The fleet layer for a [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite): several servers (edges) share one set of instances, any edge accepts
any request, and a request for an instance another edge runs is forwarded there over the private network. Works with
either runtime provider, [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) or [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker).

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Edge is built into `pocketone`. It turns on in host mode (a `multisite` section in `pocketone.yaml`) when the file has an
`edges` section, or a `mothership` section ([Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership)), which lists the edges too.

In your own Go build, give the host a router as its forward hook:

```go
edges, err := edge.FromSection(log) // the `edges` section; nil when there is none
if edges != nil {
	opts.Forward = edge.NewRouter(edge.RouterConfig{Edges: edges, Logger: log}).Forward
}
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(opts)
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/edge`.

## Configure

The `edges` section names this edge and lists the others (keys below):

```yaml
edges:
  self: lax-1
  list:
    - { id: sgp-1, internal_url: "http://10.88.0.4:8080", region: sgp }
server:
  plain: [":8080"]   # where the other edges reach this one (their internal_url for it)
```

Each entry needs `id` and `internal_url`. An instance another edge runs names its owner in `remote`:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: shop
    hosts: [shop.example.com]
    remote: edge:@sgp-1     # also accepted: edge:sgp-1, or sgp-1
```

Without a mothership, instances come from the instances file. With one, instances and edges both come from it; a
fixed `edges.list` entry wins over the mothership's for the same edge.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `edges:`

The fleet: this edge's id and a fixed list of the other edges (id, internal_url, region).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `self` | string |  | This edge's id, such as lax-1. |
| `list` | list of object |  | The other edges: id, internal_url (where this edge reaches it) and optional region. |

## Use

There's nothing to run by hand. A load balancer sends visitors to any edge, and each request ends up on the edge that
runs its instance:

- **Owner healthy:** the request is forwarded to its `internal_url`, with the original hostname. An edge is healthy
  when its source heard from it in the last 30 seconds, or else when it answers `/.well-known/health` (an edge the
  source marks offline never is).
- **Owner briefly unreachable but healthy:** requests are held and retried every 250 ms until it answers. Only
  requests without a body (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) are replayed after a failed connection.
- **Owner down or unknown:** a 503 with `Retry-After: 10`, at once.
- **Never bounced:** a request another edge already forwarded is never forwarded again; it gets a 421.
- **CORS:** for an instance with `access.cors_origins`, the entry edge answers preflights and sets the only
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` the browser sees.
- **Headers:** where both edges set the same header (such as the firewall's rate-limit headers), the owner's wins.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Edge fills the host's forward hook for instances with `remote` set. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | Either runs the instances this edge owns; an app already running here stops when its instance moves to another edge. |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | The entry edge checks the peer and the instance's rate limits before forwarding. |
| [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership) | Its mirror is an edge source: it follows the mothership's list of edges and their heartbeats. |

### Building on Edge

- **Edge sources.** Implement `edge.EdgeSource` (`Self`, `Resolve`, `Edges`) to say where the other edges are; add
  `Run` (`edge.Runner`) for background work. `YAMLProvider` is the `edges.list` one; `MultiProvider` combines several,
  the first to resolve an instance's `remote` winning.
- **Router.** `edge.NewRouter(edge.RouterConfig{...})` takes the health path, healthy window, retry interval and the
  503 and 421 messages. Plug `Router.Forward` into `multisite.Host.Forward`.
- **Timing.** `edge.WithMark(ctx)` records which edge a request was forwarded to and when, e.g. for Server-Timing.

## Example

Edge has no example program of its own. The stock binary wires it up in
[`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/multi.go), together with the mothership's edge list.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall

# Firewall

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Peer allow-lists, trusted proxies and client IPs, and per-IP and per-instance rate limits for a
[Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite), with or without [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge). Every request is checked before an instance
serves it or it's forwarded to another edge.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The firewall is built into `pocketone`. It turns on in host mode (a `multisite` section in `pocketone.yaml`), as the host's [gate/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/gate/v1), when the file has
a `firewall` or `rate_limits` section; there's nothing else to install.

In your own Go build, importing the package registers it with the host, with the same rule:

```go
import _ "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/firewall"
```

Or build one in Go and add it to the host's gates, as [the example](#example) does.

A single app doesn't need it: stock PocketBase has its own per-IP rate limits and trusted proxies.

## Configure

Two sections, both optional; either one turns the firewall on (keys below).

```yaml
firewall:
  allow_cidrs: []                 # peers allowed to connect (empty = everyone)
  trusted_proxies: []             # peers whose client-IP headers are believed
  client_ip_headers: [CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP]
  trusted_clients: []             # client IPs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance
  trusted_client_headers: [X-Client-IP] # a trusted client names its end user: each user gets their own limits
  rate_limit_header_prefix: X-RateLimit
rate_limits:                      # defaults for every instance
  ip_hourly: 1000
  instance_hourly: 10000
  ip_concurrent: 15
  instance_concurrent: 250
  file_weight: 0.1                # a /api/files request costs a tenth
  trusted: { ip_hourly: 5000, instance_hourly: 20000, ip_concurrent: 50, instance_concurrent: 250 }
  # off: true                     # no rate limiting
```

The values shown are the defaults. In dev mode (`instances: { dev: true }`) rate limiting is off unless the file has a
`rate_limits` section. A trusted limit is never lower than the normal one.

Each instance can set its own limits and trusted IPs in its `extensions.firewall` settings; missing fields keep the
defaults:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: api
    hosts: [api.example.com]
    extensions:
      firewall: { rate_limits: { ip_hourly: 5000, instance_concurrent: 500 }, trusted_ips: [203.0.113.0/24] }
```

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `firewall:`

Peers allowed to connect, trusted proxies and client-IP headers, trusted clients, the rate-limit header prefix. Turns the firewall on.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_cidrs` | list of string |  | Peers (IPs or CIDRs) allowed to connect; others get 403. Empty: everyone. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of string |  | Peers whose client-IP headers are believed. |
| `client_ip_headers` | list of string |  | Headers read, in order, for the client IP from a trusted proxy. Default CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP. |
| `trusted_clients` | list of string |  | Client IPs or CIDRs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance. |
| `trusted_client_headers` | list of string |  | Headers a trusted client uses to name its end user's IP, so each user gets their own limits. Default X-Client-IP. |
| `rate_limit_header_prefix` | string |  | Prefix of the rate-limit response headers. Default X-RateLimit. |

#### `rate_limits:`

Default rate limits for every instance (per instance: extensions.firewall.rate_limits). Turns the firewall on.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour from one client IP to one instance. Default 1000. |
| `instance_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour to one instance from everyone. Default 10000. |
| `ip_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one client IP may have open on one instance at once. Default 15. |
| `instance_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one instance may have open at once. Default 250. |
| `file_weight` | number |  | What a /api/files request costs, as a share of a request. Default 0.1. |
| `trusted.ip_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour from one trusted client IP to one instance. |
| `trusted.instance_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour to one instance. |
| `trusted.ip_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one trusted client IP may have open on one instance at once. |
| `trusted.instance_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one instance may have open at once. |
| `off` | bool |  | No rate limiting. The default in dev mode unless rate_limits is set. |

## Use

What callers see:

- **Peers outside `allow_cidrs`** get 403.
- **Client IP:** taken from `client_ip_headers` only when the peer is a trusted proxy; otherwise it's the peer. The
  app then sees that client as the request's IP, so PocketBase's logs and its own rate limits see the visitor.
- **Over a limit:** 429 with `Retry-After` and a message naming the limit and the IP.
- **Every routed response** carries `X-RateLimit-{Ip,Instance}-{Hourly,Concurrent}-{Limit,Remaining}` and
  `X-RateLimit-{Ip,Instance}-Hourly-Reset` (with your prefix), listed in `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` so browser
  code can read them.
- **Long-lived responses** (realtime) count toward the concurrency limits until they end.

### Trusted clients that serve many users

A trusted client (process-wide `trusted_clients`, or an instance's own `trusted_ips`) that serves many users, such as
a server-side proxy or SSR app, sends each request's end-user IP in a `trusted_client_headers` header. Per-IP limits
then apply to that user, still with the trusted limits; without the header all its users share one bucket. The header
is ignored from anyone else, so it can't be spoofed to escape a limit.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | The firewall is a host gate: it checks the peer, then admits each request before the runtime or the forward hook. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | Either provider; the firewall runs in front of both. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | The entry edge applies the limits before forwarding. The owner edge's rate-limit headers replace the entry edge's, since the owner counted every request for the instance. |
| [Multitenant](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants) (planned) | Will write each instance's `extensions.firewall` settings, such as its owner's trusted IPs. |

### Building on the firewall

- **Per instance.** Write `extensions.firewall.rate_limits` and `extensions.firewall.trusted_ips` into an instance's
  settings (from the instances file or your own instance source).
- **Go API.** `firewall.Firewall{Config, RateLimits}` is a `multisite.Gate` you can add to `Host.Gates` yourself;
  `NewFirewall(cfg)` builds one ready to use. `ClientIP(r)` gives a request's client. `firewall.SectionAdjust` changes
  the settings read from `pocketone.yaml` before the firewall is built.

## Example

The firewall in front of a toy host: only `127.0.0.1` may connect, at 100 requests an hour per IP. Run it from this
folder with `go run ./example --instances instances.yaml`.

```go
// The firewall in front of a host: every request is checked (allowed peers, rate limits) before a toy runtime
// answers. In a PocketOne binary the firewall turns on from pocketone.yaml's firewall / rate_limits sections; here
// it is built in Go.
//
//	go run ./example --instances instances.yaml
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/multisite"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/firewall"
)

type okRuntime struct{}

func (okRuntime) Name() string                        { return "ok" }
func (okRuntime) Serves(inst multisite.Instance) bool { return true }
func (okRuntime) Ready() bool                         { return true }
func (okRuntime) ServeInstance(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, inst multisite.Instance) {
	fmt.Fprintf(w, "hello from %s\n", inst.ID)
}

func main() {
	instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file")
	listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address")
	flag.Parse()
	fw := &firewall.Firewall{
		Config:     firewall.Config{AllowCIDRs: []string{"127.0.0.1"}},
		RateLimits: &firewall.RateLimits{IPHourly: 100},
	}
	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	h := &multisite.Host{Source: &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: *instances}, Runtimes: []multisite.Runtime{okRuntime{}}, Gates: []multisite.Gate{fw}, Listeners: multisite.Listeners{Listen: *listen}}
	if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
```

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership

# Mothership

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A control plane for a fleet of edges. The mothership is a PocketOne app that records which edges exist and which
instances run where. Each edge follows it, serves its own instances and forwards requests for the rest to the edge
that runs them.

One operator, no users: owners and accounts are the [tenants](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants) extension (planned), which extends the
mothership through its collections and the mirror's extensions. Each layer is optional: an [edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge)
runs without a mothership, and a mothership without tenants.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The edge side (the `mirror` package) is built into `pocketone`. It turns on when `pocketone.yaml` names a provider
and has a `mothership` section (below); `pocketone serve` then takes its instances and the other edges from the
mothership.

The mothership side has no switch yet. In the Go code of the PocketOne app that will be the mothership, create its
collections once the app has bootstrapped:

```go
if err := mothership.EnsureCollections(app); err != nil {
	return err
}
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mothership`. In your own edge build, `mirror.FromSection(log)`
returns the mirror for the config (nil without a `mothership` section); use it as the host's instance source and the
router's edge source, as [`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/multi.go) does.

## Configure

On each edge, add a `mothership` section to the host's config; the mirror becomes the host's [instance.source/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.source/v1). Logins come from the private `.env`:

```yaml
multisite: {}
mothership:
  url: http://10.88.0.10:8090
  email: $MOTHERSHIP_EMAIL
  password: $MOTHERSHIP_PASSWORD
  self: lax-1                       # this edge's edge_id (or edges.self)
  internal_url: http://10.88.0.5:8080
  region: lax
  apex: example.com                 # <name>.example.com routes to each instance
```

`url` and `self` are required. The edge logs in as a superuser of the mothership.

On the mothership, there's nothing to configure beyond creating the collections.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `mothership:`

A community mothership to mirror instances and edges from: url, login, this edge's id, internal URL, region, apex.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string |  | The mothership's URL. Required. |
| `email` | string |  | Superuser email this edge logs in with; use a $VAR from the .env. |
| `password` | string |  | Superuser password; use a $VAR from the .env. |
| `self` | string |  | This edge's edge_id, such as lax-1. Default: the edges section's self. Required. |
| `internal_url` | string |  | Where other edges reach this one. Set: the edge registers itself when the mothership has no record for it. |
| `region` | string |  | Region recorded when the edge registers itself. |
| `apex` | string |  | Makes <name>.<apex> a hostname of every instance. Empty: hosts only. |
| `heartbeat` | duration |  | How often this edge marks itself online. Default 15s; negative: never. |
| `resync` | duration |  | How often everything is reloaded, in case a change was missed. Default 10m. |

## Use

You manage the fleet in the mothership's dashboard, in two collections only superusers can read or write:

- **`edges`**: `edge_id` (such as `lax-1`), `internal_url`, `region`, `status` (`online`, `draining`, `offline`) and
  `last_seen`. An edge with `internal_url` set registers itself when it has no record, marks itself online every
  15 s, and offline when it shuts down.
- **`instances`**: `name` (`<name>.<apex>` routes to it), `hosts` (extra hostnames), `edge` (where it runs),
  `power` (off answers 409 "instance is powered off"), `suspension` (non-empty answers 403 with that message), `dev`,
  `version`, `secrets`, `encryption_key`, `access`, `limits`, `plugins` (extension settings; the field keeps its old name) and `status`.

Changes reach the edges within moments over PocketBase's realtime stream; there's no polling. To move an instance,
change its `edge`: the old edge drops its full record and forwards to the new one until the new edge has it. An
instance with no `edge` isn't served anywhere.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | The mirror is the host's instance source: which instances exist and which this edge runs. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | The mirror is also an edge source: where the other edges are, so requests for their instances are forwarded. It combines with a fixed `edges` list. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) and [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Run the instances this edge owns, with the version, secrets, limits and extension settings from each record. |
| [Tenants](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants) (planned) | Adds owners and accounts through mirror extensions. |

### Building on Mothership

- **Your own fields and collections.** `EnsureCollections` leaves fields an extension added alone, so an extension can add
  its own fields and collections to the mothership.
- **Mirror extensions.** Pass a `mirror.Extension` to `mirror.FromSection` or `mirror.Config.Extensions`. `Views()`
  adds filtered subscriptions (such as `owners` filtered to `instances_via_owner.edge ?= {edge}`), `Instance()`
  adjusts each instance as it's built (block a suspended owner's instances, add an owner's trusted IPs), and
  `Changed()` names the instances a change in its views affects.
- **Go API.** `mirror.New(mirror.Config{...})` builds a mirror without the config file. `Get(view, id)` and
  `Records(view)` read any view; `SelfRecord()` is this edge's record id.

## Example

There's no `example/main.go` yet. The stock binary's multi-instance mode,
[`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/multi.go), follows a mothership when the config has the
section.

## How it works

Each edge subscribes to filtered views, so it only receives what concerns it:

| View | Collection | Filter / fields | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edges` | edges | all | forwarding, and health from heartbeats |
| `routes` | instances | fields `id,name,hosts,edge,updated` | the routing table: any edge may get any visitor |
| `local` | instances | `edge = <this edge>` | full records (secrets, limits, plugins) for instances this edge runs |

An instance moving away shows up in `routes` and its full record is dropped; one moving here arrives in `local`. The
stream reconnects and reloads on its own, and reloads everything every 10 minutes in case anything was missed.

Filters cut what each edge downloads and keeps (most edges run a few of thousands of instances). They are not a
security boundary while edges log in as superusers.

### Status

Early. Built: the `edges` and `instances` collections (`EnsureCollections`) and the edge side (`mirror`). Not yet:
the mothership's own endpoints (placement, moves) and instance status reports.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite

# Multisite

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Many PocketOne instances behind one listener, routed by hostname. Each request's hostname picks an instance, the
request passes the gates (such as the [firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall)), and a runtime serves it:
[pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) runs instances in-process, [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) runs each in its own container,
and a host can run both. Everything a host plugs in is a host-scope contract: [runtime/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1),
[gate/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/gate/v1), [tls/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tls/v1),
[http.wrap/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/http.wrap/v1) and [instance.source/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.source/v1).

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Multisite is built into `pocketone`. It takes over `serve` when `pocketone.yaml` has a `multisite` section; without
one, `pocketone serve` runs a single app as usual.

```yaml
multisite: {}
providers:
  runtime/v1: [pocker, docker]   # optional: which runtimes, in preference order (default: every configured one)
```

In your own Go build, pass the host extensions you link (runtimes in preference order), build the host from the
config and run it. [`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/multi.go) is the stock binary's version:

```go
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath, Choices: providersSection,
	Extensions: []multisite.Extension{servertiming.New(), autotls.New(), &pocker.Provider{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath}}})
if errors.Is(err, multisite.ErrNoProvider) {
	// no multisite section in pocketone.yaml: serve a single app instead
}
err = h.Run(ctx)
```

At startup the host logs who provides each host contract, e.g. `multisite: runtime/v1 ← pocker, docker`.

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/multisite`.

## Configure

A host reads these `pocketone.yaml` sections:

```yaml
multisite: {}                        # host mode
server:
  https: ":443"                      # the main address
  http: ":80"                        # redirects to https (alone: serves plain HTTP)
  plain: [":8080"]                   # extra plain-HTTP addresses, no redirect (e.g. a private network)
  tls: { cert: cert.pem, key: key.pem }   # reloaded when the files change; or the autotls section
instances:
  file: ./instances.yaml             # where the instances come from
  dev: false                         # also serve unknown hostnames
pocker: { root: ./pb_root }          # a runtime's own section (pocker; docker only runs with its section)
firewall: { allow_cidrs: [10.0.0.0/8] }  # any gate's section turns that gate on
```

- `server` belongs to [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config); `providers` is the contracts' section. With no `https` or `http`, the host listens on
  `127.0.0.1:8090`.
- The `instances` section is this extension's (keys below). In production the instances file is required; with
  `dev: true` it's optional.
- The `app` section is for a single app and is refused on a multisite host: each instance has its own folder under its
  runtime's root.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `instances:`

Where a multi-instance host's instances come from (a YAML file), and dev mode (serve unknown hostnames).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | `instances.yaml` | The instances file (id, hosts and settings for each instance), reloaded when it changes. |
| `dev` | bool |  | Also serve unknown hostnames: each becomes an instance named after it, in dev mode, with its folder made on first use. |

#### `multisite:`

Serve many instances (a multisite host) instead of a single app. The runtimes are the providers of runtime/v1.

## Use

### The instances file

```yaml
instances:
  - id: blog                         # also the folder name: <root>/blog
    hosts: [blog.example.com, www.blog.example.com]
  - id: shop
    hosts: [shop.example.com]
    secrets: { STRIPE_KEY: sk_live_... }               # the app's environment, seen by its JS hooks
    encryption_key: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef   # encrypts the app's stored settings
    access: { cors_origins: [https://shop.example.com] }
    limits: { max_js_execution: 60s }                  # over the runtime's defaults
    extensions: { firewall: { trusted_ips: [203.0.113.0/24] } }   # settings for extensions, by name
  - id: old
    hosts: [old.example.com]
    blocked: { status: 402, message: "Payment required" }
```

The file is checked for changes every 2 seconds; edits apply without restarting the host. Ids are lowercase
letters, digits, dots and dashes. Other fields: `version` and `runtime` (which release or runtime runs it), `dir`
(another folder), `dev`, `superusers` (pocker upserts them when the app starts), `private` (for host Go code, never seen by JS) and `remote`
(another server runs it).

### What a request gets

- A hostname no instance maps gets 404, and no folder is created. In dev mode it becomes a new instance named after
  the hostname, in dev mode.
- A `blocked` instance answers every request with its status and message.
- An instance with `remote` set is forwarded there after the gates (a plain proxy to the URL, or
  [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) for a fleet).
- Contracts the host provides for its instances (docker's remote/v1) answer after the gates and the blocked check,
  so the firewall, rate limits and a powered-off answer apply to them too.
- `GET /.well-known/health` on any hostname reports the host's status, how many instances it knows and how many are
  running.

### Switching runtime

Switching between pocker and docker is a config change (`providers: { runtime/v1: [docker] }`, or an instance's own
`runtime: docker`): both keep instances in `<root>/<id>`. Stop the containers
first when leaving docker (they keep running across a host restart on purpose). Data only moves forward: an instance
started on a newer version than wrote its data is upgraded.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | runtime/v1: every instance runs in this process. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | runtime/v1: each instance runs in its own container (with a `docker` section). |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | A gate: peer allow-list, client IPs and rate limits. On when the config has `firewall` or `rate_limits`. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | Forwards requests for instances another edge runs (the `edges` section). |
| [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership) | Its mirror is instance.source/v1 instead of the instances file, and lists the other edges. |
| [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls) | Certificates for the main listener, issued for the hostnames instances map. |
| [Stats](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/stats) | Measures disk use and last request for each instance. |
| [Server Timing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/servertiming) | Server-Timing headers for each step of a request. |

### Building on Host

- **Host extensions.** A `multisite.Extension` (`Name`, `RegisterHost(h)`) provides host-scope contracts on `h.Scope`:
  a runtime (`runtimev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, rt)`), a gate, TLS, a wrapper, an instance source. It provides
  nothing when it isn't configured (no section). Pass it in `Options.Extensions`, or `multisite.Link` it from an
  `init` so linking the package is enough (the firewall does). By hand: `h.Use(exts...)`, then `h.Setup(choices)`.
- **Runtime.** `runtimev1.Runtime` (`Name`, `Serves`, `ServeInstance`, `Ready`), with optional `Prechecker`, `Syncer`,
  `Starter`, `Statser` and `Shutdowner`. Each instance runs on the runtime it names, else the first that serves it.
- **Instance source.** `sourcev1.Source` (`Snapshot`, `Watch`) feeds instances from anywhere, such as a control plane.
  The instances file (`YAMLSource`) is the default and steps aside for any other provider.
- **Gates.** A `gatev1.Gate` checks the peer (`AllowPeer`) and admits each request (`Admit`); `ClientIPResolver`
  passes the real client IP on to the app. Gates set on `h.Gates` directly run after the contract's.
- **Forwarding.** `multisite.Options.Forward` serves requests for instances with `remote` set (Edge fills it).
- **Instance routes.** `Host.InstanceRoutes` wrap the runtime for instances this host runs: they run after the
  peer check, the blocked answer and the gates, and before the runtime (never for forwarded instances).
  `multisite.InstanceOf(r)` is the resolved instance and `multisite.InstanceID` fits extkit's host handlers, so a
  contract the host provides for its instances goes here:

  ```go
  remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(h.Scope, myRemote)
  h.InstanceRoutes = append(h.InstanceRoutes, func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
  	return remotev1.W.HostHandler(h.Scope, multisite.InstanceID, myAuth, next)
  })
  ```
- **Listeners and wrappers.** tls/v1 (or `Host.TLS`) sets the listener's TLS, http.wrap/v1 providers wrap the whole
  handler (outside `Host.Wrappers`), and `Host.Background` runs jobs until shutdown.
- **Per-instance settings.** An extension reads its own `extensions.<name>` with `inst.ExtensionConfig(name)` and
  `multisite.DecodeExtensionConfig`.

## Example

A toy host: instances from a YAML file, served by a runtime that answers with the instance it resolved. Run it from
this folder with `go run ./example --instances instances.yaml`, then `curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' localhost:8090/`.

```go
// A minimal host: instances from a YAML file, routed by hostname, served by a toy runtime that answers with the
// instance it resolved. Real hosts plug in a provider instead (ext/pocker in-process, ext/docker in containers).
//
//	go run ./example --instances instances.yaml
//	curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' localhost:8090/
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/multisite"
)

type echoRuntime struct{}

func (echoRuntime) Name() string                        { return "echo" }
func (echoRuntime) Serves(inst multisite.Instance) bool { return true }
func (echoRuntime) Ready() bool                         { return true }
func (echoRuntime) ServeInstance(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, inst multisite.Instance) {
	fmt.Fprintf(w, "instance %s (%s%s)\n", inst.ID, r.Host, r.URL.Path)
}

func main() {
	instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file: instances: [{id: blog, hosts: [blog.localhost]}]")
	listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address")
	flag.Parse()
	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	h := &multisite.Host{Source: &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: *instances}, Runtimes: []multisite.Runtime{echoRuntime{}}, Listeners: multisite.Listeners{Listen: *listen}}
	if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
```

## How it works

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Instance`, `InstanceSource`, `YAMLSource` | The instance record (instance.source/v1) and where instances come from. |
| `Directory` | Instances by hostname and id, kept current from the source. |
| `Handler` | Health path, peer check, hostname, blocked, then remote (the `Forward` hook) or local (the instance routes, then the runtime), with the gates. |
| `Runtime` | runtime/v1: what runs instances. One or more per host, in preference order. |
| `Gate`, `ChainGates`, `HostGate` | Request gates (gate/v1). |
| `Extension`, `Link`, `Host.Use`, `Host.Setup` | Host extensions and the host's contract scope. |
| `Serve`, `TLSProvider` | Listeners: plain, TLS (a provider such as autotls, or cert files reloaded on change), redirect, graceful shutdown. |
| `Host`, `FromConfig` | All of the above assembled, by hand or from `pocketone.yaml`. |

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker

# Pocker

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Many PocketOne instances in one process (like Docker, but for PocketOne), routed by hostname. Each instance is a
normal app folder and starts on its first request, in tens of milliseconds. Pocker provides
[runtime/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1) for [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite); its peer [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) runs each instance in a container instead.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Pocker is built into `pocketone`. Add a `multisite` section to `pocketone.yaml` and `pocketone serve` hosts many
instances instead of one app, with pocker as the runtime (docker too, when it has its `docker` section):

```yaml
multisite: {}
```

In your own Go build, add it to the host's extensions ([`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/multi.go)
is the stock binary's version), or run a `pocker.Server` on its own as [the example](#example) does:

```go
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath, Extensions: []multisite.Extension{
	&pocker.Provider{
		Resolve:  cfg.ResolvePath,
		Standard: standard.New(), // every instance gets the standard set (tokens, mcp, pitr, ...)
		Extensions: []pocker.Extension{
			myextension.New(), // your own PocketOne extensions, on every instance too
		},
	},
}})
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pocker`.

## Configure

The `pocker` section sets where instances live, the JS pool, outbound network and the default limits for every
instance (keys below). Listeners, instances and the firewall are the [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) sections (`server`,
`instances`, `firewall`).

```yaml
multisite: {}
instances: { file: ./instances.yaml }
pocker:
  root: ./pb_root           # one folder per instance: <root>/<id>
  hooks_pool_size: 2
  egress_allow: []          # private networks instances may still reach
  max_js_execution: 30s     # default limits; each instance can override them
  max_js_allocation: 64MiB
```

An instance overrides any limit in its own `limits` (missing fields keep the default):

```yaml
instances:
  - id: shop
    hosts: [shop.example.com]
    limits: { max_js_execution: 60s, max_concurrent_js: 32 }
```

Every instance runs the PocketOne code in the binary; an instance's `version` is ignored.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `pocker:`

Runtime provider pocker: instances run in-process (root folder, hooks pool, egress allow list, instance limit defaults).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | string | `./pb_root` | The folder holding one folder per instance: <root>/<id>. |
| `hooks_pool_size` | int | `2` | Ignored: each instance has one JS VM (ext/jsvm). Kept so existing configs load. |
| `max_js_execution` | duration | `30s` | Longest any single JS call (hook, route, cron job, migration) may run. |
| `max_js_allocation` | int | `67108864` | Largest result a JS built-in may allocate in one step, such as 64MiB. |
| `max_call_stack_size` | int | `2000` | Deepest JS recursion allowed. |
| `max_sleep` | duration | `10s` | Longest a JS sleep() call may wait. |
| `max_query_duration` | duration | `30s` | Longest an SQL statement without its own deadline may run. |
| `http_send_max_timeout` | duration | `1m0s` | Longest timeout a JS $http.send call may use. |
| `http_send_max_body` | int | `10485760` | Largest response body a JS $http.send call may read, such as 10MiB. |
| `max_concurrent_js` | int | `16` | JS calls an instance runs at once; more wait up to max_js_execution, then fail. |
| `egress_allow` | list of string |  | Private networks (CIDRs) instances may still connect to. Default none: public addresses only. |

## Use

### Try it with any hostname

```yaml
# pocketone.yaml
server: { http: "127.0.0.1:8090" }
multisite: {}
instances: { dev: true }
pocker: { root: ./pb_root }
```

```sh
pocketone serve
curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health   # creates and serves ./pb_root/blog.localhost
```

In dev mode a hostname no instance maps becomes an instance named after it, its folder is made on first use, and it
runs in dev mode. In production only the hostnames in the instances file are served (see
[Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite#the-instances-file)).

### Each instance

- A normal app folder, `<root>/<id>`: `pb_data`, `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations`, `pb_public`. Its dashboard is at
  `https://<its hostname>/_/`.
- Its JS hooks see only its own `secrets`, through `$os.getenv` and `process.env`.
- A change to its `secrets`, `encryption_key`, `access`, `limits`, `dev`, `dir`, `superusers`, `private`, `extensions` or `remote`
  restarts it if it's running (the app stops, then a fresh one starts, as in a process restart). A hostname change doesn't restart it.
- A change in `pb_hooks` restarts just that instance. A broken hooks file affects only that instance (below).

### Broken hook files

In dev mode, a `pb_hooks` file that fails to load is logged and skipped, and the rest of the instance runs, so you can
fix it live. Otherwise an instance doesn't start with a broken file.

When a running instance's `pb_hooks` change, Pocker restarts it as PocketBase's watcher restarts a process: the running
app stops (requests in flight are cut off), then a fresh app starts with the new files. Only one app has an instance's
folder open at a time, so migrations and bootstrap code never run beside a live app. A broken file in production
leaves the instance down: requests get 502 with the error, which also goes to the instance log, and the first request
after a fix starts it.

### Logs

The app's own logs (the dashboard's Logs) are per instance, in its `pb_data`. `console.*` from JS hooks goes to
`<instance>/logs/exec.log` as JSON lines (`message`, `stream`, `time`), rotated to `exec.log.1` at 10 MiB. A start
failure is written there too.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Routing, listeners, instances file and gates. Pocker is one of its runtimes (runtime/v1). |
| [Sandbox](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox) | Every instance's JS hooks, SQL and outbound network run in it, so one instance can't reach another or the host. |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | Peer allow-list and rate limits in front of every instance; per-instance limits in `extensions.firewall`. |
| [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls) | In the stock binary: certificates for the hostnames instances map (`autotls` section). |
| [Server Timing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/servertiming) | In the stock binary: Server-Timing headers on every response. |
| [Mailtrap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap) | In the stock binary: dev instances with SMTP off send mail to a local inbox. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | Instances another edge runs are forwarded there instead of started here. |
| [Stats](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/stats) | Measures disk use and last request for each instance under `root`. |
| PocketOne extensions | In your own build, any extension such as [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr), [S3 Fallback](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback) or [Mail Relay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay) runs on every instance, and an instance's `extensions.<name>` settings override the extension's defaults. `enabled: false` turns it off for that instance. |

### Building on Pocker

- **Standard set (required).** `pocker.Provider.Standard` (or `pocker.Server.Standard`, `ManagerOptions.Standard`) is
  [ext/standard](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard)'s set, and Pocker won't start an instance without it: a server without one
  refuses to run, so no host can make an instance that lacks the standard extensions. Every instance gets its members, each turned off per instance with `extensions.<name>.enabled: false`, and its
  startup lines (`standard: on: ...`) are in the instance's own log. Listing a member in `Extensions` too is an error.
- **Contracts the host provides.** `Server.Host` (or `Provider.Host`) is the host's contract scope. A contract the
  host provides for its instances steps aside inside each instance's app, and the host answers it on the instance's
  hostname in `Server.InstanceRoutes` (or `Provider.InstanceRoutes`, `ManagerOptions.InstanceRoutes`): after the
  gates and the blocked answer, before the app. `pocker.Remote(m, host)` is remote/v1 for Pocker instances (restart
  through the Manager, logs from `logs/exec.log`); add your own auth:

  ```go
  host := extkit.NewScope("multisite")
  srv.Host = host
  srv.OnStart = func(m *pocker.Manager) { remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, pocker.Remote(m, host)) }
  srv.InstanceRoutes = append(srv.InstanceRoutes, func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
  	return remotev1.W.HostHandler(host, multisite.InstanceID, myAuth, next)
  })
  ```

  deploy/v1 works the same way with `deploy.New(...)` as the handler: `deployv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host,
  ...)` and `extkit.HostRoutes(host, deployv1.Contract, multisite.InstanceID, next)` as an instance route.
- **Extensions.** `pocker.Provider.Extensions` (or `pocker.Server.Extensions`) takes any `extkit.Extension`, registered on each
  instance's app before it starts with that instance's `extensions.<name>` settings. Host-level code can implement
  `AppIniter`, `JSIniter`, `Starter`, or be a host extension (`multisite.Extension`, registered on the host like any
  other: servertiming, autotls). See
  [POCKER.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker/pocker#extensions).
- **Setup per instance.** `SetupApp(inst, app)` runs after migrations and before the app serves, e.g. to add a route
  checked against `inst.Private`.
- **Manager.** `OnStart` hands host code the `Manager`: `WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn)` changes an instance's files
  while it's stopped (deploys, restores), `StartInstance`, `Running`, `InstanceDir`, `LogInstance`.
- **Restarts.** `app.Restart()` (a backup restore, PITR) restarts only that instance.

## Example

A Pocker build with one extension: a Go route and an admin dashboard page on every instance, in dev mode. Run it from
this folder with `go run ./example`, then open `http://blog.localhost:8090/_/` (login `admin@example.com` /
`password`).

```go
// Command pocker-extension is a Pocker build with one extension: a Go route and an admin dashboard page,
// added to every instance. See docs/extensions.md.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"io/fs"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/apis"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pocker"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/standard"
)

//go:embed ui
var uiFiles embed.FS

func main() {
	cfg := pocker.DefaultConfig()
	cfg.Dev = true // any hostname; drop this for production (instances.yaml required)

	ui, _ := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui")

	srv := &pocker.Server{
		Config:   cfg,
		Standard: standard.New(), // every instance gets the standard extensions (tokens, mcp, pages, pitr, ...)
		// Runs for every instance's app after its migrations, before it serves.
		SetupApp: func(inst pocker.Instance, app core.App) error {
			// local testing: every instance gets superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"
			if err := devusers.Ensure(app); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
				// a Go route, superuser only
				se.Router.GET("/api/hello", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
					return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"instance": inst.ID})
				}).Bind(apis.RequireSuperuserAuth())

				// an admin dashboard extension: ui/main.js is loaded by the dashboard before its router starts
				se.UIExtensions = append(se.UIExtensions, core.UIExtension{Name: "hello", FS: ui})
				return se.Next()
			})
			return nil
		},
	}

	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)
	defer stop()
	if err := srv.Run(ctx); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Untrusted instances

Pocker runs every instance's JS hooks in the [sandbox](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox). For why that's safe enough to host code
from people you don't know, and where it isn't, see [How is this safe?](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox#how-is-this-safe).
Memory is the main limit: only one-shot allocations are capped, so a hook that grows memory slowly affects the whole
process. [POCKER.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker/pocker#sandbox) lists what the sandbox covers.

## Reference

[POCKER.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker/pocker) is the full guide: production `pocketone.yaml`, every instance field, extension interfaces, the
sandbox, PocketBase changes and versions.

MIT
