# Bundle

Version 0.1.0 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Ship an app's files inside the binary instead of folders on disk: its JS hooks (`pb_hooks`), migrations
(`pb_migrations`) and public files (`pb_public`). Nothing is written to disk and nothing on disk can override them.
PocketHost's mothership uses it for its own hooks. Formerly `jsembed`.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Bundle is not in the `pocketone` binary. Add it to your own Go build: embed the folders, pass the hooks and migrations
to [jsvm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm) as extensions, and serve the public files.

```go
//go:embed hooks migrations public
var files embed.FS

hooks, _ := fs.Sub(files, "hooks")
migrations, _ := fs.Sub(files, "migrations")
public, _ := fs.Sub(files, "public")
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
	Extensions: []any{bundle.Hooks(hooks), bundle.Migrations(migrations)},
})
bundle.Public(app, public, true)
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bundle`.

## Configure

Nothing to configure. List only what you bundle: without `bundle.Hooks`, hooks still come from `HooksDir` on disk,
and the same for migrations.

## Use

- **Hooks:** `.pb.js` files come from the FS's root only. `HooksDir` is ignored, nothing is written to it, and hooks
  aren't watched.
- **Migrations:** files come from the FS's root only; `MigrationsDir` is ignored.
- **`require()`:** `__hooks` is the virtual root `/pb_embedded/pb_hooks`. Paths under it, and relative paths, load
  from the hooks FS. Everything else is "module not found": absolute disk paths, `..` escapes, `node_modules`. JS that
  reads files itself (`$os.readFile(__hooks + ...)`) gets "no such file", since the root doesn't exist on disk.
- **Public files:** `bundle.Public(app, fsys, indexFallback)` serves the FS at `GET /{path...}` like `pb_public`,
  unless the app has its own route there. With `indexFallback`, unknown paths serve `index.html` (single-page apps).

## Integrations

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [JSVM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm) | `Hooks` and `Migrations` are jsvm extensions (`HookFiles`, `Modules`, `MigrationFiles`). |

## Example

```go
// Command example serves its JS hooks and public files from files embedded in the binary: no pb_hooks or pb_public
// folder on disk.
//
//	go run ./example serve
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/hello
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/
package main

import (
	"embed"
	"io/fs"
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bundle"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
)

//go:embed hooks public
var files embed.FS

func main() {
	hooks, err := fs.Sub(files, "hooks")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	public, err := fs.Sub(files, "public")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app)
	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{Extensions: []any{bundle.Hooks(hooks)}})
	bundle.Public(app, public, true)
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

`Hooks` implements jsvm's `HookFiles` and `Modules`: the engine asks it for the hook files and for every module
`require()` resolves, and it serves only paths under the virtual root, from the FS. `Migrations` implements
`MigrationFiles`. `Public` binds the static route with `apis.Static` at the lowest priority, as PocketBase does for
`pb_public`.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap

# Mail Trap

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A development mail catcher (like MailDev or Mailpit) for testing an extension or app that sends mail. In dev mode, an
app whose SMTP is off sends its mail here instead of the host's `sendmail`, and you read it at http://127.0.0.1:8025.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Mail Trap is built into `pocketone`, for a single app and for every pocker instance on a multisite host. There's
nothing to install: run `pocketone serve --dev` with SMTP off and it's active.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
mailtrap.MustRegister(app)
app.Start()
```

Under Pocker, add `mailtrap.New()` to the extensions. The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mailtrap`.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section or settings screen. It turns itself on only when both are true:

- the app is in dev mode (`serve --dev`, or a dev instance under Pocker), and
- the app's SMTP is off (Settings → Mail).

Turn SMTP on, or run without `--dev`, and it does nothing. Two environment variables move its ports:

| Variable | Default |
|---|---|
| `P1_MAILTRAP_HTTP` | `127.0.0.1:8025` (the web inbox) |
| `P1_MAILTRAP_SMTP` | `127.0.0.1:1025` (SMTP) |

Never expose these ports: anyone who can reach them can read the mail.

## Use

1. Start the app with `--dev`. It prints the inbox address once it's active.
2. Make your extension or app send mail: a verification, a password reset, `$app.newMailClient()`, a bulk mail campaign.
   Each caught message is also printed as one line in the terminal.
3. Open http://127.0.0.1:8025. The list refreshes every 2 seconds. Click a message to see it as **HTML**, **Text** or
   **Raw** source. **Clear** empties the inbox.

It keeps the last 500 messages, in memory only; they're gone when the process exits. If its ports are taken, it still
catches mail and prints each message in the terminal.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) | Provides `mail.fallback/v1`: with SMTP off, an app's mail goes to the contract's providers in order (`providers: { mail.fallback/v1: [mailtrap, mailrelay] }`); in dev mode Mail Trap takes it, otherwise it passes it on. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | One inbox for every dev instance. Each message is labeled with the instance that sent it (its `X-Pocker-Instance` header), and the inbox filters by instance. |
| [Mail Relay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay) | Mail Relay's example uses the trap's SMTP port as its relay, so relayed mail goes through the real SMTP path and lands here. |
| [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | In dev mode with SMTP off, campaign mail lands in the inbox instead of being sent. |

### Building on Mail Trap

- **Its hook runs last.** It binds `OnMailerSend` after the app's own hooks, so your `onMailerSend` hooks still run
  and can change the message first. When it takes a message it never calls the next handler, so `sendmail` never runs.
- **SMTP for other tools.** The SMTP listener accepts any message (and any AUTH), so anything that speaks SMTP can
  send to it.
- **Go API.** `mailtrap.Default(reason)` returns the process-wide trap, starting it on first use. A `Trap` has
  `Messages()`, `Clear()`, `Add(from, to, raw, label)` and `AddMessage(msg, label)`, and `Handler()` serves the inbox.
  `Trap{SMTPAddr, HTTPAddr}.Start(ctx)` runs a separate trap, for example in a test.
- **Inbox API.** `GET /api/messages` (newest first, without bodies), `GET /api/messages/{id}`,
  `GET /api/messages/{id}/raw` (.eml) and `DELETE /api/messages`, on the inbox address.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/mailtrap/example/main.go) runs one app in dev mode with the trap. Run `go run ./example serve --dev` from
this folder, request a password reset for `user@example.com` (password `password`) from the dashboard (log in as
`admin@example.com` / `password`), and read the mail at http://127.0.0.1:8025.

```go
// Command example runs one app in dev mode with the dev mail trap: request a password reset for user@example.com
// in the dashboard and read the mail at http://127.0.0.1:8025.
//
//	go run ./example serve --dev
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mailtrap"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app)
	mailtrap.MustRegister(app)
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

It's built on PocketBase's own `OnMailerSend` hook (the same way [Mail Relay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay) takes over an
instance's mail), so PocketBase is unchanged. It used to live in core (`tools/mailer/trap.go`); it moved here on
2026-11-13.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard

# Standard Set

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

The extensions every PocketOne app has: settings, page templates, a cache, API tokens (with the OAuth server), remotes (remote/v1), MCP,
PocketPages, S3 redirects, point-in-time restore, backups, bulk mail and deploy. The stock `pocketone` binary and every Pocker instance use it,
so an app never misses one because its host forgot to list it. Members can be reconfigured or turned off per app,
never removed.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The standard set is built into `pocketone`. In your own Go build, make the app with it instead of
`pocketbase.New()`:

```go
set := standard.New()
app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks"})
app.Start()
```

`NewApp` registers the members, loads `pb_hooks` with their JS APIs (`$mcp`, `$tokens`, `$bulkmail`) and resolves
their contracts. On an app you built yourself, call `set.Register(app, jsvmConfig)` instead.

## Configure

- **Reconfigure a member:** replace it, e.g. `set.PITR = pitr.New(pitr.Config{Retention: 7 * 24 * time.Hour})`. A
  member set to nil is an error.
- **Turn one off:** `enabled: false` in its `pocketone.yaml` section, or in an instance's `extensions.<name>` under
  Pocker. Extensions that require it turn off too, and say why.
- **Add your own:** `set.Add(myextension.New())`. Extras register after the members, under the same rules.
- **Pick providers:** `set.Providers` is `pocketone.yaml`'s `providers:` section, for a contract more than one
  extension provides.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `providers:`

Which extension provides a contract when several do.

## Use

Each app logs what it got when it starts:

```
standard: on: settings, templates, cache, tokens, remotes, mcp, pages, s3redirect, pitr, backups, bulkmail, deploy
standard: tokens/v1 ← tokens
```

With remotes off (deploy requires its remote/v1):

```
standard: remotes off: enabled: false
standard: deploy off: needs remote/v1, which nothing provides
```

## Integrations

| With | What happens |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Every instance gets the set (`Server.Standard`), with its own `extensions.<name>` settings. |
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) | Members find each other through contracts (`tokens/v1`), resolved per app; the startup lines show who provides what. |

## Example

```go
// A PocketOne app with the standard set and one extra extension: run it with `go run . serve`.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mailtrap"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pitr"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/standard"
)

func main() {
	set := standard.New()
	set.PITR = pitr.New(pitr.Config{Retention: 7 * 24 * time.Hour}) // reconfigure a member
	set.Add(mailtrap.New())                                         // add your own

	app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks"})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/spec

# PocketPages v1 specification

The contract for `ext/pages`, PocketOne's server-rendered multi-page app extension. The test fixtures
([`fixtures/`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/fixtures)), the starter kits and the PocketPages site are written against this document. Where the
implementation and this document disagree, one of them is a bug.

v1 is a clean API. It keeps PocketPages' ideas (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware,
private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for the npm package (0.x) don't run unchanged; "Changes from
0.x" (section 12) lists every difference.

## 1. The `pb_pages` folder

Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others:

```
myapp/
  pb_data/  pb_hooks/  pb_migrations/  pb_public/
  pb_pages/
```

- A single app finds it at `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`, or at `--pagesDir` (a relative path resolves against the
  working directory, like `--hooksDir`).
- Serving is automatic: the standard PocketOne binary includes pages, and an app serves its `pb_pages` whenever the folder
  exists (it starts serving if the folder appears later). There is no on/off switch; no folder, no pages.
- Under the multitenant host every instance has its own `pb_pages`.
- If the folder doesn't exist, the extension does nothing for that app.
- Page code can `require()` modules from `pb_pages` (`_private/` folders, then `node_modules`), then from the app's
  usual module paths. The same `require` works in modules, JSX/TSX components and EJS templates:
  - `./x` and `../x` are files in `pb_pages`, relative to the requiring file, never above `pb_pages`. Without an
    extension, `.js`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.json` and `.cjs` are tried, then a folder's `package.json` or `index`.
  - A bare name (`pkg`, `pkg/sub`, `@scope/pkg`) is looked up first in `_private/` folders, from the requiring file's
    folder up to the top of `pb_pages`, the same lookup as `include` (4.2; the extensions above are tried). Then it's
    looked up in the nearest `node_modules` folder, the same way up. A package resolves through its `package.json`: `exports` (a string,
    or conditions, where `require`, then `node`, then `default` are used), else `main`, else `index.js`. With
    `exports`, only what it lists can be required, and no entry may point outside the package.
  - Then `pb_hooks/node_modules`, then the app folder's `node_modules` (the folder that holds `pb_pages`, where 0.x
    sites keep `package.json`).
  - Anything not found that way goes to the app's own module loader. If that fails too, the error lists the folders
    searched.
  - A require cycle (`a` requires `b`, which requires `a`) gets the exports as they are so far, as in Node.
  - `node_modules` is never routed or served, and isn't watched: after changing files in it, change any file in
    `pb_pages` (or restart) to reload.
- Page code runs in the app's JS VM, so PocketBase's JSVM globals (`$app`, `Record`, `$dbx`, `$security`, ...) are
  available, as far as the sandbox allows for untrusted apps.
- Deploying: `pb_pages` is part of an app's code, next to `pb_hooks` and `pb_migrations` (the `deploy` extension
  uploads it the same way).
- Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves `pb_pages`.

### 1.1 Special names

A path segment (file or folder name) starting with one of these characters is never a URL:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+` | Framework file: `+config`, `+middleware`, `+page`, `+api` (`.js` or `.ts`); `+layout`, `+error`, `+404` (`.ejs`, `.jsx` or `.tsx`). `+middleware`, `+page`, `+api` and `+layout`: one of each per folder. `+config`, `+error` and `+404`: only at the top of `pb_pages` (in a subfolder they're an error at startup). Any other `+` name is an error at startup. |
| `_` | Private. `_private/` folders hold partials and modules for `include()` and `ctx.resolve()`. Other `_` names are ignored. |
| `-` | Ignored (drafts, notes). |
| `.` | Ignored (dotfiles), except a top-level `.well-known/`, which is served as static files (ACME challenges, `security.txt`, app links). |

`node_modules/` is never routed. Hook files (`*.pb.js`, `*.pb.ts`) belong in `pb_hooks`: in `pb_pages` they're a
startup error and never served.

### 1.2 Groups

A folder named `(name)` groups files without adding a URL segment: `(marketing)/about.ejs` serves `/about`. Groups can
carry their own `+layout.ejs`, `+middleware.js` and `_private/`.

## 2. Routes

### 2.1 Pages

A **page** is a template file: `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` or `.tsx` (4.5).

| File | URL |
|---|---|
| `index.ejs` | `/` |
| `about.ejs` | `/about` |
| `docs/index.md` | `/docs` (and `/docs/`) |
| `docs/routing.md` | `/docs/routing` |
| `products/[id].ejs` | `/products/123`, with `ctx.params.id = "123"` |
| `[org]/[repo]/index.ejs` | `/acme/web`, with `ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" }` |

- The extension is dropped. `index` maps to its folder.
- `[name]` matches exactly one non-empty segment. A segment may mix text and a parameter only as the whole segment;
  `post-[id].ejs` is an error at startup.
- A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one.
- Matching is case-sensitive.

### 2.2 API routes

A `+api.js` file serves its folder's URL without a template: `feeds/rss/+api.js` serves `/feeds/rss`.
`[param]` folders work as for pages. If a folder has both `+api.js` and an `index` page, startup fails.

A `+page.js` in a folder with no page (no template file) and no `+api.js` serves the folder's URL the same way, from
JS: `logout/+page.js` serves `/logout` (3.2).

### 2.3 Static files

Every other file is served as-is at its path (groups removed): `assets/app.css` serves `/assets/app.css`. Files that
mustn't be served (build inputs such as a Tailwind source) take a `-` prefix: `assets/-app.tailwind.css`.

- Content type from the extension.
- `ETag` from the content hash; `If-None-Match` answers `304`.
- Fingerprinted URLs (see `ctx.asset`, 6.5) are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

### 2.4 Precedence

1. `/api/...` and `/_/...` are PocketBase's. Pages never see them, and a `pb_pages/api/` folder is an error at
   startup.
2. Among matching routes the most specific wins: compare segment by segment from the left; a literal segment beats a
   `[param]`. So `products/new.ejs` beats `products/[id].ejs` for `/products/new`.
3. A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error).
4. A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase.
5. If `pb_pages/+404.ejs` exists, a `GET`/`HEAD` that nothing (pages, `pb_public`, PocketBase) answers renders it
   inside the root layout with status `404` (never for `/api/` or `/_/`). The root `+middleware.js` runs first;
   page code can still change the status.

The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt when anything in `pb_pages` changes. A rebuild never
restarts the app or reloads `pb_hooks`. Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path; the
previous table keeps serving if there was one.

## 3. Request flow

For a URL that matches a page or API route, one JS call does all of this, in order:

1. **Plugins:** every plugin's `extendContext`, then every plugin's `onRequest` (built-in and JS plugins, in config
   order), so an `onRequest` can use what any plugin added to `ctx`.
2. **Middleware**, root first: every `+middleware.js` from `pb_pages/` down to the route's folder (groups included).
3. **Handlers**: the folder's `+page.js` (or `+api.js`): `load`, then the handler for the request method.
4. **Template** (pages only), then **layouts**, innermost first.
5. **Response.**

The call runs under the app's usual JS limits (execution time, memory), as one unit. If any step sends a response
(`ctx.res.redirect`, `json`, `html`, `text`, `file`, `sse`), the later steps are skipped.

### 3.1 Middleware

```js
// pb_pages/admin/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  ctx.data.section = 'admin'
  return next()
}
```

- One signature: `(ctx, next)`. Call `next()` to continue; return its result.
- Returning without calling `next()` ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (500, and in dev
  the error page names the middleware file).
- Share data through `ctx.data`.

### 3.2 Handlers: `+page.js`

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id)
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { qty } = ctx.req.body()
    // ...
    return ctx.res.redirect(`/products/${ctx.params.id}`, { flash: 'Added to cart' })
  },
}
```

- Exports any of `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`. All are optional: a page renders for any method.
- `load` runs for every method; then the method's handler, if there is one. `HEAD` runs `load` and `get` like
  `GET` (only the body is dropped), so keep side effects in `post`/`put`/`patch`/`delete`.
- A handler may set `ctx.data` fields, or return a plain object, which is shallow-assigned into `ctx.data`
  (`Object.assign`). There is no deep merge.
- A `+page.js` applies to every page in its folder. `ctx.route.name` tells them apart.
- A method with no handler still renders the page, for every method (like PHP): a template can handle a form itself
  by checking `ctx.req.method`, with no `+page.js`.
- Only routes with nothing to render (`+api.js`, and a `+page.js` without a page) answer `405` for a method with no
  handler, with an `Allow` header listing the methods that have handlers (`GET, HEAD` when there's a `get`), in the
  order `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE`.
- **Without a page.** A `+page.js` in a folder with no template serves the folder's URL from JS (2.2): there's nothing
  to render, so a handler must send a response (`ctx.res.html`, `ctx.res.redirect`, `ctx.res.json`, ...), and
  returning without one is a 500. Methods without a handler answer `405`, `GET` included. Unlike `+api.js`, errors
  are pages (`+error.ejs` or the HTML error page), not JSON. Folder middleware runs; layouts don't.

### 3.3 API handlers: `+api.js`

Same exports as `+page.js`. There is no template, so a handler must send a response; returning without one is a
500.

```js
// pb_pages/feeds/latest/+api.js
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20)
    return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) => ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') })))
  },
}
```

## 4. Templates

### 4.1 EJS

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<% code %>` | Run JS, no output |
| `<%= expr %>` | Output, HTML-escaped |
| `<%- expr %>` | Output, raw |
| `<%# comment %>` | Nothing |
| `<%%` | A literal `<%` |
| `-%>` | Also remove the newline right after the tag |
| `<%_` / `_%>` | Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line |
| `<script server> code </script>` | Same as `<% code %>` |

- Escaping replaces `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` with `&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` `&#34;` `&#39;`. `null` and `undefined` output as an empty string.
- A template is compiled once per content hash and reused.

**In scope inside a template:** `ctx`, `data` (= `ctx.data`), `params` (= `ctx.params`), `include`, `slot`, `asset`
(= `ctx.asset`), `meta` (= `ctx.meta`), `require` (the same `require` as page code, 1).

A template returns its text. There is no `echo`; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

### 4.2 Partials: `include`

```ejs
<%- include('nav') %>
<%- include('card', { product }) %>
```

- `include(name, locals?)` renders a template from a `_private/` folder and returns its text. Use `<%-` so its HTML
  isn't escaped.
- Lookup: `_private/` in the current template's folder, then each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`. For a template
  that is itself inside a `_private/` folder, the search starts at the folder containing that `_private/` (so its
  siblings are found first). A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`, unless it names a `_private/` folder itself
  (`/_private/card`, `/blog/_private/card`, as in 0.x), which is a path from the top of `pb_pages`. `..` is not allowed.
- `name` may include its extension. The exact name is tried first; then `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` are added, in
  that order, so a dotted name such as `nav.main` finds `nav.main.ejs`.
- The partial sees the same `ctx`, plus `locals` as top-level variables. As in EJS, `locals` is also the whole object,
  so an optional one can be tested without a `ReferenceError`: `<% if (locals.subtitle) { %>`. A page or layout gets an
  empty `locals`.
- Including more than 32 levels deep is an error (recursion guard).

### 4.3 Slots and layouts

`+layout.ejs` files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every `+layout.ejs` from its own folder up to `pb_pages/`,
applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/products/[id].ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %><%= data.product.getString('name') %><% }) %>
<h1><%= data.product.getString('name') %></h1>
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ejs -->
<html>
  <head><title><%- slot('title') || 'My shop' %></title></head>
  <body><%- slot() %></body>
</html>
```

- `slot(name, fn)` defines a named slot: `fn`'s output is captured and nothing is output in place.
- `slot(name)` returns a slot's content (`''` if not defined). `slot()` returns the content being wrapped: the page,
  or the inner layout. `<%- slot %>` (no call, as 0.x layouts wrote it) prints the same thing.
- Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout. Defining the same name
  again replaces it; inside the new definition's `fn`, `slot(name)` still returns the previous content, so a layout
  can wrap it (`slot('title', () => { %>Docs: <%- slot('title') %><% })`).
- Layouts are skipped when the response isn't HTML (a handler set another `Content-Type`) or after
  `ctx.res.layout(false)`.
- A page with an inner extension gets that type: `robots.txt.ejs` serves `/robots.txt` as `text/plain` and
  `feed.xml.ejs` serves `/feed.xml` as XML, so layouts are skipped. `.html` (or no inner extension) is HTML. Page
  code can still set another `Content-Type`.

### 4.4 Markdown pages

A `.md` page is EJS first, then Markdown (CommonMark + GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks).

- Front matter between `---` lines at the top is YAML, removed before EJS runs. Each top-level key is passed to
  `ctx.meta(key, value)`, for pages and for included `.md` partials.
- Headings get `id`s: lowercased, characters other than `a-z 0-9 - _ space` removed, spaces to `-`; a repeated id
  gets `-1`, `-2`, ... appended.
- Fenced code blocks render as `<pre><code class="language-<lang>">`. Raw HTML passes through unchanged.
- Relative image paths go through `ctx.asset`.
- A `.md` partial is rendered (EJS, then Markdown) on its own and inserted as HTML; Markdown never runs twice on the
  same text. Leave blank lines around an `include` in Markdown so the HTML stays a block.

### 4.5 JSX and TSX

`.jsx` and `.tsx` files are templates too: pages, layouts (`+layout.tsx`), `+error`/`+404`, and partials in
`_private/`. They're compiled when first used by esbuild, which is built into the binary (no Node, no build step), and
cached by content like EJS. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked.

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/[id].tsx
import Price from './_private/Price'

export default function Product({ data, slot }: any) {
  slot('title', data.product.getString('name'))
  return (
    <article class="product">
      <h1>{data.product.getString('name')}</h1>
      <Price cents={data.product.getInt('price')} />
    </article>
  )
}
```

- The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. Props: `ctx`, `data`, `params`,
  `meta`, `asset`, `include`, `slot`, `children`, plus an `include`'s locals.
- JSX renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration, no client-side React. Event
  handler props (functions) are dropped; use plain attributes (`onclick="..."`, `hx-get`, `data-on:click`).
- Text and attribute values are escaped. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html }}` inserts raw HTML. `class` and
  `className` both work, as do `for` and `htmlFor`. `style` takes a string or an object (`{ marginTop: 4 }` →
  `margin-top:4`). `true` renders a bare attribute; `false`, `null` and `undefined` leave it out.
- `<html>` renders with `<!doctype html>` in front of it (JSX can't write a doctype).
- In a layout, `children` is the inner content. `slot(name)` reads a named slot, `slot(name, content)` sets one
  (content is JSX or a string), `slot()` is the same as `children`.
- `include(name, locals)` returns the partial's HTML, ready to put in JSX. EJS can `include` a `.jsx`/`.tsx` partial:
  its locals become props.
- Components are ordinary modules: `import Card from './_private/Card'` (resolved like `require`, 3.2). Partials
  are looked up with extensions in this order: `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`.

**TypeScript modules.** `+page.ts`, `+api.ts`, `+middleware.ts`, `+config.ts` and any `.ts` file reached by
`require`/`import` work like their `.js` versions. A module whose only export is `export default` behaves like
`module.exports = ...`.

## 5. Responses

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| A handler or middleware sent one | That one |
| Page rendered | `200 text/html; charset=utf-8` (or the status set with `ctx.res.status`) |
| `HEAD` | As `GET`, without a body |
| No handler for the method | Page: rendered as usual. `+api.js` or a `+page.js` without a page: `405` + `Allow` |
| Error thrown | `500` (see 8) |

JSON is only sent through `ctx.res.json` (or `+api.js`). Template output is never parsed as JSON.

## 6. The `ctx` object

One object per request, passed to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.

### 6.1 `ctx.req`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `method` | `"GET"`, `"POST"`, ... |
| `url` | `{ href, origin, pathname, search }` |
| `query(name)` | First value of a query parameter as a string, or `undefined` |
| `query(name, { all: true })` | Every value, as an array of strings |
| `query()` | `{ name: firstValue }` for every parameter |
| `header(name)` | Request header, `''` if absent |
| `cookie(name)` | Cookie value as a string, or `undefined` |
| `cookie(name, { json: true })` | Cookie parsed as JSON (`undefined` if absent or not JSON) |
| `cookies()` | `{ name: value }`, strings |
| `body()` | Parsed body: JSON object, or form fields (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data`) as `{ name: value }` (repeated names as arrays) |
| `files(name)` | Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase `*filesystem.File` values ready for a record field |
| `ip` | Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) |
| `event` | The underlying PocketBase `RequestEvent`, for anything not covered here |

Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

### 6.2 `ctx.res`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `status(code)` | Status for the rendered page. Returns `ctx.res`. |
| `header(name, value)` | Set a response header; returns `ctx.res`. `header(name)` reads it back. |
| `cookie(name, value, options?)` | Set a cookie. Non-string values are `JSON.stringify`'d; the value is then percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`), and `ctx.req.cookie` decodes it. Defaults: `path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` when the request is HTTPS. Options: `path`, `domain`, `maxAge` (seconds), `expires` (a `Date`, milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string; with `maxAge` too, browsers use `maxAge`), `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`. |
| `clearCookie(name, options?)` | Expire a cookie (same `path`/`domain` as when set). |
| `redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?)` or `redirect(location, status)` | Send a redirect. `status` must be a 3xx code. `flash` sets a one-time message (6.4). |
| `json(data)` / `json(status, data)` | Send JSON. |
| `html(html)` / `html(status, html)` | Send HTML as-is (no layouts). |
| `text(text)` / `text(status, text)` | Send plain text. |
| `file(path)` | Send a file from `pb_pages` (path relative to `pb_pages`). |
| `sse()` | Start a `text/event-stream` response; returns `{ send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() }`. |
| `layout(false)` | Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). |
| `sent` | `true` once a response has been sent. |

### 6.3 Data and routing

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `ctx.data` | Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. Starts as `{}`. |
| `ctx.params` | Route parameters, strings. Never includes query parameters. |
| `ctx.route` | `{ path, name, file }`: the URL pattern without groups (`/products/[id]`, `/docs` for `docs/index.md`), the file name without extension (`[id]`, `index`; `+api` for API routes) and the file relative to `pb_pages`, groups included. |

### 6.4 Flash messages

- `ctx.res.redirect(path, { flash: 'Saved' })` stores the message as JSON in a cookie (`pp_flash`, encoded like any
  cookie, `HttpOnly`, `Max-Age=300`).
- `ctx.flash()` on the next request returns it and clears it (`Max-Age=0`). It returns `undefined` when there is
  none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value.
- A flash can be any JSON value.

### 6.5 Helpers

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `ctx.auth` | The authenticated record, or `null`. Set by PocketBase's own auth (an `Authorization` header) or by the `auth` plugin's cookie. |
| `ctx.app` | The app (`$app`): records, collections, settings. |
| `ctx.pb()` | A PocketBase JS SDK client (the bundled synchronous build) acting as the signed-in user (`ctx.auth`), or as a guest. Its requests go to the app's own API in-process (no network), so collection API rules, `expand` and field visibility apply exactly as for a browser. API errors throw the SDK's `ClientResponseError` (`e.status`, `e.response`). Only `/api/` routes; file uploads through the SDK aren't supported (use `ctx.app`). |
| `ctx.env(name)` | Environment variable, `''` if unset (the app's environment; under the sandbox, the instance's). |
| `ctx.log` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`: to the app's log. `debug` only shows in dev. |
| `ctx.meta(key, value?)` | Per-request key/value store for page metadata (title, description). Set with two arguments, read with one. |
| `ctx.asset(path)` | URL for a static file in `pb_pages`, with its content hash: `asset('app.css')` → `/assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css`. Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; `/`-paths from `pb_pages`. A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged. |
| `ctx.include(name, locals?)` | Render a `_private/` partial from JS (handlers, middleware, plugins) and get its text; same lookup as the template `include`, from the route's folder. |
| `ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?)` | Load a module from `_private/`, looked up from the route's folder up (like `ctx.include`; wherever it's called from); without an extension, the name, then `.js`, `.ts` and `.json` are tried. Modes: `require` (default, the module's exports), `raw` (file text), `script` (text wrapped in `<script>`), `style` (wrapped in `<style>`). |
| `ctx.pagesDir` | The absolute path of this app's `pb_pages` folder, e.g. for listing files with `$os.readDir`. Read-only. |
| `ctx.store(name, value?)` | The app's in-memory store (`$app.store()`): set with two arguments, read with one. |
| `ctx.dev` | `true` in dev mode. |

Fingerprinted asset names carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: `name.<hash>.ext`.

## 7. Configuration: `+config.js`

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
  debug: false,
}
```

| Key | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins` | `[]` | Module names, built-in names (`auth`, `realtime`), or JS plugin factories such as add-ons (9). EJS and Markdown are always on. |
| `debug` | `false` | Detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output even outside dev mode. |

A string in `plugins` is a module name, required from `+config.js` (1): a `_private/` file (`'datastar'` finds
`_private/datastar.js`), a package in `node_modules` (`'my-plugin'`) or a path (`'./plugins/my-plugin.js'`). Its export, or its `default` export, must be a
plugin factory (9.2). Only when no module by that name is found is the string a built-in (9.1), so a
`_private/auth.js` or a package named `auth` would replace the built-in `auth`. To skip that order and load one exact
file, list `require('./path')` instead of the name: a `./` path is never looked up in `_private/` or `node_modules`. A module that is found but fails to load is an error; it never falls back to
the built-in.

`+config.js` runs on each page request, so these aren't caught at startup: unknown keys, names that are neither a
module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error (a 500; dev mode shows the
reason on the page), and the reason goes to the log.

## 8. Errors

- Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a `500`.
- **Dev mode or `debug: true`:** an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the
  `.ejs`/`.md` source), and the stack trimmed to `pb_pages`-relative paths.
- **Otherwise:** a plain "Something went wrong" page. The full error always goes to the app's log.
- `throw ctx.httpError(status, message)` sends that status (e.g. `404`, `403`) with a plain page showing `message`.
  In a `+api.js` it's JSON: `{ "status": 404, "message": "..." }`.
- A custom error page: `pb_pages/+error.ejs` renders for every `ctx.httpError` and every 500 outside dev mode, with
  `ctx.error = { status, message }`, inside the root layout.

## 9. Plugins

### 9.1 Built-in

Turned on by name in `+config.js` when no module by that name is found (7).

**`auth`:** cookie sessions on PocketBase auth, without calling the app over HTTP.
- Every request: reads the `pb_auth` cookie, validates the token, sets `ctx.auth` (or clears a bad cookie).
- The cookie holds `{ token, record }` as JSON (the JS SDK's cookie format), `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` on
  HTTPS, lasting as long as the collection's auth token.
- `identity` arguments accept any of the collection's identity fields (email by default).
- **MFA:** pages has no second sign-in step yet, so every sign-in method (password, OTP, anonymous, OAuth2, and
  `register`'s sign-in) refuses an account that needs MFA, as PocketBase decides it: the collection has MFA on and its
  MFA rule matches the record (an empty rule matches everyone; a rule that can't be checked counts as a match). The
  error says so; nothing is signed in and an OTP isn't used up. A wrong password still says only that the credentials
  are invalid. `ctx.session.signIn(record)` is the exception: it signs in a record the app authenticated itself.
- `ctx.session.authMethods({ collection })` → `{ password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa:
  { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } }`, as PocketBase's auth-methods API.
- `ctx.session.register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true })`: creates the
  record; sends the verification email when `verify`; signs in when `signIn`.
- `ctx.session.signInWithPassword(identity, password, { collection })`
- `ctx.session.requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false })` → `otpId`. Always returns an id (unknown emails
  get one that never validates, as PocketBase does); with `create: true` a missing record is created first.
- `ctx.session.signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection })`
- `ctx.session.signInAnonymously({ collection })`
- `ctx.session.requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true })`:
  stores state in a cookie and returns the provider's URL; with `redirect` it also sends the redirect
  (`ctx.res.sent`). `redirectPath` must be a path on this site. PKCE is used when the provider supports it.
- `ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?)`: completes it on the redirect path (the state cookie
  carries the provider, collection and PKCE verifier; it lasts 10 minutes and works once). The sign-in runs through
  PocketBase's own `auth-with-oauth2` endpoint in-process, so sign-up, account linking (to the signed-in account,
  if any), the anti-hijacking checks and `onRecordAuthWithOAuth2Request` hooks behave as in PocketBase. `createData`
  is extra data for a new record. Returns `{ token, record, meta }` (`meta` is PocketBase's OAuth2 meta, with
  `isNew`). Accounts that need MFA throw an error: pages doesn't do MFA yet.
- Apple answers with a POST, so read `state` and `code` from `ctx.req.body()` there. On HTTPS the state cookie is
  `SameSite=None` so it survives that cross-site POST.
- `ctx.session.signIn(record)`: set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself.
- `ctx.session.signOut()`
- Email flows, with PocketBase's own checks and mail templates: `requestVerification(email, { collection })`,
  `confirmVerification(token)`, `requestPasswordReset(email, { collection })`,
  `confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm)`, `requestEmailChange(newEmail)` (needs `ctx.auth`),
  `confirmEmailChange(token, password)`. Request methods never reveal whether an email exists.
- Every sign-in method sets `ctx.auth` for the rest of the request and returns `{ token, record }`.

**`realtime`:** PocketBase realtime from page code.
- `ctx.realtime.send(topic, data, { filter }?)` sends to every client subscribed to `topic` (the filter only narrows
  that set). `data` is always
  JSON-encoded (a string arrives as a JSON string, as PocketBase's own messages do).
- `filter(client)` returns `true` to include a client. `client` is PocketBase's realtime client: `id()`,
  `get(key)`, `set(key, value)`, `hasSubscription(topic)`.
- `ctx.realtime.client(id)` returns one client by id, or `null`.
- Sending never waits for slow clients: each message is handed to the client's queue in the background.

### 9.2 JS plugins

A JS plugin is a factory that returns hooks:

```js
module.exports = (config) => ({
  name: 'my-plugin',
  onRequest(ctx) {},                       // before middleware
  extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () => 'hi' },
  transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html },     // after each page or layout renders (not partials)
})
```

- `config` is the plugin's entry in `+config.js` when it's an object (`{ factory, ...options }`), else `{}`.
- `name` is required and unique.
- 0.x hook names (`onExtendContextApi`, `onRender`, `onResponse`, `handles`) are an error that names the v1 hook to
  use.
- There's no hook for treating other kinds of files as pages: a page's inner extension already does that
  (`robots.txt.ejs` serves `/robots.txt` as `text/plain`, 4.5).
- Hooks run in config order. Every hook is optional.
- JS plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's JS (sandboxed in a multitenant host).

### 9.3 Add-ons

Plugins for third-party libraries ship as JS files in `ext/pages/addons/`, not built into `ext/pages`. Copy one into
`pb_pages/_private/` and list it in `+config.js` by name (`'datastar'`).

**`datastar.js`** ([Datastar](https://data-star.dev)) adds `ctx.datastar`:
- `ctx.datastar.scripts({ spa: { scope, selector }, realtime }?)` returns the script tags (`spa` turns on
  client-side navigation for links under `scope`, swapping `selector`). With `realtime: true` the page subscribes to
  the `datastar` realtime topic and sets a `$clientId` signal to its realtime client id.
- `ctx.datastar.patchElements(html, { selector, mode }?)`, `ctx.datastar.patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?)`
  (`signals` is an object), `ctx.datastar.executeScript(js)` send SSE events on the current response. The first one
  starts the stream (`ctx.res.sent` becomes `true`); later steps still run, but their output isn't sent and the
  automatic patch below doesn't happen. The stream closes when the request ends.
- `ctx.datastar.signals()` returns the request's signals as an object (from the `datastar` query parameter on
  `GET`, the JSON body otherwise). `readSignals(target)` (or 0.x's `readSignals(request, target)`) merges them into
  `target` and returns it.
- Script helpers, each an `executeScript` (options `{ eventId, retryDuration, autoRemove = true, attributes }`;
  `autoRemove` adds `data-effect="el.remove()"` so the script tag removes itself, `attributes` is a list of extra
  attribute strings such as `'type="module"'`): `consoleLog(msg)`, `consoleError(err)`, `redirect(url)` (a full
  page load), `dispatchCustomEvent(name, detail, { selector, bubbles, cancelable, composed, eventId, retryDuration
  }?)` (on `document` by default), `replaceURL(url)` (`history.replaceState`) and `prefetch(urls)` (a
  `speculationrules` script that stays in the page).
- `mode` is one of `outer` (default), `inner`, `replace`, `prepend`, `append`, `before`, `after`, `remove`.
- When a request has `Datastar-Request: true`, the rendered page (without layouts) is sent as a `patchElements`
  event, into `Datastar-Selector` if given.
- `ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements(html, options?, { filter }?)`, `.patchSignals(signals, options?, { filter }?)`
  and `.executeScript(js, { filter }?)` send the same events to `datastar` realtime subscribers (needs `realtime`).

## 10. Dev mode

On when the app runs in dev mode (`--dev`) or `+config.js` sets `debug: true`:
- detailed error pages (8);
- `ctx.log.debug` output;
- template cache keyed by content hash, so edits show on the next request (the route table is rebuilt on any file
  change in every mode).

## 11. Starter kits

`pocketone pages create <name> [--starter <kit>]` creates the folder `<name>` (it must not exist) and copies the
whole kit into it. Run it with `cd <name> && pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data` (`pocketone` keeps `pb_data` next to its
executable by default; `pb_pages` and `pb_migrations` are found next to `pb_data`). `pocketone pages starters` lists
the kits. Kits: `minimal` (default), `mvp`, `htmx`,
`daisyui`, `daisyui-docs`, `datastar`, `auth`. The command needs a build that includes `ext/pages`. It copies
`pb_pages/` plus anything beside it (`pb_migrations/`, `README.md`, a `package.json` for CSS tooling). Kits ship
inside `ext/pages` (`starters/`).

## 12. Changes from 0.x (npm PocketPages)

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `pb_hooks/pages/`, booted by `require('pocketpages')` in a `.pb.js` | `pb_pages/`, no boot file, no npm install |
| `api` object, re-spread into each call | `ctx` with `req`, `res`, `data`, `params`, `route`, helpers |
| Query parameters mixed into `params`, JSON-parsed | `ctx.params` is route parameters only; `ctx.req.query()` returns strings |
| Cookies JSON-parsed on read | Strings; `{ json: true }` to parse |
| Middleware: return a value, or call `next(extra)`, chosen by arity | `(ctx, next)`, data on `ctx.data` |
| `+load.js`, `+get.js`, `+post.js`, ... per folder, results deep-merged | One `+page.js` exporting `load`, `get`, `post`, ...; returned objects shallow-assigned |
| `+config.js` may export `(api) => ({...})` | It must export an object; a function is an error |
| Template output that parses as JSON is sent as JSON | Only `ctx.res.json` or `+api.js` |
| `<!-- slot:name -->` comments; layouts read `slot` / `slots` | `slot(name, fn)` to define, `slot(name)` / `slot()` to read |
| `echo()` writes during render | Templates return text; streaming only through `ctx.res.sse()` |
| `redirect(path, { message })` puts the flash in `?__flash=` | `ctx.res.redirect(path, { flash })`, one-time cookie, `ctx.flash()` |
| `asset()` fingerprint: full SHA-256 | First 12 hex characters |
| `+config.js` plugins: npm package names, EJS options | A name is required first (a `_private/` file or package), then a built-in; or a JS factory. EJS and Markdown always on |
| Plugin hooks `onRequest({ request, response })`, `onExtendContextApi`, `onRender`, `onResponse`, `handles` | `extendContext(ctx)`, `onRequest(ctx)`, `transform`; a 0.x hook name is an error |
| `*.pb.js` beside pages in `pb_hooks/pages/` | Hook files stay in `pb_hooks`; in `pb_pages` they're a startup error |
| `require('../lib/x')` could reach `pb_hooks` from the pages folder | `require` never leaves `pb_pages`; use `require(__hooks + '/lib/x')` |
| Cookies (and `pb_auth`) readable by browser JS | `HttpOnly` by default; pass `{ httpOnly: false }` for a cookie the page's JS reads. `pb_auth` stays `HttpOnly`, so `pb.authStore.loadFromCookie(document.cookie)` no longer works |
| Realtime `send(topic, message)` sent the message as is; `filter(clientId, client, topic, message)` replaced the subscription check | The data is JSON-encoded (a string arrives quoted: `JSON.parse` it); `filter(client)` narrows clients that are subscribed to the topic |
| `.md`, `.jsx`, `.tsx` were static files unless a plugin handled them | Always pages |
| EJS ran over the whole `.md` file, front matter included | Front matter is plain YAML, read before EJS runs |
| auth plugin through the JS SDK over HTTP (`api.pb()`) | `ctx.session.*`, direct app calls |
| `url()`, `stringify()`, micro-dash globals | Removed: use `ctx.req.url`, `JSON.stringify`, plain JS |
| `pb()` (js-sdk plugin over HTTP to `localhost:8090`) | `ctx.pb()`: same SDK, built in, in-process, as the signed-in user |
| Route with fewer segments could match a longer URL | Segment counts must match |
| `create-pocketpages` | `pocketone pages create <name> [--starter <kit>]` |


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/overview

# Overview of PocketPages

PocketPages turns a folder of files into a server-rendered website, inside PocketOne. It is built in as the `pages` extension (`ext/pages`): no npm package, no boot file, no build step.

Use PocketPages to create slim and modern web apps:

- Start small and iterate
- SEO-first principles
- No build step
- Fast server-side rendering

## Hello world in just one file

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/index.ejs -->
<%= `Hello, world!` %>
```

<%- include('browser', { content: `Hello, world!` }) %>

Inside `<%` and `%>` you write plain JavaScript. Every page gets a `ctx` object with the request, the response, your data, and the app itself (`ctx.app`), so you can read and write records directly.

## Retro file-based routing

Files become URLs, and `+layout.ejs` files wrap the pages below them:

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ejs -->
<html>
  <body style="background-color: #b5dcb5">
    <%- slot() %>
  </body>
</html>
```

<%- include('browser', { bodyTags: `style="background-color: #b5dcb5"`, content: `Hello, world!` }) %>

## Coming from the npm package?

PocketPages v1 is a clean API. Apps written for PocketPages 0.x (the npm package) don't run unchanged. See [Moving from PocketPages 0.x](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/moving-from-0x).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/moving-from-0x

# Moving from PocketPages 0.x

PocketPages v1 is part of PocketOne (the `pages` extension). It keeps the ideas of the npm package (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware, private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for 0.x don't run unchanged.

There is no migration tool. Start a new app with `pocketone pages create <name>`, then move your pages over using the list below. The npm package is being retired.

## Folder and boot

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `pb_hooks/pages/`, booted by `require('pocketpages')` in a `.pb.js` file | `pb_pages/` next to `pb_data`. No boot file, no npm install. |
| `create-pocketpages` | `pocketone pages create <name> [--starter <kit>]` |

Delete the `.pb.js` boot file and the `pocketpages` dependencies, and move the contents of `pb_hooks/pages/` to `pb_pages/`.

## The context object

0.x passed an `api` object and spread its members into each template. v1 passes one `ctx` object with `req`, `res`, `data`, `params`, `route` and helpers. See the [ctx reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx).

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `request`, `response` | `ctx.req`, `ctx.res` |
| `body()`, `formData` | `ctx.req.body()` |
| `redirect(path)` | `ctx.res.redirect(path)` |
| `response.redirect(path, status)` | `ctx.res.redirect(path, status)` (unchanged) |
| `env()`, `store()`, `dbg()`, `info()`, `warn()`, `error()` | `ctx.env()`, `ctx.store()`, `ctx.log.debug()` / `info()` / `warn()` / `error()` |
| `auth`, `request.auth` | `ctx.auth` |
| `resolve(name)` | `ctx.resolve(name)` |

Inside templates, `data`, `params`, `asset` and `meta` are still available without the `ctx.` prefix. The other
0.x template globals are gone, including `resolve`, `redirect` and `env`: use `ctx.resolve()`, `ctx.res.redirect()` and
`ctx.env()`.

## Parameters, query strings and cookies

- Query parameters are no longer mixed into `params`, and nothing is JSON-parsed for you. `ctx.params` holds route parameters only; read the query string with `ctx.req.query(name)`, which returns strings.
- Cookies are strings. Pass `{ json: true }` to parse one: `ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true })`.

## Middleware

0.x middleware either returned a value or called `next(extra)`, depending on how many arguments it declared. v1 has one signature:

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.user = ctx.auth
  return next()
}
```

Put shared data on `ctx.data`. See [Middleware](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware).

## Loaders

`+load.js`, `+get.js`, `+post.js` and friends are replaced by one `+page.js` per folder that exports `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete`. Returned objects are shallow-assigned into `ctx.data` (no deep merge). As in 0.x, every handler is optional and a page renders for any method, so templates that check the request method keep working (`request.method` becomes `ctx.req.method`).

```js
// 0.x: +load.js
module.exports = (api) => ({ products: $app.findAllRecords('products') })

// v1: +page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') }
  },
}
```

See [Loading Data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data).

## JSON

0.x sent template output as JSON if it parsed as JSON. v1 never does. Send JSON with `ctx.res.json()`, usually from a `+api.js` file. See [API Routes and JSON](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes).

## Layouts and slots

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `<!-- slot:name -->` comments in the page | `slot('name', () => { %>...<% })` |
| `slot` and `slots.name` in layouts | `slot()` and `slot('name')` |

See [Layouts and Slots](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/layouts).

## Output

`echo()` is gone. A template returns its text; anything you want in the output goes through a tag. For streaming, use `ctx.res.sse()`.

## Flash messages

0.x put the message in a `?__flash=` query parameter with `redirect(path, { message })`. v1 uses a one-time cookie:

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
```

Read it on the next request with `ctx.flash()`. See [flash](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash).

## Assets

`asset()` URLs now carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256, not the full hash.

## Configuration and plugins

- `+config.js` still takes plugin package names, which are loaded with `require` as before, but the packages must be
  v1 plugins: the 0.x `pocketpages-plugin-*` packages don't run on v1. `auth` and `realtime` are built in, EJS and
  Markdown are always on, and Datastar is an [add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar) you copy into `pb_pages/_private/` and list as `'datastar'`. Its API is 0.x's, with `signals()` added alongside `readSignals`. npm plugin package names and EJS options are gone.
- `+config.js` must export an object (`module.exports = { ... }`). 0.x's function form, `module.exports = (api) => ({ ... })`, is an error.
- A `package.json` at the app's root still works: bare `require('pkg')` looks in the app folder's `node_modules` after `pb_pages`.
- EJS and Markdown are always on. `pocketpages-plugin-ejs` and `pocketpages-plugin-marked` have no v1 equivalent because they aren't needed.
- The auth plugin no longer goes through the JS SDK over HTTP (`api.pb()`). Use `ctx.session.*`, which calls the app directly. See [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth).

See [+config.js](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/config) and [Plugins](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins).

## Behavior that changed quietly

These don't fail with an error, so check for them when porting:

- **Cookies are `HttpOnly` by default.** Pass `{ httpOnly: false }` to `ctx.res.cookie` for a cookie your page's JS reads. The `pb_auth` cookie stays `HttpOnly`, so `pb.authStore.loadFromCookie(document.cookie)` in the browser no longer works.
- **Realtime messages are JSON-encoded.** `ctx.realtime.send(topic, data)` sends `JSON.stringify(data)`, so a string (such as an HTML fragment) arrives in quotes: `JSON.parse` it on the client. A `filter` now gets one argument, the client, and only narrows clients already subscribed to the topic.
- **`.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` files are always pages**, never served as static files.
- **Front matter is plain YAML.** EJS tags inside it aren't run.
- **`require` never leaves `pb_pages`.** To load code from `pb_hooks`, use `require(__hooks + '/lib/x')`.
- **Hook files (`*.pb.js`) go in `pb_hooks`.** In `pb_pages` they're an error and aren't served.

## Removed globals

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `url()` | `ctx.req.url` |
| `stringify()` | `JSON.stringify` |
| micro-dash | plain JavaScript |
| `pb()` (JS SDK plugin) | `ctx.pb()`, built in: same SDK, no host setting, runs in-process as the signed-in user |

## Routing

A route with fewer segments no longer matches a longer URL. Segment counts must match: `products/[id].ejs` serves `/products/123` but not `/products/123/reviews`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/agents

# Coding agents

Coding agents tend to write PocketPages as if it were a Node framework, or as if it were the 0.x npm package. The `pocketpages` Agent Skill teaches them v1: `pb_pages/`, `ctx`, routing, templates, layouts, auth and deploying. It's built from these docs and the v1 spec, so it changes when they change.

**Claude Code**

```
/plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone
/plugin install pocketone@pocketone
```

The plugin also has the `pocketone` skill, for the binary, `pocketone.yaml` and its extensions.

**Other agents that read Agent Skills** (Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others)

```bash
npx skills add pockethost/pocketone
```

Or copy [`agent/skills/pocketpages`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/agent/skills/pocketpages) into your project.

## llms.txt

- [pocketone.dev/llms.txt](https://pocketone.dev/llms.txt) indexes every docs page, these PocketPages pages included, with a one-line summary.
- [pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt](https://pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt) holds every docs page in one Markdown file.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/installation

# Installation

PocketPages v1 is built into PocketOne as the `pages` extension (`ext/pages`). There is nothing to install from npm: the standard `pocketone` binary includes it.

<%- include('quickstart') %>

`pocketone pages create myapp` creates a new app. Add `--starter <kit>` to start from a [starter kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/starter-kits).

_Note: `--dir` tells `pocketone` where `pb_data` is. PocketPages looks for `pb_pages` next to it. Create the superuser before the first `serve`; otherwise PocketBase opens its superuser installer in your browser._

Browse to `http://localhost:8090` and you'll see the starter's home page. The default `minimal` kit is one splash page:

<%- include('browser', { content: `<h1>PocketPages</h1>` }) %>

To start editing, open

```
myapp/pb_pages/index.ejs
```

Changes appear on the next refresh. The app doesn't restart.

## Where pages live

Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others:

```
myapp/
  pb_data/  pb_hooks/  pb_migrations/  pb_public/
  pb_pages/
```

- PocketPages finds the folder at `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`, or wherever `--pagesDir` points.
- If the folder doesn't exist, the extension does nothing for that app.
- Under a multitenant host, every instance has its own `pb_pages`.

## How does it work?

PocketPages is a multi-page app server for PocketOne. It listens for requests and renders pages using file-based routing rules, like old-school PHP. URLs under `/api/` and `/_/` always belong to PocketBase. A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/starter-kits

# Starter Kits

To start a new app from a starter kit, run:

```bash
pocketone pages create myapp --starter <kit>
```

Without `--starter`, `pocketone pages create myapp` creates a plain app (the `minimal` kit). `pocketone pages starters`
lists the kits. The folder must not exist yet. Then run it:

```bash
cd myapp
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

`pocketone` keeps `pb_data` next to its executable unless you pass `--dir`; `pb_pages` and `pb_migrations` are found next
to `pb_data`.

Each starter kit is an ordinary `pb_pages` folder written against the v1 API, so everything in these docs applies to it.

| Starter | What it shows | Live demo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **minimal** | A minimal PocketPages starter with just the basics | [pocketpages-minimal.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-minimal.pockethost.io) |
| **mvp** | MVP.css, a minimalist classless CSS framework | [pocketpages-mvp.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-mvp.pockethost.io) |
| **auth** | Password, anonymous, OTP and OAuth2 sign-in, plus verification, password reset and email change | [pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io) |
| **daisyui** | Tailwind CSS with DaisyUI components | [pocketpages-daisyui.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-daisyui.pockethost.io) |
| **daisyui-docs** | Documentation site template with DaisyUI and navigation | [pocketpages-daisyui-docs.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-daisyui-docs.pockethost.io) |
| **htmx** | HTMX integration for dynamic interactions | [pocketpages-htmx.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-htmx.pockethost.io) |
| **datastar** | Realtime chat and counter using Datastar | [pocketpages-datastar.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-datastar.pockethost.io) |


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/creating-a-page

# Creating a PocketPages Page

A **page** is a template file, `.ejs` or `.md`, anywhere in `pb_pages/`. Its path becomes its URL.

## Creating pages

1. **Create a file**: inside `pb_pages/`, create an `.ejs` file. For example, an "About" page:

```text
pb_pages/about.ejs  -> serves "/about"
```

2. **`index` files**: `index` maps to its folder.

```text
pb_pages/index.ejs           -> serves "/"
pb_pages/products/index.ejs  -> serves "/products" (and "/products/")
```

3. **Nested pages**: folders become URL segments.

```text
pb_pages/
├── index.ejs         -> "/"
├── about.ejs         -> "/about"
├── contact.ejs       -> "/contact"
└── products/
    ├── index.ejs     -> "/products"
    └── details.ejs   -> "/products/details"
```

4. **Markdown pages**: a `.md` file works the same way. It runs through EJS first, then Markdown. See [Markdown](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown).

```text
pb_pages/docs/routing.md  -> "/docs/routing"
```

The extension is always dropped from the URL. To add data or handle forms, put a `+page.js` next to the page; see [Loading Data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/directory-structure

# Directory Structure

All pages live in the `pb_pages/` folder, next to `pb_data/`:

```
myapp/
  pb_data/
  pb_hooks/
  pb_migrations/
  pb_public/
  pb_pages/
    +config.js
    +layout.ejs
    index.ejs
    about.ejs
    _private/
      nav.ejs
    assets/
      app.css
    products/
      [id]/
        +page.js
        index.ejs
```

## Special names

A file or folder name starting with one of these characters is never a URL:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+` | Framework file: `+layout.ejs` (or `.jsx`, `.tsx`), `+middleware.js`, `+page.js`, `+api.js`, one of each per folder. `+config.js`, `+error.ejs` and `+404.ejs` are allowed only at the top of `pb_pages`. Any other `+` name, any other extension (such as `+layout.md`), and a top-only file in a subfolder are errors at startup. |
| `_` | Private. `_private/` folders hold partials and modules for `include()` and `ctx.resolve()`. Other `_` names are ignored. |
| `-` | Ignored (drafts, notes). |
| `.` | Ignored (dotfiles), except a top-level `.well-known/`, which is served as static files (ACME challenges, `security.txt`, app links). |

`node_modules/` is never routed either.

## Groups

A folder named `(name)` groups files without adding a URL segment: `(marketing)/pricing.ejs` serves `/pricing`. A group can have its own `+layout.ejs`, `+middleware.js` and `_private/`.

## What else

- Every other file is a [static file](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content), served as-is.
- Page code can `require()` modules by name from `_private/` folders (nearest first), then `pb_pages/node_modules`, then
  `pb_hooks/node_modules` and the app folder's `node_modules`, then the app's usual module paths.
- Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves `pb_pages`.
- A `pb_pages/api/` folder is an error at startup, because `/api/` belongs to PocketBase.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/routing

# File-Based Routing

URLs come from the files and folders in `pb_pages/`.

## Pages

| File | URL |
|---|---|
| `index.ejs` | `/` |
| `about.ejs` | `/about` |
| `docs/index.md` | `/docs` (and `/docs/`) |
| `docs/routing.md` | `/docs/routing` |
| `products/[id].ejs` | `/products/123`, with `ctx.params.id = "123"` |
| `[org]/[repo]/index.ejs` | `/acme/web`, with `ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" }` |

- The extension is dropped. `index` maps to its folder.
- `[name]` matches exactly one non-empty segment. A parameter must be the whole segment: `post-[id].ejs` is an error at startup.
- Segment counts must match: `products/[id].ejs` doesn't match `/products/123/reviews`.
- A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one.
- Matching is case-sensitive.

See [Accessing Parameters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/parameters).

## Groups

A folder named `(name)` doesn't add a URL segment. Use groups to give part of the site its own layout or middleware:

```text
pb_pages/
  (site)/
    +layout.ejs     # wraps everything in (site)
    index.ejs       # /
    about.ejs       # /about
  xapi/
    count.ejs       # /xapi/count, outside the (site) layout
```

## API routes

A `+api.js` file serves its folder's URL without a template: `feeds/rss/+api.js` serves `/feeds/rss`. `[param]` folders work as for pages. A folder can't have both a `+api.js` and an `index` page. See [API Routes and JSON](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes).

A `+page.js` in a folder with no page serves the folder's URL from JS too: `logout/+page.js` serves `/logout`. See [Pages without a template](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data#pages-without-a-template).

## Static files

Every other file is served as-is at its path, with groups removed: `assets/app.css` serves `/assets/app.css`. See [Static content](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content).

## Which route wins

1. `/api/...` and `/_/...` belong to PocketBase. Pages never see them.
2. Among matching routes the most specific wins: segments are compared from the left, and a literal segment beats a `[param]`. So `products/new.ejs` beats `products/[id].ejs` for `/products/new`.
3. A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error).
4. A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase.

## When routes change

The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt whenever anything in `pb_pages` changes. A rebuild never restarts the app or reloads `pb_hooks`. Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path, and the previous route table keeps serving.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/parameters

# Route and Query Parameters

Route parameters come from the URL path. Query parameters come from the query string. v1 keeps them apart.

## Route parameters

Use square brackets in file or folder names to capture a URL segment:

```
pb_pages/
  products/
    [productId]/
      index.ejs
      reviews/
        [reviewId].ejs
```

This handles URLs like `/products/123` and `/products/123/reviews/456`.

Read them through `params` (the same object as `ctx.params`):

```ejs
<!-- products/[productId]/reviews/[reviewId].ejs -->
<h1>Product: <%= params.productId %></h1>
<p>Review: <%= params.reviewId %></p>
```

Route parameters are always strings. `ctx.params` never includes query parameters.

## Query parameters

Read the query string with `ctx.req.query()`:

```
/products/123?sort=latest&tag=red&tag=blue
```

```ejs
<p>Sort by: <%= ctx.req.query('sort') %></p>
<p>Tags: <%= ctx.req.query('tag', { all: true }).join(', ') %></p>
```

| Call | Returns |
|---|---|
| `ctx.req.query(name)` | First value as a string, or `undefined` |
| `ctx.req.query(name, { all: true })` | Every value, as an array of strings |
| `ctx.req.query()` | `{ name: firstValue }` for every parameter |

Values are strings. Nothing is parsed for you; if you pass JSON in a query parameter, parse it yourself:

```js
const filters = JSON.parse(ctx.req.query('filters') ?? '{}')
```

## The route itself

`ctx.route` describes the matched route: `{ path, name, file }`. For `products/[productId]/index.ejs`, `path` is `/products/[productId]`, `name` is `index`, and `file` is `products/[productId]/index.ejs`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data

# Loading Data in PocketPages

You can load data right in a template, or in a `+page.js` file next to it.

## Inline data loading

The simplest way is a `<% %>` block at the top of your template:

```ejs
<%
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
%>

<h1>Products</h1>
<% for (const product of products) { %>
  <div class="product">
    <h2><%= product.getString('name') %></h2>
  </div>
<% } %>
```

## Server script blocks

For better formatting support in editors, you can write `<script server<%- '>' %>` instead of `<% %>`. They mean the same thing:

```ejs
<script server<%- '>' %>
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
  const categories = ctx.app.findAllRecords('categories')
</script>

<h1>Products by Category</h1>
<% for (const category of categories) { %>
  <h2><%= category.getString('name') %></h2>
<% } %>
```

## Structured loading with `+page.js`

A `+page.js` file keeps data loading and form handling out of the template:

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id)
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { qty } = ctx.req.body()
    // ...
    return ctx.res.redirect(`/products/${ctx.params.id}`, { flash: 'Added to cart' })
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/products/[id]/index.ejs -->
<h1><%= data.product.getString('name') %></h1>
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %><p><%= flash %></p><% } %>
```

### Exports

`+page.js` exports any of `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete`.

1. `load` runs first, for every method.
2. Then the handler for the request method runs, if there is one.
3. Then the page renders.

A handler can set fields on `ctx.data`, or return a plain object. A returned object is shallow-assigned into `ctx.data` (`Object.assign`); there is no deep merge.

```js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') }
  },
  get(ctx) {
    ctx.data.mode = 'view'
  },
}
```

If a handler sends a response (`ctx.res.redirect`, `json`, `html`, `text`, `file`, `sse`), the page doesn't render.

### One `+page.js` per folder

A `+page.js` applies to every page in its folder. Use `ctx.route.name` to tell them apart:

```js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    if (ctx.route.name === 'details') {
      ctx.data.reviews = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('reviews', 'product = {:id}', '-created', 20, 0, { id: ctx.params.id })
    }
  },
}
```

### Methods without a handler

Every handler is optional. A page renders for any method, like PHP, so a template can handle a form on its own:

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/contact.ejs, no +page.js -->
<% if (ctx.req.method === 'POST') { %>
  <p>Thanks, <%= ctx.req.body().name %>!</p>
<% } else { %>
  <form method="post"><input name="name" /><button>Send</button></form>
<% } %>
```

A `post` (or `put`, ...) handler in `+page.js` is the tidier place for form logic as a page grows, but you don't need
one. Only routes with nothing to render, [`+api.js`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes) and a `+page.js` without a page, answer `405`
for a method they have no handler for.

## Example: a contact form

```js
// pb_pages/contact/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') }
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, message, department } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      const record = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('messages'))
      record.set('email', email)
      record.set('message', message)
      record.set('department', department)
      ctx.app.save(record)
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: 'Failed to send message', values: { email, message, department } }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/contact', { flash: 'Thanks, we got your message.' })
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/contact/index.ejs -->
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %><p><%= flash %></p><% } %>
<% if (data.error) { %><mark><%= data.error %></mark><% } %>

<form method="post">
  <input name="email" type="email" value="<%= data.values?.email %>" />
  <select name="department">
    <% for (const d of data.departments) { %>
      <option value="<%= d.id %>"><%= d.getString('name') %></option>
    <% } %>
  </select>
  <textarea name="message"><%= data.values?.message %></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

## Pages without a template

A `+page.js` in a folder with no page file serves the folder's URL from JS. Use it for a page you'd rather build in
code, or for a URL that only acts and redirects:

```js
// pb_pages/logout/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```js
// pb_pages/hello/+page.js
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    return ctx.res.html(`<h1>Hello ${ctx.auth ? ctx.auth.getString('name') : 'there'}</h1>`)
  },
}
```

- With no template to render, each handler must send a response; returning without one is a 500.
- Methods without a handler answer `405`, `GET` included: `/logout` above only takes `POST`.
- Folder middleware runs; layouts don't, so wrap HTML yourself (or render a partial with `ctx.include`).
- Errors show your `+error.ejs` page. For JSON responses and JSON errors, use [`+api.js`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes) instead.

## Middleware or `+page.js`?

- Only the route's own folder's `+page.js` runs.
- Every `+middleware.js` from `pb_pages/` down to the route's folder runs, root first.

Use [middleware](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware) for data or checks that a whole section of the site shares.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes

# API Routes and JSON

A `+api.js` file serves its folder's URL without a template. Use it for JSON, feeds, webhooks and anything else that isn't an HTML page.

```js
// pb_pages/feeds/latest/+api.js
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20)
    return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) => ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') })))
  },
}
```

A request to `/feeds/latest` returns:

```json
[{ "id": "abc123", "title": "Hello" }]
```

## How it works

- `+api.js` has the same exports as `+page.js`: `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`.
- There is no template, so a handler must send a response. Returning without one is a `500`.
- `[param]` folders work as for pages: `products/[id]/+api.js` serves `/products/123`.
- A folder can't have both a `+api.js` and an `index` page.
- Middleware runs for API routes too.
- `ctx.httpError()` thrown in a `+api.js` answers with JSON: `{ "status": 404, "message": "..." }`.

## Sending responses

| Call | Sends |
|---|---|
| `ctx.res.json(data)` / `ctx.res.json(status, data)` | JSON |
| `ctx.res.text(text)` / `ctx.res.text(status, text)` | Plain text |
| `ctx.res.html(html)` / `ctx.res.html(status, html)` | HTML as-is, without layouts |
| `ctx.res.file(path)` | A file from `pb_pages` |
| `ctx.res.redirect(location)` | A redirect |
| `ctx.res.sse()` | A `text/event-stream` |

See [res](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res).

## JSON from a page

JSON is only sent through `ctx.res.json` (or a `+api.js`). Template output is never parsed as JSON, even if it looks like JSON. A page's `+page.js` can still answer with JSON for one method:

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id)
    return ctx.res.json({ id: product.id, name: product.getString('name') })
  },
}
```

## Keep `/api/` free

`/api/` belongs to PocketBase. Pages never see it, and a `pb_pages/api/` folder is an error at startup. Put your routes somewhere else, such as `feeds/`, `xapi/` or `hooks/`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ejs

# EJS

EJS is always on. There is nothing to install or configure.

## Tags

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<% code %>` | Run JS, no output |
| `<%= expr %>` | Output, HTML-escaped |
| `<%- expr %>` | Output, raw |
| `<%# comment %>` | Nothing |
| `<%%` | A literal `<%` |
| `-%>` | Also remove the newline right after the tag |
| `<%_` / `_%>` | Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line |
| `<script server<%- '>' %> code </script>` | Same as `<% code %>` |

## Escaping

`<%= %>` replaces `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` with `&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` `&#34;` `&#39;`. `null` and `undefined` output as an empty string.

```ejs
<p><%= '<b>"x"</b>' %></p>   <!-- <p>&lt;b&gt;&#34;x&#34;&lt;/b&gt;</p> -->
<p><%- '<b>raw</b>' %></p>    <!-- <p><b>raw</b></p> -->
<p><%= null %></p>            <!-- <p></p> -->
```

Use `<%-` only for HTML you trust, such as the output of `include()` or `slot()`.

## In scope

Inside a template you can use:

| Name | |
|---|---|
| `ctx` | The [request context](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx) |
| `data` | `ctx.data` |
| `params` | `ctx.params` |
| `include` | Render a [partial](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials) |
| `slot` | Define or read a [slot](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/layouts) |
| `asset` | `ctx.asset` |
| `meta` | `ctx.meta` |
| `require` | Load a module: a path, or a name looked up in `_private/` then `node_modules` (see [JavaScript Runtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm)) |

## Output
