A template returns its text. There is no `echo()`; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

```ejs
<ul>
<% for (const n of [1, 2]) { -%>
  <li><%= n %></li>
<% } -%>
</ul>
```

## Caching

A template is compiled once per content hash and reused, so an edited file is recompiled on the next request.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown

# Markdown Support

A `.md` file is a page, just like an `.ejs` file. Markdown is always on.

## How it works

1. **EJS first**: the file runs through EJS, so every [EJS tag](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ejs) works in Markdown.
2. **Then Markdown**: the result is rendered as Markdown: CommonMark plus GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists and autolinks.

## Front matter

YAML between `---` lines at the top of the file is front matter. Each top-level key is passed to `ctx.meta(key, value)`:

```markdown
---
title: My Blog Post
description: A detailed guide about something interesting
---

# Content starts here...
```

Read the values in a layout with `meta`:

```ejs
<title><%= meta('title') %></title>
<meta name="description" content="<%= meta('description') %>">
```

## Headings

Headings get `id`s, so you can link to them: the text is lowercased, characters other than `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`, `_` and space are removed, and spaces become `-`. `## Front matter` gets `id="front-matter"`.

## Images

Relative image paths go through [`ctx.asset`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset), so they get fingerprinted URLs:

```markdown
![Logo](logo.png)
```

## Markdown partials

A `.md` file in a `_private/` folder can be included from EJS with `include()`. It's rendered the same way, EJS then Markdown:

```ejs
<%- include('intro') %>
```

## Notes

- Layouts are `+layout.ejs`, `+layout.jsx` or `+layout.tsx`. A layout can't be Markdown: `+layout.md` is an error at
  startup. A Markdown page is still wrapped by the layouts above it.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx

# JSX and TSX

A `.jsx` or `.tsx` file is a template, just like an `.ejs` file. It can be a page, a layout (`+layout.tsx`), an error page (`+error.tsx`, `+404.tsx`) or a partial in `_private/`. PocketOne compiles it the first time it's used, with esbuild built into the binary: no Node, no `npm install`, no build step. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked.

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/[id].tsx
import Price from './_private/Price'

export default function Product({ data, slot }: any) {
  slot('title', data.product.getString('name'))
  return (
    <article class="product">
      <h1>{data.product.getString('name')}</h1>
      <Price cents={data.product.getInt('price')} />
    </article>
  )
}
```

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/_private/Price.tsx
export default ({ cents }: { cents: number }) => <span class="price">${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}</span>
```

## Props

The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. It gets:

| Prop | |
|---|---|
| `ctx` | The [request context](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx). |
| `data`, `params`, `meta` | The same as `ctx.data`, `ctx.params` and `ctx.meta`. |
| `asset`, `include` | The same helpers EJS templates have. `include(name, locals)` returns HTML you can put in JSX. |
| `slot` | `slot(name)` reads a named slot, `slot(name, content)` sets one, `slot()` is the inner content. |
| `children` | In a layout, the inner content. |

A partial also gets the locals it was included with, as props. EJS can include a `.jsx` or `.tsx` partial the same way: its locals become props.

## Server-rendered HTML only

JSX renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration and no client-side React.

- Event handler props (functions) are dropped. Use plain attributes: `onclick="..."`, `hx-get`, `data-on:click`.
- Text and attribute values are escaped. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }}` inserts raw HTML.
- `class` and `className` both work, as do `for` and `htmlFor`.
- `style` takes a string or an object: `{ marginTop: 4 }` renders `margin-top:4`.
- `true` renders a bare attribute. `false`, `null` and `undefined` leave it out.
- `<html>` gets `<!doctype html>` in front of it, since JSX can't write a doctype.

## Layouts

```tsx
// pb_pages/+layout.tsx
export default function Layout({ children, slot }: any) {
  return (
    <html>
      <head>
        <title>{slot('title')}</title>
      </head>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

Layouts in `.ejs`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` mix freely: an EJS page can sit inside a TSX layout and the other way round.

## TypeScript modules

`+page.ts`, `+api.ts`, `+middleware.ts`, `+config.ts` and any `.ts` file reached by `require` or `import` work like their `.js` versions. A module whose only export is `export default` behaves like `module.exports = ...`.

Components are ordinary modules, so `import Card from './_private/Card'` resolves the same way as [`require`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm). When a partial name has no extension, `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` are tried, in that order.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials

# Using Partials in PocketPages

Partials are reusable templates that you include from other templates. They live in `_private/` folders, which are never routed.

## Including a partial

```ejs
<%- include('nav') %>
<%- include('card', { product }) %>
```

- `include(name, locals?)` renders a template from a `_private/` folder and returns its text. Use `<%-` so its HTML isn't escaped.
- `name` may omit the extension; `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` are tried, in that order.
- The partial sees the same `ctx`, plus `locals` as top-level variables.
- `locals` is also the whole object, as in EJS. Use it for optional values: `<%= title %>` throws if `title` wasn't passed, but `<% if (locals.subtitle) { %>` doesn't.
- Including more than 32 levels deep is an error.

## Where partials are found

```
pb_pages/
  _private/
    header.ejs
    footer.ejs
  blog/
    _private/
      sidebar.ejs
    posts/
      _private/
        post-card.ejs
      index.ejs
```

PocketPages looks in `_private/` in the current template's folder, then in each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`.

```ejs
<!-- In blog/posts/index.ejs -->
<%- include('post-card', { post }) %>  <!-- blog/posts/_private/post-card.ejs -->
<%- include('sidebar') %>              <!-- blog/_private/sidebar.ejs -->
<%- include('header') %>               <!-- _private/header.ejs -->
```

A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`:

```ejs
<%- include('/header') %>  <!-- always pb_pages/_private/header.ejs -->
<%- include('/blog/_private/sidebar') %>  <!-- a path that names a _private folder: blog/_private/sidebar.ejs -->
```

The extension is optional. A dotted name such as `include('nav.main')` finds `nav.main.ejs`.

This means you can:

- Keep section-specific partials in that section's `_private/`.
- Hoist a shared partial up to a common parent.
- Override a parent's partial with a local one of the same name, and still reach the root one with `/name`.

## Passing data

Pass only what the partial needs:

```ejs
<%- include('user-card', { name: user.getString('name'), joined: user.getString('created') }) %>
```

```ejs
<!-- _private/user-card.ejs -->
<div class="card">
  <h3><%= name %></h3>
  <p>Joined <%= joined %></p>
</div>
```

Partials can also read `ctx`, `data` and `params` directly. Passing values explicitly keeps them easy to reuse.

## Markdown partials

A `.md` partial is rendered as EJS, then Markdown:

```ejs
<%- include('intro') %>  <!-- _private/intro.md -->
```

## JavaScript modules

`_private/` folders also hold JS modules. Load them with [`ctx.resolve()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve), which uses the same lookup.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/layouts

# Layouts and Slots

`+layout.ejs` files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every `+layout` from its own folder up to `pb_pages/`, applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout, written as `+layout.ejs`, `+layout.jsx` or `+layout.tsx`. A layout can't be Markdown: `+layout.md` is an error at startup.

```plaintext
pb_pages/
  +layout.ejs          # applied last (outermost)
  products/
    +layout.ejs        # applied first
    [id].ejs
```

For `/products/123`, `[id].ejs` renders, then `products/+layout.ejs` wraps it, then `+layout.ejs` wraps that.

## `slot()`

In a layout, `slot()` returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ejs -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <title>My Application</title>
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <%- slot() %>
  </main>
  <footer>&copy; <%= new Date().getFullYear() %> My Application</footer>
</body>
</html>
```

`<%- slot %>` without parentheses prints the same content, so 0.x layouts that wrote it still work.

## Named slots

A page (or an inner layout) defines a named slot with `slot(name, fn)`. `fn`'s output is captured and nothing is output in place. A layout reads it with `slot(name)`, which returns `''` if it isn't defined.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/products/[id].ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %><%= data.product.getString('name') %><% }) %>
<h1><%= data.product.getString('name') %></h1>
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ejs -->
<html>
  <head><title><%- slot('title') || 'My shop' %></title></head>
  <body><%- slot() %></body>
</html>
```

- Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout.
- Defining the same name again replaces it. Inside the new definition's `fn`, `slot(name)` still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it:

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/docs/+layout.ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Docs: <%- slot('title') %><% }) %>
<main><%- slot() %></main>
```

## Data in layouts

Layouts render after the page, with the same `ctx`. Everything middleware, `+page.js` and the page put on `ctx.data` or `ctx.meta` is there.

## When layouts are skipped

- When the response isn't HTML (a handler set another `Content-Type`).
- When a handler or middleware sent the response itself (`ctx.res.json`, `ctx.res.html`, `ctx.res.redirect`, ...).
- For `+api.js` routes, which have no template.
- After `ctx.res.layout(false)`, called from middleware, `+page.js` or the page itself.
- With the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar), for requests that carry `Datastar-Request: true`.

To serve HTML fragments without the site layout, call `ctx.res.layout(false)`, put the layout in a group (`(site)/+layout.ejs`) and the fragments outside it, or send them with `ctx.res.html()`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/private-files

# Working with Private Files and Directories

## Names that are never routed

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+` | Framework file (`+layout.ejs`, `+page.js`, ...) |
| `_` | Private. `_private/` folders hold partials and modules. Other `_` names are ignored. |
| `-` | Ignored (drafts, notes) |
| `.` | Ignored (dotfiles) |

```
pb_pages/
  _private/        # private (not routable)
  -drafts/         # ignored
  helpers/         # normal folder (routable)
  +page.js         # framework file (not routable)
  +layout.ejs      # framework file (not routable)
  index.ejs        # page
```

## The `_private` folder

`_private/` folders serve two purposes:

1. Template partials, rendered with [`include()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials)
2. JavaScript modules and other files, loaded with [`ctx.resolve()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve)

Both use the same lookup: `_private/` in the current template's folder, then each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`. A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`.

```
pb_pages/
  _private/
    header.ejs
    format.js
  products/
    _private/
      product-card.ejs
      queries.js
    index.ejs
```

```ejs
<!-- In products/index.ejs -->
<%
  const queries = ctx.resolve('queries')   // products/_private/queries.js
  const format = ctx.resolve('format')     // _private/format.js
%>
<%- include('header') %>                  <!-- _private/header.ejs -->
<% for (const p of queries.featured(ctx.app)) { %>
  <%- include('product-card', { p, format }) %>
<% } %>
```

## Modules

A module in `_private/` is a CommonJS file:

```js
// pb_pages/products/_private/queries.js
module.exports = {
  featured: (app) => app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'featured = true', '-created', 10),
}
```

## Notes

1. Files in `_private/` are never served.
2. Keep secrets in environment variables (see [Managing Secrets](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets)), not in files.
3. Keep private files close to where they're used, and hoist them up when several sections share them.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware

# Middleware

Middleware files (`+middleware.js`) run before your handlers and templates. Use them to:

- Check authentication
- Load data a whole section shares
- Set headers
- Validate requests

## Basic example

```js
// pb_pages/admin/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  ctx.data.section = 'admin'
  return next()
}
```

- One signature: `(ctx, next)`. Call `next()` to continue, and return its result.
- Returning without calling `next()` ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (a `500`; in dev mode the error page names the middleware file).
- Share data through `ctx.data`.

## Order

Every `+middleware.js` from `pb_pages/` down to the route's folder runs, root first. Groups count too.

```
pb_pages/
  +middleware.js         # runs first (all routes)
  products/
    +middleware.js       # runs second (/products/...)
    [id]/
      +middleware.js     # runs third (/products/[id])
```

The full order for a request is:

1. Plugins' `onRequest`
2. Middleware, root first
3. The folder's `+page.js` or `+api.js` (`load`, then the method's handler)
4. The template, then layouts, innermost first
5. The response

If any step sends a response, the later steps are skipped.

## Common uses

### Auth guard

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```

### Request validation

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!/^[a-z0-9]+$/.test(ctx.params.id)) throw ctx.httpError(400, 'Invalid ID')
  return next()
}
```

### Shared data

```js
// pb_pages/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.categories = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('categories', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
  return next()
}
```

```ejs
<nav>
  <% for (const c of data.categories) { %>
    <a href="/categories/<%= c.id %>"><%= c.getString('name') %></a>
  <% } %>
</nav>
```

### Headers

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.res.header('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY')
  return next()
}
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/asset-management

# Asset Management

Static files in `pb_pages` (images, CSS, JS, fonts) can be served with fingerprinted URLs that change when the file changes.

## Where to put assets

Anywhere in `pb_pages`, next to the pages that use them or in a shared folder:

```
pb_pages/
  assets/
    app.css
    logo.png
  feature/
    index.md
    header.jpg
```

## In templates

Use `asset()` (the same as `ctx.asset()`):

```ejs
<link rel="stylesheet" href="<%= asset('/assets/app.css') %>">
<img src="<%= asset('header.jpg') %>">
```

`asset('/assets/app.css')` returns something like `/assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css`.

- Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; `/`-paths from `pb_pages`.
- A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged.

## In Markdown

Relative image paths go through `asset()` automatically:

```markdown
![Header](header.jpg)
```

## How it works

1. A fingerprinted name carries the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: `name.<hash>.ext`.
2. Fingerprinted URLs are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
3. When the file changes, its hash and URL change, so browsers and CDNs fetch the new one.

See [asset](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset) and [Caching](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/caching).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content

# Serving Static Content in PocketPages

Any file in `pb_pages` that isn't a page (`.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`), a framework file (`+...`), private (`_...`) or ignored (names starting with `-` or `.`) is a static file. It's served as-is at its path, with groups removed:

```
pb_pages/
  assets/
    app.css            -> /assets/app.css
    logo.png           -> /assets/logo.png
  documents/
    terms.pdf          -> /documents/terms.pdf
  (marketing)/
    brochure.pdf       -> /brochure.pdf
  favicon.ico          -> /favicon.ico
  index.ejs            -> /  (a page, not static)
```

- The content type comes from the extension.
- The `ETag` comes from the content hash; a matching `If-None-Match` gets `304`.
- A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error).

For cache-friendly URLs, reference files through [`asset()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/asset-management).

## `pb_pages` and `pb_public`

A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, so you can keep using `pb_public` for files you don't want next to your pages.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets

# Managing Secrets in PocketPages

Keep API keys, passwords and other secrets in environment variables, and read them with `ctx.env(name)`. It returns `''` when the variable is unset.

```js
// pb_pages/checkout/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const key = ctx.env('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY')
    if (!key) throw new Error('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set')
    // ...
  },
}
```

`ctx.env` reads the app's environment. Under a multitenant host's sandbox, it reads the instance's environment.

## Best practices

1. **Never put secrets in the page.** Anything a template outputs goes to the browser.

   ```ejs
   <!-- DON'T -->
   <meta name="api-key" content="<%= ctx.env('API_KEY') %>">

   <!-- OK: a public value -->
   <meta name="api-endpoint" content="<%= ctx.env('PUBLIC_API_ENDPOINT') %>">
   ```

2. **Check for required variables** and fail clearly when one is missing.
3. **Use descriptive names**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, not `KEY`.
4. **Never commit secrets** to version control, and use different values in development and production.

## Setting environment variables

```bash
# Shell
export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
pocketone serve
```

```dockerfile
# Docker
ENV STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/config

# Configuration with `+config.js`

Create `pb_pages/+config.js` to configure PocketPages for the app. It's only allowed at the top of `pb_pages`; a `+config.js` in a subfolder is an error at startup.

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
  debug: false,
}
```

## Options

| Key | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins` | `[]` | Built-in plugins by name, or JS plugin factories. EJS and Markdown are always on. |
| `debug` | `false` | Detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output even outside dev mode. |

`+config.js` must export an object; exporting a function (0.x's `(api) => ({...})` form) is an error.

`+config.js` runs on each page request, so these aren't caught at startup: unknown keys, names that are neither a
module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error (a 500; dev mode shows the
reason on the page), and the reason goes to the log.

## Plugins

Each entry in `plugins` is one of:

- **A name**, loaded with `require`: a `_private/` file (`'datastar'` for the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar)),
  then a package in `node_modules`, then a built-in (`'auth'` or `'realtime'`). It must export a plugin factory. See
  [Plugins](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins).
- **A JS plugin factory**: a function that returns hooks, such as `require('./_private/my-plugin.js')`. A `require`
  with a path loads exactly that file, skipping the name lookup, so it's how you choose one copy over another.
- **An object with a factory and options**: `{ factory, ...options }`. The object is passed to the factory as its `config`.

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: [
    'auth',
    'realtime',
    { factory: require('./_private/banner.js'), text: 'Hello' },
  ],
}
```

Plugin hooks run in the order the plugins are listed. See [Plugin Authoring](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring).

## Debug

`debug: true` turns on what dev mode (`--dev`) turns on: detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output. See [Debugging](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/debugging).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/caching

# Understanding Caching in PocketPages

## Fingerprinted assets

`asset()` adds a content hash to a file's URL:

```ejs
<img src="<%= asset('/images/logo.png') %>">
<!-- <img src="/images/logo.3f9a1c2b7d4e.png"> -->
```

- The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256.
- Fingerprinted URLs are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, so browsers and CDNs keep them for a year.
- When the file changes, the hash changes, and so does the URL. Old copies are never served for the new URL.
- A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged (and not fingerprinted).

## Static files

Every static file gets an `ETag` from its content hash. A request with a matching `If-None-Match` gets `304 Not Modified`.

## Templates

A template is compiled once per content hash and reused. Edit a file and the next request uses the new version, in every mode.

## Routes

The route table is built at startup and rebuilt whenever anything in `pb_pages` changes. A rebuild never restarts the app.

## Pages

Rendered pages aren't cached. To let browsers or a CDN cache a page, set a header in a handler or middleware:

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.res.header('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=60')
  return next()
}
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors

# Errors

## Thrown errors

Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a `500`.

- **Dev mode or `debug: true`:** an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the `.ejs` or `.md` source), and the stack trimmed to `pb_pages`-relative paths.
- **Otherwise:** a plain "Something went wrong" page.

The full error always goes to the app's log.

## `ctx.httpError(status, message)`

Throw `ctx.httpError()` to answer with a specific status:

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    let product
    try {
      product = ctx.app.findFirstRecordByData('products', 'slug', ctx.params.id)
    } catch (e) {
      throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such product') // findFirstRecordByData throws when nothing matches
    }
    ctx.data.product = product
  },
}
```

- In a page, it sends that status with a plain page showing `message`.
- In a `+api.js`, it sends JSON: `{ "status": 404, "message": "No such product" }`.

## A custom error page

Create `pb_pages/+error.ejs`. It renders for every `ctx.httpError` and for every `500` outside dev mode, inside the root layout, with `ctx.error = { status, message }`:

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+error.ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Error <%= ctx.error.status %><% }) %>
<h1><%= ctx.error.status %></h1>
<p><%= ctx.error.message %></p>
```

`+error` and `+404` live only at the top of `pb_pages`. Either may be `.ejs`, `.jsx` or `.tsx`.

## A custom 404 page

Create `pb_pages/+404.ejs`. It renders inside the root layout, with status `404`, for a `GET` or `HEAD` that nothing answers: no page, no file in `pb_public` and no PocketBase route. It never renders for `/api/` or `/_/`. The root `+middleware.js` runs first, and page code can still change the status.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+404.ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Not found<% }) %>
<h1>Not found</h1>
<p>Nothing lives at <%= ctx.req.url.pathname %>.</p>
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/debugging

# Debugging in PocketPages

## Dev mode

Run `pocketone` with `--dev`:

```bash
pocketone serve --dev
```

Dev mode turns on:

- detailed error pages (message, file and line, trimmed stack; see [Errors](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors));
- `ctx.log.debug` output.

## `debug: true`

To get the same in production, set `debug: true` in `+config.js`:

```js
module.exports = {
  debug: true,
}
```

Turn it off again when you're done. Detailed error pages show error messages, file paths and stack traces to anyone who triggers an error.

## Logging

`ctx.log` writes to the app's log:

```js
ctx.log.debug('loaded product', ctx.params.id)  // only in dev mode or with debug: true
ctx.log.info('order placed')
ctx.log.warn('stock is low')
ctx.log.error('payment failed')
```

See [log](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/log).

## Template changes

Templates are cached by content hash and the route table is rebuilt on any file change, in every mode. If a change doesn't show, check the app's log for a startup error (bad file name, route conflict): the previous route table keeps serving until the error is fixed.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/deploying

# Going Live

A PocketPages app is a `pb_pages` folder. To go live, run PocketOne on your server (pages is built in) and put `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`, along with your other `pb_*` folders:

```
pb_data/
pb_hooks/
pb_migrations/
pb_public/
pb_pages/
```

Or point `pocketone` at it with `--pagesDir`.

## Updating

Copy the changed files into `pb_pages`. The route table is rebuilt on any change, and templates are cached by content hash, so updates show on the next request without restarting the app. If an update has a startup error (a bad name or a route conflict), it's logged with the file path and the previous route table keeps serving.

## Before you go live

- Run without `--dev`, and keep `debug: false` in `+config.js`.
- Set secrets as environment variables (see [Managing Secrets](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets)).
- Serve over HTTPS. Cookies set with `ctx.res.cookie` are marked `Secure` on HTTPS requests.

## Multitenant hosts

Under a multitenant PocketOne host, every instance has its own `pb_pages`, and page code runs with the same limits as the rest of the instance's JS.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins

# Plugins

Plugins add features to `ctx` and hook into each request. Turn them on in `+config.js`:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
}
```

Each entry is one of:

- **A name in quotes.** It's loaded with `require`, which looks in this order:
  1. a `_private/` folder in `pb_pages` (`'datastar'` finds `_private/datastar.js`)
  2. `pb_pages/node_modules`, for a package from your `package.json`
  3. the built-in plugins, `'auth'` and `'realtime'`

  A path such as `'./plugins/my-plugin.js'` works too.
- **A plugin factory**, usually `require('./_private/my-plugin.js')`. Writing the `require` yourself with a path skips
  the lookup above and loads exactly that file, which is how you pick one copy over another: `'datastar'` would find
  `_private/datastar.js` first, while `require('./node_modules/datastar')` always loads the package.

Datastar isn't built in. It's an add-on file you copy into `pb_pages/_private/` and list by name.

EJS and Markdown are always on; they aren't plugins.

## Built-in plugins

| Name | Adds |
|---|---|
| [`auth`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth) | Cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: sets `ctx.auth` from the `pb_auth` cookie and adds `ctx.session.*` sign-in methods. |
| [`realtime`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime) | `ctx.realtime.send()` to PocketBase realtime subscribers. |

## JS plugins

A JS plugin is a module that exports a factory returning hooks. List it by name, or `require()` it yourself, which you
need for options (`{ factory, ...options }`):

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'my-plugin', { factory: require('./_private/other-plugin.js'), color: 'blue' }],
}
```

See [Plugin Authoring](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring).

| Add-on | Adds |
|---|---|
| [Datastar](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar) | `ctx.datastar.*` helpers for [Datastar](https://data-star.dev). Copy [`addons/datastar.js`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/datastar.js) into `pb_pages/_private/`; the `datastar` starter kit already has it. |

## Order

Plugins' hooks run in the order they're listed, and `onRequest` hooks run before any middleware.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth

# Authentication Plugin

The `auth` plugin gives you cookie sessions on PocketBase auth. It calls the app directly, not over HTTP.

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth'],
}
```

## What it does on every request

It reads the `pb_auth` cookie, validates the token and sets `ctx.auth` to the authenticated record. A bad cookie is cleared.

`ctx.auth` is also set without the plugin when a request carries PocketBase's own `Authorization` header.

## `ctx.session`

| Method | |
|---|---|
| `register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true }?)` | Create an auth record. `data` holds extra fields. `verify` sends the verification email; `signIn` signs the new account in (returns `{ token: '', record }` when `false`). |
| `signInWithPassword(email, password, { collection }?)` | Sign in with a password. |
| `requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false }?)` | Send a one-time password. Returns the `otpId`. An unknown email still gets an id, one that never validates; with `create: true` the account is created first. |
| `signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection }?)` | Sign in with a one-time password. |
| `signInAnonymously({ collection }?)` | Sign in as a new anonymous user. |
| `requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true }?)` | Store state in a cookie and return the provider's URL. With `redirect` it also sends the redirect; pass `redirect: false` to send the URL some other way. `redirectPath` must be a path on this site. |
| `signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?)` | Complete an OAuth2 sign-in on the redirect path. Returns `{ token, record, meta }`; `meta.isNew` is `true` for a new account. |
| `signIn(record)` | Set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself. It skips the MFA check below. |
| `signOut()` | Sign out. |
| `authMethods({ collection }?)` | The sign-in methods a collection has turned on: `{ password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa: { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } }`, as PocketBase's auth-methods API. |

### MFA

Pages doesn't have a second sign-in step yet. If a collection has MFA turned on (Collections → `users` → Options →
Multi-factor authentication) and its MFA rule matches the account, every sign-in method above refuses it with "This
account needs a second sign-in step (MFA), which pages doesn't support yet." An empty rule matches every account. To
use pages sign-in, turn MFA off for the collection, or give it a rule that leaves out the accounts that sign in here.

Every sign-in method sets `ctx.auth` for the rest of the request and returns `{ token, record }`.

### Email flows

These use PocketBase's own checks and mail templates. The request methods never reveal whether an email exists.

| Method | |
|---|---|
| `requestVerification(email, { collection }?)` | Send the verification email (skipped for an account that's already verified). |
| `confirmVerification(token)` | Mark the account verified. Returns the record. |
| `requestPasswordReset(email, { collection }?)` | Send the password reset email. |
| `confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm)` | Set the new password (and mark the account verified). Returns the record. |
| `requestEmailChange(newEmail)` | Send a confirmation email to `newEmail`. Needs a signed-in user (`ctx.auth`). |
| `confirmEmailChange(token, password)` | Change the email after checking the current password. Returns the record. |

A bad or expired token throws an error.

## Example

```js
// pb_pages/login/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, password } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password)
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: 'Invalid email or password', email }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```js
// pb_pages/logout/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

See the [Authentication guide](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication) for complete flows: registration, one-time passwords, OAuth2 and anonymous sign-in.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar

# Datastar Add-on

The Datastar add-on adds helpers for [Datastar](https://data-star.dev). It's a JS plugin that ships with PocketPages
rather than a built-in: copy [`addons/datastar.js`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/datastar.js)
into `pb_pages/_private/` (the `datastar` starter kit already has it) and list it in `+config.js` by name:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['datastar'],
}
```

Add the script tags to your root layout's `<head>`. They load [Datastar](https://data-star.dev) v1.0.5. Datastar 1.0 uses
a colon between the attribute name and its key (`data-on:click`, `data-bind:name`, `data-signals:count`,
`data-class:active`, `data-attr:href`); the older hyphen form (`data-on-click`) is ignored. See the
[Datastar attribute reference](https://data-star.dev/reference/attributes).

```ejs
<head>
  <%- ctx.datastar.scripts() %>
</head>
```

## `ctx.datastar`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `scripts({ spa, realtime }?)` | Returns the script tags. |
| `patchElements(html, { selector, mode, useViewTransition, viewTransitionSelector, namespace }?)` | Sends a patch-elements SSE event on the current response. `mode` is `outer` (default), `inner`, `replace`, `prepend`, `append`, `before`, `after` or `remove`; `namespace` is `html` (default), `svg` or `mathml`. |
| `patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?)` | Sends a patch-signals SSE event (JSON Merge Patch: `null` removes a signal). |
| `executeScript(js, { autoRemove, attributes }?)` | Sends a script to run in the browser. |
| `consoleLog(msg)` / `consoleError(err)` | Logs to the browser console. |
| `redirect(url)` | Sends the browser to `url` (a full page load). A Datastar fetch can't follow `ctx.res.redirect`, so use this from `@get`/`@post` handlers. |
| `dispatchCustomEvent(name, detail, { selector }?)` | Fires a `CustomEvent` on `document`, or on the elements matching `selector`. |
| `replaceURL(url)` | Changes the address bar without a navigation (`history.replaceState`). |
| `prefetch(urls)` | Adds speculation rules so the browser prefetches `urls`. |
| `signals()` | Reads the request's signals as an object: from the `datastar` query parameter for GET and DELETE, from the body otherwise. |
| `readSignals(target)` | Merges the request's signals into `target` and returns it (0.x's `readSignals(request, target)` also works). |
| `realtime.*` | Sends the same patches to realtime subscribers. Needs the [`realtime`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime) plugin. |

Every send also takes `eventId` and `retryDuration` (in ms; the default 1000 isn't sent).

## Pages as patches

When a request has the `Datastar-Request: true` header, the rendered page is sent without layouts, as a `patchElements` event. If the request has a `Datastar-Selector` header, the patch goes into that element.

This is how this site navigates between docs pages: the layout calls

```ejs
<%- ctx.datastar.scripts({ spa: { scope: '#toc', selector: '#content' } }) %>
```

so links in the table of contents fetch the page and patch it into `#content`. Plain left-clicks are intercepted;
modified clicks (Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt, middle-click), links with a `target` attribute and links to other origins navigate
normally. Back/Forward work, including back to the page you landed on: each page opens at the top, and Back/Forward
return you to where you were scrolled.

## Example: a counter

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/counter/index.ejs -->
<button data-on:click="@post('/counter')">
  Count: <span id="count"><%= ctx.store('count') || 0 %></span>
</button>
```

```js
// pb_pages/counter/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const count = (ctx.store('count') || 0) + 1
    ctx.store('count', count)
    ctx.datastar.patchElements(`<span id="count">${count}</span>`)
  },
}
```

## Example: reading signals

```js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { name, email } = ctx.datastar.signals()
    if (!name || !email) {
      ctx.datastar.patchSignals({ error: 'Please fill all fields' })
      return
    }
    ctx.datastar.patchElements('<div id="form">Thanks!</div>')
  },
}
```

## Broadcasting

With the `realtime` plugin on, `ctx.datastar.realtime.*` sends patches to every realtime subscriber instead of the current response:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime', 'datastar'] }
```

```js
ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements(`<span id="count">${count}</span>`)
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime

# Realtime Plugin

The `realtime` plugin sends messages to [PocketBase realtime](https://pocketbase.io/docs/realtime/) subscribers.

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['realtime'],
}
```

## `ctx.realtime.send(topic, data, { filter }?)`

Sends `data` to the subscribers of `topic`. `filter(client)` may limit the recipients.

```js
// pb_pages/ping/+api.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.realtime.send('ping', { at: new Date().toISOString() })
    return ctx.res.json({ ok: true })
  },
}
```

On the client, subscribe with the PocketBase JS SDK:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/pocketbase/dist/pocketbase.umd.js"></script>
<script>
  const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin)
  pb.realtime.subscribe('ping', (data) => console.log('Received:', data))
</script>
```

## Filtering recipients

```js
ctx.realtime.send('alerts', 'Maintenance at 10:00', {
  filter: (client) => !!client.get('auth'),
})
```

## Sending HTML

For hypermedia libraries (HTMX, Datastar), send rendered HTML. `include()` is available in templates, so render the partial there:

```js
// pb_pages/xapi/chat/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post() {}, // accept POST; the page renders and sends
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/chat/index.ejs -->
<% ctx.realtime.send('chat', include('chat-msg', { message: ctx.req.body().message })) %>
```

See [Realtime Events](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/realtime) and the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar), which can send Datastar patches over realtime.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring

# Plugin Authoring Guide

A JS plugin is a factory that returns hooks:

```js
// pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.js
module.exports = (config) => ({
  name: 'my-plugin',
  onRequest(ctx) {},                                   // before middleware
  extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () => 'hi' },
  transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html },      // after each template or layout renders
})
```

Turn it on in `+config.js`:

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['my-plugin'], // pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.js
}
```

## `config`

`config` is the plugin's entry in `+config.js` when that entry is an object (`{ factory, ...options }`), else `{}`:

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: [{ factory: require('./_private/banner.js'), text: 'Beta' }],
}
```

```js
// pb_pages/_private/banner.js
module.exports = (config) => ({
  name: 'banner',
  transform({ html }) {
    return html.replace('<body>', `<body><div class="banner">${config.text}</div>`)
  },
})
```

## Hooks

Every hook is optional. Hooks run in the order plugins are listed in `+config.js`.

| Hook | When |
|---|---|
| `name` | The plugin's name. |
| `onRequest(ctx)` | At the start of each request, before middleware. |
| `extendContext(ctx)` | Add members to `ctx`. |
| `transform({ html, ctx, file })` | After each template or layout renders. Return the new HTML. |

## Example: a context helper

```js
module.exports = () => ({
  name: 'format',
  extendContext(ctx) {
    ctx.formatDate = (d) => new Date(d).toLocaleDateString()
  },
})
```

```ejs
<p>Posted <%= ctx.formatDate(data.post.getString('created')) %></p>
```

## Permissions

JS plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's JS. Under a multitenant host, that means the instance's sandbox.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx

# The `ctx` Object

PocketPages creates one `ctx` object per request and passes it to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.

```js
// +middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => next()

// +page.js / +api.js
module.exports = { load(ctx) {} }
```

```ejs
<!-- any template -->
<p><%= ctx.req.url.pathname %></p>
```

In templates, `data`, `params`, `asset` and `meta` are shortcuts for `ctx.data`, `ctx.params`, `ctx.asset` and `ctx.meta`.

## Members

| Member | |
|---|---|
| [`ctx.req`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/req) | The request: method, URL, query, headers, cookies, body, files |
| [`ctx.res`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res) | The response: status, headers, cookies, redirects, JSON, HTML, text, files, SSE |
| [`ctx.data`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data) | Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates |
| [`ctx.params`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data#ctxparams) | Route parameters |
| [`ctx.route`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data#ctxroute) | The matched route: `{ path, name, file }` |
| [`ctx.flash()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash) | The one-time message from the previous redirect |
| [`ctx.auth`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/auth) | The authenticated record, or `null` |
| [`ctx.app`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/app) | The app (`$app`) |
| [`ctx.pb()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/pb) | A JS SDK client acting as the visitor (API rules apply) |
| [`ctx.env(name)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/env) | Environment variable |
| [`ctx.log`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/log) | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` |
| [`ctx.meta(key, value?)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/meta) | Per-request page metadata |
| [`ctx.asset(path)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset) | Fingerprinted URL for a static file |
| [`ctx.include(name, locals?)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials) | Render a `_private/` partial from JS and get its text (same lookup as `include`, from the route's folder) |
| [`ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve) | Load a module from `_private/` |
| [`ctx.store(name, value?)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/store) | The app's in-memory store |
| `ctx.pagesDir` | Absolute path of the app's `pb_pages` folder (read-only), e.g. for `$os.readDir` |
| `ctx.dev` | `true` in dev mode |
| [`ctx.httpError(status, message)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors) | An error to throw for a specific status |
| [`ctx.error`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors) | `{ status, message }`, in `+error.ejs` |

## Added by plugins

| Member | Plugin |
|---|---|
| `ctx.session` | [auth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth) |
| `ctx.realtime` | [realtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime) |
| `ctx.datastar` | [datastar](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar) |

JS plugins can add their own members with [`extendContext`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/req

# `ctx.req`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `method` | `"GET"`, `"POST"`, ... |
| `url` | `{ href, origin, pathname, search }` |
| `query(name)` | First value of a query parameter as a string, or `undefined` |
| `query(name, { all: true })` | Every value, as an array of strings |
| `query()` | `{ name: firstValue }` for every parameter |
| `header(name)` | Request header, `''` if absent |
| `cookie(name)` | Cookie value as a string, or `undefined` |
| `cookie(name, { json: true })` | Cookie parsed as JSON (`undefined` if absent or not JSON) |
| `cookies()` | `{ name: value }`, strings |
| `body()` | Parsed body: a JSON object, or form fields as `{ name: value }` (repeated names as arrays) |
| `files(name)` | Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase `*filesystem.File` values ready for a record field |
| `ip` | Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) |
| `event` | The underlying PocketBase `RequestEvent`, for anything not covered here |

Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

## Examples

```ejs
<p>You asked for <%= ctx.req.url.pathname %><%= ctx.req.url.search %></p>
<p>Page <%= Number(ctx.req.query('page') ?? 1) %></p>
<p>Browser: <%= ctx.req.header('User-Agent') %></p>
```

### Forms

`body()` parses JSON, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data`:

```js
// pb_pages/contact/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, message } = ctx.req.body()
    // ...
  },
}
```

### File uploads

```html
<form method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <input type="file" name="avatar" />
  <button>Upload</button>
</form>
```

```js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const record = ctx.app.findRecordById('users', ctx.auth.id)
    record.set('avatar', ctx.req.files('avatar')[0])
    ctx.app.save(record)
    return ctx.res.redirect('/account')
  },
}
```

### Cookies

```js
const theme = ctx.req.cookie('theme')                     // 'dark' or undefined
const prefs = ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true }) ?? {}
```

Set cookies with [`ctx.res.cookie()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res#cookies).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res

# `ctx.res`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `status(code)` | Status for the rendered page. Returns `ctx.res`. |
| `header(name, value)` | Set a response header. `header(name)` reads it back. |
| `cookie(name, value, options?)` | Set a cookie. |
| `clearCookie(name, options?)` | Expire a cookie (same `path` / `domain` as when set). |
| `redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?)` or `redirect(location, status)` | Send a redirect. `status` must be a 3xx code. `flash` sets a [one-time message](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash). |
| `json(data)` / `json(status, data)` | Send JSON. |
| `html(html)` / `html(status, html)` | Send HTML as-is (no layouts). |
| `text(text)` / `text(status, text)` | Send plain text. |
| `file(path)` | Send a file from `pb_pages` (path relative to `pb_pages`). |
| `sse()` | Start a `text/event-stream` response. |
| `layout(false)` | Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). Returns `ctx.res`. |
| `sent` | `true` once a response has been sent. |

Once a response is sent, the later steps of the request (handlers, template, layouts) are skipped.

## Status and headers

```ejs
<% ctx.res.status(404).header('Cache-Control', 'no-store') %>
<h1>Not here</h1>
```

## Redirects

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
return ctx.res.redirect('/new-home', 301) // or { status: 301 }
```

## Cookies

```js
ctx.res.cookie('theme', 'dark', { maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 365 })
ctx.res.cookie('prefs', { compact: true })   // objects are JSON.stringify'd
ctx.res.clearCookie('theme')
```

- Non-string values are `JSON.stringify`'d. The value is then percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`), and `ctx.req.cookie` decodes it.
- Defaults: `path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` when the request is HTTPS.
- Options: `path`, `domain`, `maxAge` (seconds), `expires` (a `Date`, milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string; with `maxAge` too, browsers use `maxAge`), `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`.

## JSON, HTML, text and files

```js
return ctx.res.json({ ok: true })
return ctx.res.json(201, { id: record.id })
return ctx.res.html('<p>Fragment</p>')
return ctx.res.text(404, 'Not found')
return ctx.res.file('downloads/manual.pdf')
```

## Server-sent events

`sse()` starts a `text/event-stream` response and returns `{ send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() }`:

```js
// pb_pages/clock/+api.js
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const stream = ctx.res.sse()
    stream.send('time', new Date().toISOString())
    stream.close()
  },
}
```

Streaming is only available through `sse()`. Templates return their text all at once.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data

# `ctx.data`, `ctx.params`, `ctx.route`

## `ctx.data`

A plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. It starts as `{}`. In templates it's also available as `data`.

```js
// +middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.user = ctx.auth
  return next()
}
```

```js
// +page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') }  // Object.assign'd into ctx.data
  },
}
```

```ejs
<% for (const p of data.products) { %>
  <li><%= p.getString('name') %></li>
<% } %>
```

A handler's returned object is shallow-assigned into `ctx.data`. There is no deep merge.

## `ctx.params`

Route parameters from `[name]` segments, as strings. Never includes query parameters (use [`ctx.req.query()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/req)). In templates it's also available as `params`.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/[org]/[repo]/index.ejs, at /acme/web -->
<p><%= params.org %>/<%= params.repo %></p>  <!-- acme/web -->
```

## `ctx.route`

`{ path, name, file }`: the route pattern, the page name and its file relative to `pb_pages`.

| Page file | `path` | `name` |
|---|---|---|
| `products/[id].ejs` | `/products/[id]` | `[id]` |
| `docs/index.md` | `/docs` | `index` |

A `+page.js` applies to every page in its folder; use `ctx.route.name` to tell them apart.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash

# `ctx.flash()`

A flash is a one-time message that survives one redirect, such as "Saved" after a form post.

## Setting a flash

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
```

The message is stored as JSON in a cookie (`pp_flash`, `HttpOnly`, `Max-Age=300`). It can be any JSON value:

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/cart', { flash: { type: 'success', text: 'Added to cart' } })
```

## Reading it

On the next request, `ctx.flash()` returns the message and clears the cookie. It returns `undefined` when there is none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value.

```ejs
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %>
  <div class="alert alert-<%= flash.type %>"><%= flash.text %></div>
<% } %>
```

Read it in your layout to show flashes on every page.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/auth

# `ctx.auth`

The authenticated record, or `null`. It's set by:

- PocketBase's own auth, when the request has an `Authorization` header;
- the [`auth` plugin](../plugins/auth.md), from its `pb_auth` cookie.

```ejs
<% if (ctx.auth) { %>
  <p>Welcome, <%= ctx.auth.email() %></p>
  <% if (!ctx.auth.verified()) { %><p>Please verify your email.</p><% } %>
<% } else { %>
  <a href="/login">Log in</a>
<% } %>
```

`ctx.auth` is a PocketBase record, so the usual record methods work: `get(field)`, `getString(field)`, `email()`, `verified()`, `isSuperuser()`, `collection()`.

## Protecting pages

```js
// pb_pages/account/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/app

# `ctx.app`

The app (`$app`): records, collections, settings. Page code calls it directly, with no HTTP round trip.

```js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return {
      product: ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id),
      latest: ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 10),
    }
  },
}
```

Everything in PocketBase's [JavaScript records](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-records/) and [database](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-database/) docs that uses `$app` works on `ctx.app`.

Calls through `ctx.app` don't apply collection API rules: page code is trusted server code. Check `ctx.auth` yourself before reading or changing data on a user's behalf.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/pb

# `ctx.pb()`: the JS SDK in page code

`ctx.pb()` returns a [PocketBase JS SDK](https://github.com/pocketbase/js-sdk) client, the same API you use in the
browser:

```js
// pb_pages/posts/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    const page = ctx.pb().collection('posts').getList(1, 20, {
      filter: 'published = true',
      sort: '-created',
      expand: 'author',
    })
    return { posts: page.items }
  },
}
```

- **It acts as the visitor.** When someone is signed in (`ctx.auth`, for example through the `auth` plugin), the
  client is authenticated as them; otherwise it's a guest. Your collections' API rules, `expand` and hidden fields
  apply exactly as they would in the browser.
- **It's synchronous.** Calls return their result directly; no `await`.
- **No network.** Requests go straight to your app's own API, in-process. There's no host or port to set, and
  it works the same on any server.
- **Errors** throw the SDK's `ClientResponseError`:

  ```js
  try {
    const post = ctx.pb().collection('posts').getOne(ctx.params.id)
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.status === 404) throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such post')
    throw e
  }
  ```

- **Limits:** only `/api/` routes; file uploads through the SDK aren't supported, so use `ctx.app` for those.

## `ctx.pb()` or `ctx.app`?

| | `ctx.pb()` | `ctx.app` |
|---|---|---|
| Permissions | the visitor's: API rules apply | full access, no rules |
| API | the JS SDK, same as the browser | PocketBase's JSVM API (`findRecordsByFilter`, `save`, ...) |
| Use it for | reading and writing on the visitor's behalf | admin work, background jobs, anything rules shouldn't limit |

When in doubt, use `ctx.pb()`: if a page shows something, the visitor is allowed to see it.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/env

# `ctx.env(name)`

Returns an environment variable, or `''` if it's unset.

```js
const key = ctx.env('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY')
```

It reads the app's environment. Under a multitenant host's sandbox, it reads the instance's environment.

See [Managing Secrets](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/log

# `ctx.log`

Writes to the app's log.

```js
ctx.log.debug('cart', ctx.data.cart)
ctx.log.info('order placed')
ctx.log.warn('stock is low')
ctx.log.error('payment failed')
```

`debug` only shows in dev mode (`--dev`) or with `debug: true` in `+config.js`. See [Debugging](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/debugging).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/meta

# `ctx.meta(key, value?)`

A per-request key/value store for page metadata (title, description). Set with two arguments, read with one. In templates it's also available as `meta`.

```ejs
<!-- a page -->
<% meta('title', data.product.getString('name')) %>
<% meta('description', data.product.getString('summary')) %>
```

```ejs
<!-- +layout.ejs -->
<title><%= meta('title') || 'My shop' %></title>
<meta name="description" content="<%= meta('description') %>">
```

Layouts render after the page, so they see what the page set.

## Front matter

In a `.md` page, each top-level key of the YAML front matter is passed to `ctx.meta(key, value)`:

```markdown
---
title: About us
description: Who we are
---
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset

# `ctx.asset(path)`

Returns the URL for a static file in `pb_pages`, with its content hash. In templates it's also available as `asset`.

```ejs
<link rel="stylesheet" href="<%= asset('/assets/app.css') %>">
<!-- <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css"> -->
```

- Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; `/`-paths from `pb_pages`.
- A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged.
- The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: `name.<hash>.ext`.
- Fingerprinted URLs are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

Relative image paths in Markdown pages go through `ctx.asset` automatically.

See [Asset Management](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/asset-management).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve

# `ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?)`

Loads a module from a `_private/` folder. The lookup starts at the **route's** folder (the page being served), wherever `ctx.resolve` is called from, so a layout or partial gets the same answer as the page: `_private/` in the route's folder, then each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`. A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`. Without an extension, the name, then `.js`, `.ts` and `.json` are tried.

```js
// pb_pages/_private/shout.js
module.exports = (s) => String(s).toUpperCase()
```

```ejs
<p><%= ctx.resolve('shout')('hi') %></p>  <!-- HI -->
```

## Modes

| Mode | Returns |
|---|---|
| `require` (default) | The module's exports |
| `raw` | The file's text |
| `script` | The text wrapped in `<script>` |
| `style` | The text wrapped in `<style>` |

```ejs
<head>
  <%- ctx.resolve('theme.css', { mode: 'style' }) %>
  <%- ctx.resolve('widgets.js', { mode: 'script' }) %>
</head>
```

## Modules from `node_modules`

Page code can also `require()` by name: `_private/` folders first (nearest to the file calling `require`), then packages from `pb_pages/node_modules`, then the app's usual module paths. See [JavaScript Runtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/store

# `ctx.store(name, value?)`

The app's in-memory store (`$app.store()`). Set with two arguments, read with one.

```js
ctx.store('visits', (ctx.store('visits') || 0) + 1)
```

```ejs
<p>Visits since start: <%= ctx.store('visits') %></p>
```

- Values are shared by every request to the app.
- The store lives in memory: it's empty again after the app restarts. Keep anything that must last in a collection.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm

# JavaScript Runtime

Middleware, handlers, templates and plugins run in PocketBase's JavaScript runtime. It is neither a browser nor Node.js, so there are no Web APIs or Node APIs such as `Buffer` and `require('fs')`.

Each request runs as one unit under the app's usual JS limits (execution time, memory). Under a multitenant host, that's the instance's sandbox.

## Talking to the app

Use [`ctx.app`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/app), which is `$app`. PocketBase's [JS docs](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-overview/) cover [database operations](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-database/) and [record operations](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-records/):

```js
const records = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter(
  'articles',
  'status = {:status} && author = {:author}',
  '-created',
  20,
  0,
  { status: 'pending', author: ctx.auth.id }
)
```

## Can I use my favorite npm package?

Maybe. Page code can `require()` modules by name from `_private/` folders (nearest first), then from `pb_pages/node_modules`, then `pb_hooks/node_modules` and the app folder's `node_modules`, then from the app's usual module paths. A `_private/` file with the same name as a package wins. Packages that are plain CommonJS JavaScript, with no Node or browser APIs, have the best chance of working.

Install packages in the app folder (next to `pb_pages`), not inside `pb_pages`. Every file in `pb_pages` that isn't
private is served, so a `package.json` there would be public:

```bash
cd myapp
npm install some-package
```

```js
const somePackage = require('some-package')
```

Your own modules go in `_private/` and load with [`ctx.resolve()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication

# Authentication

PocketPages keeps PocketBase auth in a cookie with the built-in [`auth` plugin](plugins/auth.md). Turn it on:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth'],
}
```

## How a request is authenticated

- If the request has PocketBase's own `Authorization` header, `ctx.auth` is that record.
- Otherwise, the `auth` plugin reads the `pb_auth` cookie, validates the token and sets `ctx.auth` (or clears a bad cookie).
- With neither, `ctx.auth` is `null`.

Every `ctx.session` sign-in method sets the cookie, sets `ctx.auth` for the rest of the request, and returns `{ token, record }`. `ctx.session.signOut()` clears it.

## Protecting pages

```js
// pb_pages/account/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```

```ejs
<% if (ctx.auth) { %>
  <p>Welcome, <%= ctx.auth.email() %></p>
  <form method="post" action="/logout"><button>Log out</button></form>
<% } else { %>
  <a href="/login">Log in</a>
<% } %>
```

## Passwords

```js
// pb_pages/login/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, password } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password)
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: e.message, email }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/login/index.ejs -->
<form method="post">
  <label>Email</label>
  <input name="email" type="email" value="<%= data.email %>" />
  <label>Password</label>
  <input name="password" type="password" />
  <button type="submit">Log in</button>
</form>
<% if (data.error) { %><mark><%= data.error %></mark><% } %>
```

### Registration

```js
// pb_pages/register/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, password, name } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      ctx.session.register(email, password, { data: { name } })
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: `Error registering: ${e.message}` }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/', { flash: 'Welcome!' })
  },
}
```

## One-time passwords

A two-step form: request a code, then sign in with it. Turn on OTP for the collection in the dashboard and set up mail (Settings > Mail settings).

```js
// pb_pages/login/otp/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { step, email, otpId, code } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      if (step === 'request') {
        return { otpId: ctx.session.requestOTP(email), email }
      }
      ctx.session.signInWithOTP(otpId, code)
      return ctx.res.redirect('/', { flash: 'Signed in' })
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: e.message, otpId, email }
    }
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/login/otp/index.ejs -->
<% if (data.error) { %><mark><%= data.error %></mark><% } %>

<% if (!data.otpId) { %>
  <form method="post">
    <input type="hidden" name="step" value="request" />
    <input name="email" type="email" required />
    <button type="submit">Send code</button>
  </form>
<% } else { %>
  <p>Check your email for the code.</p>
  <form method="post">
    <input type="hidden" name="step" value="confirm" />
    <input type="hidden" name="otpId" value="<%= data.otpId %>" />
    <input name="code" required />
    <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
  </form>
<% } %>
```

## OAuth2

Configure the provider in the dashboard (Collections > users > Options > OAuth2). Then start the flow from a form:

```html
<form method="post" action="/auth/oauth">
  <input type="hidden" name="provider" value="google" />
  <button type="submit">Sign in with Google</button>
</form>
```

```js
// pb_pages/auth/oauth/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.requestOAuth2(ctx.req.body().provider)
  },
}
```

`requestOAuth2` stores its state in a cookie and redirects to the provider. The provider sends the user back to `/auth/oauth/confirm` (change it with `{ redirectPath }`):

```js
// pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(ctx.req.query('state'), ctx.req.query('code'))
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: e.message }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/index.ejs -->
<mark><%= data.error %></mark>
```

See the [Google OAuth2 speedrun](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2) for setting up Google.

## Anonymous sign-in

```js
// pb_pages/try/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signInAnonymously()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/dashboard')
  },
}
```

## Your own auth flow

If you authenticate a record yourself, set the session cookie with `ctx.session.signIn(record)`.

## Signing out

```js
// pb_pages/logout/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

## Security

1. Serve over HTTPS in production.
2. Turn on PocketBase's rate limiting.
3. Turn on email verification for your auth collection.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/htmx

# HTMX Integration with PocketPages

[HTMX](https://htmx.org) lets HTML elements fetch HTML from the server and swap it into the page. PocketPages renders that HTML.

## Setting up HTMX

Add HTMX to your layout:

```html
<script
  src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/htmx/2.0.11/htmx.min.js"
  integrity="sha512-YdHy6FzjD4qoyI/yWGIbsKnJHe98r96np9XeYp3ovFL+0sNP/NbDrYlSLDr5a6Ndi5sRi9GgJj+suE7yLeUMNQ=="
  crossorigin="anonymous"
  referrerpolicy="no-referrer"
></script>
```

## Route organization

HTMX requests want HTML fragments, not whole pages wrapped in your layout. Put the layout in a group, and the fragment routes outside it:

```
pb_pages/
  (site)/             # Pages with layouts
    +layout.ejs       # Main site layout
    index.ejs         # /
    products/
      index.ejs       # /products
  xapi/               # HTMX endpoints (no layouts)
    products/
      search.ejs      # /xapi/products/search
      create/
        +page.js
        index.ejs     # /xapi/products/create
```

1. `(site)` holds full pages. Its `+layout.ejs` wraps them, and the group adds nothing to the URL.
2. `xapi/` holds fragments. No layout applies to them, because there is no `+layout.ejs` at the root.

Don't name the folder `api/`: `/api/` belongs to PocketBase.

A handler can also send a fragment directly with `ctx.res.html()`, which never applies layouts.

## Sharing partials

Render the same fragment on the first page load and in HTMX responses by keeping it in a `_private/` partial:

```
pb_pages/
  _private/
    product-card.ejs    # shared partial
  (site)/
    products/
      index.ejs         # includes the partial
  xapi/
    products/
      more.ejs          # includes the same partial
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/_private/product-card.ejs -->
<div class="product-card" id="product-<%= product.id %>">
  <h3><%= product.getString('name') %></h3>
  <p><%= product.getString('description') %></p>
</div>
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/(site)/products/index.ejs -->
<% const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 20) %>
<div class="products-container">
  <% for (const product of products) { %>
    <%- include('product-card', { product }) %>
  <% } %>
</div>
<button hx-get="/xapi/products/more?page=2" hx-target=".products-container" hx-swap="beforeend">
  Load More
</button>
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/products/more.ejs -->
<%
  const page = Number(ctx.req.query('page') ?? 1)
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 20, (page - 1) * 20)
%>
<% for (const product of products) { %>
  <%- include('product-card', { product }) %>
<% } %>
```

## Search as you type

```html
<!-- pb_pages/(site)/index.ejs -->
<input
  type="search"
  name="q"
  hx-get="/xapi/products/search"
  hx-trigger="input changed delay:500ms"
  hx-target="#search-results"
  placeholder="Search products..."
/>
<div id="search-results"></div>
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/products/search.ejs -->
<%
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter(
    'products', 'name ~ {:q}', 'name', 20, 0, { q: ctx.req.query('q') ?? '' }
  )
%>
<% for (const product of products) { %>
  <%- include('product-card', { product }) %>
<% } %>
```

## Forms

```html
<!-- pb_pages/(site)/products/new.ejs -->
<form hx-post="/xapi/products/create" hx-target="#products-list" hx-swap="beforeend">
  <input type="text" name="name" placeholder="Product Name" required />
  <textarea name="description" placeholder="Description" required></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Create Product</button>
</form>
<div id="products-list"></div>
```

```js
// pb_pages/xapi/products/create/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { name, description } = ctx.req.body()
    const product = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('products'))
    product.set('name', name)
    product.set('description', description)
    ctx.app.save(product)
    return { product }
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/products/create/index.ejs -->
<%- include('product-card', { product: data.product }) %>
```

## Out-of-band updates

Update more than one element with a single response:

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/products/create/index.ejs -->
<%- include('product-card', { product: data.product }) %>
<div id="product-count" hx-swap-oob="true"><%= ctx.app.countRecords('products') %> Products</div>
```

## Polling

```html
<div hx-get="/xapi/products/latest" hx-trigger="every 30s">
  <!-- refreshed every 30 seconds -->
</div>
```

## Realtime updates

With the [`realtime` plugin](plugins/realtime.md), a page can push rendered HTML to every subscriber. A template has `include()`, so render the partial there and send it:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime'] }
```

```js
// pb_pages/xapi/chat/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post() {}, // accept POST; the page below does the work
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/chat/index.ejs -->
<% ctx.realtime.send('chat', include('chat-msg', { message: ctx.req.body().message })) %>
```

```html
<!-- pb_pages/(site)/index.ejs -->
<form hx-post="/xapi/chat" hx-swap="none" hx-on::after-request="if(event.detail.successful) this.reset()">
  <input type="text" name="message" />
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
<div id="chat"></div>
```

In the browser, subscribe to the topic with the PocketBase JS SDK and append what arrives:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/pocketbase/dist/pocketbase.umd.js"></script>
<script>
  const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin)
  pb.realtime.subscribe('chat', (html) => {
    document.getElementById('chat').insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', html)
  })
</script>
```

## Best practices

1. **Route organization**: keep fragment routes outside the layout group, in a folder like `xapi/`.
2. **Response size**: return only the HTML the swap needs.
3. **Loading states**: use `hx-indicator` to show progress.
4. **Security**: check `ctx.auth` in middleware before changing data, validate input on the server, and debounce triggers like search inputs.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/realtime

# Realtime Events

PocketBase pushes realtime messages to browsers over server-sent events. In PocketPages, page code sends, and browsers receive.

## Sending from a page

Turn on the [`realtime` plugin](plugins/realtime.md) and call `ctx.realtime.send()`:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime'] }
```

```js
// pb_pages/rooms/[id]/+api.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.realtime.send(`rooms/${ctx.params.id}/delta`, ctx.req.body())
    return ctx.res.json({ ok: true })
  },
}
```

Limit recipients with a filter:

```js
ctx.realtime.send('alerts', 'Hi', { filter: (client) => !!client.get('auth') })
```

Page code can't subscribe to realtime topics itself; it only sends.

## Receiving in the browser

Use the [PocketBase JS SDK](https://github.com/pocketbase/js-sdk#realtimeservice):

```js
const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin)

const unsubscribe = await pb.realtime.subscribe(`rooms/${ROOM_ID}/delta`, (e) => {
  console.log('Received delta:', e)
})

// Later
unsubscribe()
```

The SDK reconnects on its own and resubscribes to its topics after a reconnect.

## Hypermedia

To push HTML instead of data, see [HTMX Integration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/htmx#realtime-updates) and the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar#broadcasting).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/custom-domain-fly-cloudflare

# Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy

Custom domains on your Fly.io app with Cloudflare in front can be a little complex because you must validate the domain on Fly.io BEFORE turning on Cloudflare proxying. Follow these steps.

## 1. Create the Fly.io App

- Start by deploying your app on [Fly.io](https://fly.io/). Follow the standard process to get your app up and running.

## 2. Register Your Domain

- If you haven't already, register your domain. It's often convenient to register it through [Cloudflare](https://cloudflare.com), which will also handle your DNS and proxying needs.

## 3. Configure DNS in Cloudflare

- In Cloudflare's DNS settings, add **A** and **AAAA** records pointing to your Fly.io app's public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
- **Important:** Turn off proxying (the orange cloud icon) for these records. This ensures that the Fly.io app can be accessed directly.

## 4. Add a Certificate in Fly.io

- In your Fly.io dashboard, add an SSL certificate for your custom domain.
- Since proxying is turned off, Fly.io should be able to validate the certificate immediately. Your app should now respond on your custom domain, but it's not yet proxied through Cloudflare.

## 5. Verify Domain Ownership and Proxying

- From the Fly.io certificate area, add the **CNAME** record required for domain ownership verification.
- **Important:** Turn off proxying for the CNAME record as well. Fly.io needs to verify ownership whenever the SSL certificate is renewed, which requires direct access.
- Go back to Fly.io, check the certificate, and ensure domain ownership verification is successful.

## 6. Turn On Proxying in Cloudflare

- Once everything is verified and working, return to Cloudflare and turn on proxying (enable the orange cloud) for your A and AAAA records.
- In Cloudflare’s **SSL/TLS** settings, set the encryption mode to **Full** (not Full Strict) to ensure proper SSL handshakes between Cloudflare and Fly.io.

## 7. Test Your Setup

- Finally, browse to your new domain to confirm everything is working as expected with Cloudflare proxying enabled.

You now have a fully functioning Fly.io app served through a custom domain with Cloudflare as the proxy!


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2

# Google OAuth2 Setup Guide

This guide walks you through setting up Google OAuth2 sign-in for your PocketPages app.

## 1. Create/Select Google Cloud Project

1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com)
2. Either select an existing project or create a new one
3. If creating new, provide a project name when prompted

![Creating a new Google Cloud project](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-54-56.png)
![Naming the new project](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-56-00.png)
![Selecting the project](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-56-28.png)

## 2. Configure OAuth Credentials

1. Navigate to "Credentials" in the left sidebar
2. Click "Create Credentials" and select "OAuth client ID"

![Navigating to credentials](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-56-56.png)
![Creating OAuth credentials](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-57-07.png)

### Configure Application Type

1. Select "Web application" as the application type
2. Configure your authorized origins and redirect URIs:
   - **Authorized JavaScript origins**: Your application domain (e.g., `http://localhost:8090`)
   - **Authorized redirect URIs**: Your auth callback URL (e.g., `http://localhost:8090/auth/oauth/confirm`)

![Selecting web application](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-57-57.png)
![Configuring URIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-07-00-42.png)

### Configure Consent Screen (if needed)

If you haven't set up a consent screen before, you'll need to configure it:

1. Choose External/Internal user type
2. Fill in the required application information

![Consent screen setup](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-57-19.png)
![Consent screen details](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-57-27.png)

### Download Credentials

1. After creating the OAuth client, download the JSON credentials file
2. Store this file securely - it contains sensitive information

![Downloading credentials](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-58-27.png)
![Credentials JSON format](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-58-37.png)

## 3. Configure OAuth2 in the dashboard

OAuth2 providers belong to an auth collection, usually `users`:

1. Open your app's dashboard (`/_/`) and go to **Collections**.
2. Open the `users` collection's settings (the gear icon) and its **Options** tab.
3. Under **OAuth2**, turn it on.
4. Click **Add provider** and pick **Google**.

![OAuth2 settings for the users collection](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-00.png)
![OAuth2 providers section](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-09.png)
![Adding new provider](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-17.png)
![Selecting Google provider](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-24.png)

There's no site URL to set for this. The `auth` plugin builds the redirect URL from the address the request came in
on: the scheme and host the browser used, plus `/auth/oauth/confirm`. So the redirect URI in Google must match that
