address exactly. `http://localhost:8090` and `http://127.0.0.1:8090` are different to Google, so add each one you
use, plus your live domain (`https://example.com/auth/oauth/confirm`). Behind a proxy, the host is the one the
browser asked for, and HTTPS is detected from `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

### Provider Configuration

1. Enter your Client ID and Client Secret from the downloaded credentials
2. Configure any additional auth options as needed
3. Save your changes

![Configuring Google provider](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-32.png)
![Saving changes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-59.png)

## Customizing the Return URL

By default, the `auth` plugin uses `/auth/oauth/confirm` as the OAuth2 return path. Change it when you start the flow:

```js
ctx.session.requestOAuth2('google', { redirectPath: '/custom/oauth/callback' })
```

Remember to add the new redirect URL to your Google OAuth2 configuration too.

## Implementation Guide

### 1. Turn on the auth plugin

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth'],
}
```

### 2. Login form

```html
<form method="post" action="/auth/oauth">
  <input type="hidden" name="provider" value="google" />
  <button type="submit">Sign in with Google</button>
</form>
```

### 3. Start the flow

```js
// pb_pages/auth/oauth/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.requestOAuth2(ctx.req.body().provider)
  },
}
```

`requestOAuth2` stores its state in a cookie and redirects the user to Google's consent screen.

### 4. Callback

```js
// pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(ctx.req.query('state'), ctx.req.query('code'))
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: e.message }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/index.ejs -->
<mark><%= data.error %></mark>
```

### 5. Migration

Set up Google OAuth2 in a PocketBase migration:

```js
migrate(
  (app) => {
    const users = app.findCollectionByNameOrId('users')
    users.oauth2.enabled = true
    users.oauth2.providers = [
      {
        name: 'google',
        clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
        clientSecret: 'YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET',
      },
    ]
    app.save(users)
  },
  (app) => {
    const users = app.findCollectionByNameOrId('users')
    users.oauth2.enabled = false
    users.oauth2.providers = []
    app.save(users)
  }
)
```

### 6. Protected routes

```js
// pb_pages/account/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```

### 7. Auth state in the UI

```ejs
<% if (ctx.auth) { %>
  <div>Welcome, <%= ctx.auth.email() %></div>
  <form method="post" action="/logout"><button>Log out</button></form>
<% } else { %>
  <a href="/login">Log in</a>
<% } %>
```

### 8. Logout

```js
// pb_pages/logout/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

See [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication) and the [auth plugin](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth).

## Troubleshooting

Common issues and solutions:

- **Invalid redirect URI**: Ensure your redirect URI exactly matches what's configured in Google Cloud Console
- **Consent screen not showing**: Make sure you've properly configured the OAuth consent screen
- **Authentication failed**: Verify your client ID and secret are correctly copied to the dashboard

## Security Considerations

- Always use HTTPS in production
- Keep your client secret secure
- Regularly rotate credentials
- Review Google OAuth2 access regularly in your Google Cloud Console


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses

# Speedrun: Setting Up Email with Google Suite and AWS SES

<!-- @import "[TOC]" {cmd="toc" depthFrom=2 depthTo=6 orderedList=false} -->

<!-- code_chunk_output -->

- [Prerequisite: Make sure you can receive emails first](#prerequisite-make-sure-you-can-receive-emails-first)
- [Create an SES Identity](#create-an-ses-identity)
- [Add DNS Records](#add-dns-records)
- [Add a custom FROM domain](#add-a-custom-from-domain)
- [Add DMARC settings](#add-dmarc-settings)
- [Verifying the Setup](#verifying-the-setup)
- [Submit for Approval](#submit-for-approval)
- [Creating SMTP Credentials](#creating-smtp-credentials)
- [Configure SMTP in the dashboard](#configure-smtp-in-the-dashboard)

<!-- /code_chunk_output -->

## Prerequisite: Make sure you can receive emails first

To receive emails, you'll need an email provider. I use Google Suite, but you can choose any provider you prefer.

[Setting up a new email domain in Google Suite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail).

(Someone should write about how to do it using Proton.me)

## Create an SES Identity

Log in to your Amazon SES account and follow their getting started guide to create a FROM address and sending domain. Make sure you're in the region you prefer. This is important if you have existing domains because AWS frowns upon approving multiple sending regions.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-20-29-10.png)

Start by creating an Identity:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-20-30-52.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-20-33-41.png)

## Add DNS Records

You'll need to add DNS records provided by SES to your DNS provider. Unlike Google Suite, you'll need to enter these values manually. They do not provide integrations with any DNS providers.

![AWS SES DNS Setup](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-03-06-20-55.png)

**Note for Cloudflare users: If you’re using Cloudflare, make sure these records are not proxied.**

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-28-33.png)

## Add a custom FROM domain

Deliverability is better if you add a custom FROM domain:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-38-12.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-38-51.png)

It requires a few additional DNS entries. Note that the MX `priority` goes into a separate field, not the MX server field:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-41-08.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-42-35.png)

## Add DMARC settings

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-45-05.png)

## Verifying the Setup

After adding the DNS records, go back to AWS SES and wait for the domain to show as verified. Then, send a verification email. You should receive it if everything is set up correctly.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-32-26.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-35-46.png)

If verification takes too long, go to **Identities > DKIM**, click **Edit**, then **Save** to trigger an immediate re-verification.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-33-32.png)

## Submit for Approval

Before you can send emails to anyone, you must submit everything for approval in AWS SES. This step is crucial to avoid issues when sending emails outside your verified domain.

If you have previously had a domain approved, you may be able to skip this step. To find out, simply try sending a test message to anything with a different domain.

## Creating SMTP Credentials

Create SMTP credentials in the AWS SES console. These credentials will be used in your app's dashboard for sending emails.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-48-53.png)

## Configure SMTP in the dashboard

Once you have your SMTP credentials, head over to the dashboard (Settings → Mail).

Enter the SMTP credentials in the dashboard, and ensure the **SENDER** address is correctly set. If SES hasn't verified your email yet, you can test it by sending an email to `test@<yourdomain>`, which should go through if the domain is the same.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-53-02.png)


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail

# Setting up a new email domain in Google Suite

The process of setting up a new email domain in Google Suite involves several steps. In this guide, we will walk you through the process, from adding the domain to activating Gmail and setting up a catch-all email. By following these steps, you'll be able to configure your email domain effectively and ensure smooth communication within your organization. Let's get started!

<!-- @import "[TOC]" {cmd="toc" depthFrom=2 depthTo=6 orderedList=false} -->

<!-- code_chunk_output -->

- [Add the domain](#add-the-domain)
- [Domain Verification](#domain-verification)
- [Activating Gmail](#activating-gmail)
- [Adding a Catch-All Email](#adding-a-catch-all-email)
- [Test Your Email Setup](#test-your-email-setup)
- [Add a Sender Account to Gmail](#add-a-sender-account-to-gmail)

<!-- /code_chunk_output -->

## Add the domain

Go to the [domains admin](https://admin.google.com/ac/domains/manage) and add a new domain.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-12-14.png)

Set up an "alias domain," which involves a verification step where you need to update your DNS records. Otherwise, you may have to do the following steps manually.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-04-47.png)

## Domain Verification

If you're using Cloudflare as your DNS manager, Google will automatically recognize it and add the necessary DNS records.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-06-15.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-07-10.png)

Then, wait for domain verification to complete. It should be fast.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-07-35.png)

## Activating Gmail

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-11-38.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-12-59.png)

Once again, Cloudflare makes it easy and automatic. Otherwise, this may involve manual steps if Google is not integrated with your DNS provider.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-14-04.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-15-06.png)

## Adding a Catch-All Email

I set up a catch-all email so that any email sent to `<anything>@pocodex.dev` is routed to `ben@pocodex.dev` if the specific email address doesn’t exist. This is optional, but you might want to consider what happens to unrecognized email addresses in your setup.

[This Google help article](https://apps.google.com/supportwidget/articlehome) covers it, but here it is below too:

I like to go to [Default Routing](https://admin.google.com/ac/apps/gmail/defaultrouting) and add a rule:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-21-45.png)

Use a regex to match the entire domain like `@pocodex\.dev$`. I also like to prepend `[CATCHALL] - ` to the subject so I know that it wasn't sent to my "real" address.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-25-59.png)

Redirect the emails to your "real" email address:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-25-14.png)

Finally, make sure you only perform this on unrecognized email addresses.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-24-55.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-51-48.png)

## Test Your Email Setup

Send an email to yourself using the new domain to ensure that everything is working correctly.

You may need to wait a bit for the MX records to propagate. Just because Google says everything is verified doesn't mean the Internet at large has received the memo.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-39-27.png)

If you want to be extra sure, try sending from a completely different email provider like Proton or AOL.

Once you receive messages, you're all set!

## Add a Sender Account to Gmail

Sometimes you might want to send email FROM your domain, such as replies or customer messages. To do that, go to your user settings in Gmail and add an account:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-56-56.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-57-35.png)
